**Prompt:** Phase 2-extension (entity extension per Summary §2.10, §6.16.6, §6.28.2, C.131, C.132, C.133, C.135, C.136, C.140, C.141; Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy §12.1, §12.2, §12.3)

**Actions:**

Four new subsections added to §4.4 Seller Console Entities. These entities cover the Marketplace-Monetization non-AI layer (Promoted Listings, Featured Placements, Verification Reviews) and the Seller-Onboarding funnel ledger. All four carry required hygiene (scope isolation per §7.2, `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` where applicable, k-anonymity floors on aggregate attribution, retention-with-DSAR/residency/GDPR clauses, state-machines-as-tables, numbered testable acceptance criteria, and ≥3 failure modes each).

- `§4.4.19 PromotedListing (Org-Scoped, Seller-Purchased, Platform-Attributed)` — keyword-targeted, category-scoped paid-placement under second-price auction clearing with dual metrics (CPM + qualified-EOI); category-cap 3 enforced under SERIALIZABLE + `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; k=5 floor on impression attribution with 24-hour flush TTL; `rev_marketplace_discovery` cost center isolation (never consumes AI Wallet). Covers ten eligibility rules (plan-tier, claim-verified software, published SoftwarePage, KB health floor, ≥1 closed bid in 90d, active category, category cap, monthly allotment, top-up hard-cap, vendor opt-out clearance).
- `§4.4.20 FeaturedPlacement (Marketplace-Domain, Ops-Curated, Public)` — editorial-only at launch per §2.10 / C.131 / Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy §12.3; paid-commitment variant reserved under feature-flag `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled` (default `false`) plus `paid_featured_write` entitlement; three public surfaces (CategoryPage M9, ComparisonPage M11, HeatMapCell M13); FTC 16 CFR Part 255 `"Featured"` label with accessible tooltip; hard 1-year expiry ceiling; partial unique index prevents duplicate slot assignment; revoke cascades from vendor opt-out, verification downgrade, and upheld abuse findings.
- `§4.4.21 VerificationReviewRecord (Org-Scoped, Seller)` — Ops-review ledger for Verified/Certified tier upgrades with quarterly re-review cadence (Certified = 90-day default) and document-expiry-rereview automation; separation-of-duties rule (same reviewer cannot approve prerequisite Verified and dependent Certified without senior-reviewer override); EU-residency routing lock; 14-day appeal window (Authored Extension); 30-day post-rejection cooling-off (Authored Extension); SLA classes 5 biz-day Verified / 10 biz-day Certified with auto-rejection on breach and zero-cost resubmit credit.
- `§4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession (Org-Scoped, Seller, Funnel-Instrumented)` — per-seller-user onboarding-funnel ledger implementing the Summary §6.28.2 seven-stage flow; system-of-record for the **Seller Activation Metric** (C.135) (`activation_metric_elapsed_seconds = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM first_requirement_response_at - stage_1_arrival_at)`; target p50 < 20 min, p90 < 60 min) computed in-transaction with monotonicity trigger; Stage-3-population-latency P0 availability alert at p90 > 10,000 ms; `hero_moment_completed_at` authoritative timestamp; Three Conversion Moments (C.133) tracked at Stage 7; 7-day-no-advancement Abandonment Classifier; `reactivated` state preserves original `stage_1_arrival_at` so latency remains truthful on return.

**Conflicts resolved.**

1. **§26.6 vs §26.10 acceptance criteria scope.** §26.6 covers §26.1–§26.5 (original seller profile, verification, capability declarations). §26.10 extends — it does not replace — §26.6, covering §26.7–§26.9 only. Both sections remain authoritative for their respective scope.
2. **`page_enrichment` cost center.** §4.4.10 states `enrichment_cost_center = sourcera_owned`. §26.7.2 elaborates the cost center as `platform_marketing` (a sub-classification of `sourcera_owned` per §34.3.5). No conflict; §26.7.2 adds specificity without contradiction.
3. **Domain verification method enumeration.** §4.4.9 `claim_verified_by_method` enum and §26.7.3 both list 4 methods. §26.7.3 adds user-facing UX detail (polling intervals, TTLs) but does not introduce new method values. Consistent.

**Authored Extensions (require human sign-off).**

1. **§26.7.1 Empty-State publish gate.** Summary §6.15.4 says "Verified domain ownership gates publication" but does not specify a content-completeness gate. §26.10 AC #1 authors the requirement that at least one published Capability Declaration OR SellerSoftware must exist before publishing a SellerOrgPage. Rationale: an empty page harms SEO trust. Flagged for human sign-off.
2. **§26.7.2 Re-enrichment rate limit (7 days).** No source specifies a rate limit on re-enrichment. Authored to prevent abuse of `sourcera_owned` AI budget. The 7-day value is a judgment call.
3. **§26.7.2 Firecrawl domain crawl cap (50 pages).** No source specifies the crawl scope. Authored as a reasonable bound to prevent runaway crawl costs.
4. **§26.9.1 Schema.org validation gate blocking publish.** Summary says "Structured data for search engines" but does not specify validation gating. Authored because invalid structured data triggers Google penalties, directly undermining the SEO moat.
5. **§26.9.5 Google Search Console URL removal request on opt-out.** Authored Extension — whether Sourcera will have Search Console API access at launch is TBD. Flagged explicitly in §26.9.5.
6. **§26.9.6 30-day stale-index alert threshold.** No source specifies the monitoring cadence. 30 days is a standard SEO monitoring interval.

**Self-Challenge Log (5 findings; all resolved in-place).**

1. **Empty-state SellerOrgPage publish ambiguity.** Initial draft allowed publishing an empty page (hero section only). Challenge: empty pages with Schema.org structured data but no content harm SEO trust signals and waste crawl budget. Resolved: AC #1 gates publish on ≥1 published capability or product.
2. **Re-enrichment abuse vector.** Initial draft had no rate limit on re-enrichment. Challenge: a seller could trigger unlimited Opus-tier `page_enrichment` runs billed to `sourcera_owned`. Resolved: 7-day cooldown with Ops override.
3. **SoftwarePage publication without SellerOrgPage.** Initial draft gated SoftwarePage publication only on `claim_status`. Challenge: a published SoftwarePage for an Org with no SellerOrgPage creates an orphaned product page with no parent vendor context. Resolved: AC #12 requires a published SellerOrgPage or verified Seller Profile claim for domain verification inheritance.
4. **Comparison Page race on simultaneous opt-out + claim revocation.** Initial draft addressed opt-out and claim revocation separately. Challenge: concurrent events could briefly create an inconsistent participant count. Resolved: both events funnel through the same min-count evaluation; the archive transition is idempotent (second trigger is a no-op if already archived).
5. **Schema.org validation blocking publish in staging.** Initial draft applied validation universally. Challenge: staging environments may not have valid Schema.org dependencies (e.g., missing product data). Resolved: §26.9.1 explicitly marks validation as non-blocking in staging.

**Counterfactual Pass Log (15 failure modes across §26.7–§26.9 — verified).**

- §26.7 SellerOrgPage (5): Firecrawl target site unresponsive → graceful failure with revert to draft; AI content fails content validator → draft discarded + Ops alert; seller's robots.txt blocks crawler → no crawl + user notice; Opus API outage → 3x retry then fail; domain verification revoked post-publish → cascade to suppressed.
- §26.8 SellerSoftware/SoftwarePage (5): two Orgs claim same product → claim_disputed + Ops arbitration; seller Org loses domain ownership → Ops revocation + 30-day re-claim block; category deprecated while product references it → migration worker reassigns; KB namespace orphaned on soft-delete → KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 migration; SoftwarePage publish with claim not verified → HTTP 409 rejection.
- §26.9 SEO (5): Schema.org payload drift from stale cache → nightly reconciliation worker; suppressed page still in sitemap → next regeneration excludes within 24h; redirect chain exceeds depth 3 → enforced by §4.5.4 constraint; stale index (not re-crawled in 30d) → Ops alert; opt-out revocation recovery → organic re-indexing via sitemap lastmod update.

**Self-Challenge Log.**

- *Did the §3.10.3 clarification introduce a new implementation requirement?* No — the long-press-to-enter-selection flow is already specified in §38.7.1 (`Shift+Click` → `long_press` first row → tap last row) and §38.6.2 mobile row ("long-press → action sheet"). The clarification only names the inter-section relationship.
- *Could the §3.8.1 per-tier clamp confuse engineers building the resize handle?* Mitigated by pointing explicitly to §38.6.2 (runtime tier resolution) and §38.6.3 (per-tier persistence schema). A handle implementation reads `UserUIPreference.side_peek_width_px_per_tier_json[current_tier]` and clamps against the tier's bound from §38.6.2; both are pre-existing contracts.
- *Does `supported` correctly characterize mobile keyboard navigation when no hardware keyboard is present?* Yes — the `mobile_feature_parity_status` `supported` definition explicitly covers "Feature available with mobile-specific UX patterns. Functional capability is equivalent; the UX is different." Gesture equivalents provide navigation capability parity; virtual-keyboard chevrons provide field-to-field navigation parity. `parity` would be too strong (no literal Tab key); `simplified` would be too weak (capability is not reduced, only expressed differently).
- *Does splitting the two CI jobs create a new surface area for engineering drift?* The two jobs were already named distinctly in §38.8; the disambiguation only surfaces the existing distinction. Both jobs are expected to exist in the same CI stage (`ci_spec_gates`); implementing one without the other is itself a regression that the other catches.

- *§3.10.3 clarification regresses desktop behavior:* No — change is scoped to the mobile-placement row only.
- *§3.8.1 per-tier clamp introduces cross-tier resize confusion on viewport resize between `desktop` and `desktop_xl`:* §38.8.1 Cross-Tier Transition Contract already mandates state preservation on reflow; the Peek width persists per-tier in `UserUIPreference.side_peek_width_px_per_tier_json` so a user who resized to 720px on `desktop_xl` and then drags the browser into `desktop` simply falls back to that tier's persisted width or default — no data loss.
- *§38.8.2 `supported` label masks a real capability gap for motor-impaired users who rely on keyboards:* Mitigated by §38.7.6 AC #12, which requires non-gesture fallbacks (explicit visible buttons) for every swipe-action or long-press-action surface; by the external-Bluetooth-keyboard hotplug path in §38.7.3; and by §37 accessibility requirements for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.

#### Authored Extensions (Require Human Sign-Off)

1. **§3.7.12 External-Target Clipboard Confirmation Pattern** — entirely new subsection. Source documents (Summary, UX) are silent on this pattern. Authored at Master Spec fidelity to give the §25.7.7 mobile-leakage clause a proper home. Notable design decisions requiring sign-off: (a) session-scoped per-thread suppression rather than persisted user-preference (chosen to keep the affordance lightweight and avoid building a new preference surface); (b) heuristic-based external-target detection rather than DOM-aware target classification (chosen because the OS clipboard does not always expose the paste target — heuristic is the achievable contract); (c) Cancel-as-default-focus (chosen for safety bias).
2. **§31.6.1 Payload Body-Exclusion Gates** — entirely new subsection. The Internal Comment exclusion rule and gate name pre-existed in §25.7.10; §31.6.1 is the cross-cutting registry that gives the pattern a single home and projects two analogous gates for Selection Report draft and restricted-class KB entries. The two projected gates are flagged for Phase 11 / §10.13 / §22 to author the canonical exclusion rule and CI gate registration in their own webhook subsections.
3. **§4.3.15 `suppressed_reason` documentation extension** — the field constraint update (citing Appendix J + enumerating five values inline + notes on `visibility_tightened` and `ops_impersonation_suppressed`) is a documentation-fidelity edit, not a behavioral extension. No human sign-off required beyond authoring-convention compliance.

#### Self-Challenge Log

After authoring, re-read each edit as a hostile staff engineer:

- **§4.3.15 enum citation.** Will a junior engineer correctly populate the enum at write time? Yes — the field row now points at Appendix J as authoritative and inlines the values for quick reference. The two non-obvious values (`visibility_tightened`, `ops_impersonation_suppressed`) carry usage notes inline.
- **§3.7.12 dialog pattern.** Could QA write deterministic tests against this? Yes — five numbered Acceptance Criteria each name a Playwright test. The trigger heuristic is unambiguous (three conditions must hold; each is observable). The session-scoped suppression is bounded (per-thread, reset on tab-close).
- **§3.7.12 mobile divergence.** Is the OS-clipboard-hook-not-available degradation observable? Yes — the audit event omission is the documented signal. The release notes commitment is explicit.
- **§31.6.1 cross-cutting gates.** Is the operational invariant (transport limit independent of authorization limit) testable? Yes — both gates run on every PR, and a payload that is under 256 KB but contains firewall-sensitive body still fails the body-exclusion gate.
- **§25.7.7 reference update.** Does the new wording correctly disclaim DLP responsibility while committing to the user-awareness affordance? Yes — explicit "user-awareness affordance, not a DLP control" clause; explicit "platform does not modify or watermark copied content" clause.

#### Counterfactual Pass

Three realistic failure modes per new authored content, each addressed:

**§3.7.12 (External-Target Clipboard Confirmation):**

1. Browser does not expose a clipboard-write hook → Confirmation cannot render; audit event omitted; documented in surface release notes.
2. Heuristic registry mis-classifies a Sourcera buyer-console route as external → Conservative — dialog renders; user proceeds; per-target false-positive rate tuned monthly per §50 Ops process.
3. Selection spans firewall-protected and non-protected regions → Dialog renders if any portion is protected; full selection copied (no silent partial truncation).
4. Session-scoped suppression vs new external target within same session → Per-thread suppression is target-agnostic; reset on tab-close. Behavior is documented and bounded.

**§31.6.1 (Payload Body-Exclusion Gates):**

1. CI gate is updated but webhook handler regression silently emits body → CI gate runs against the generated payload schema, not the handler; if the handler emits an extra field, the gate detects the schema drift.
2. Subscriber assumes body is in payload (legacy integration drift) → Subscribers MUST issue authenticated §32 read; this is documented in §31.6.1 and in the per-domain webhook subsection. Backward-compatibility note: prior versions of the spec carried Internal Comment body in the payload; the body removal is recorded in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` Breaking Changes.
3. Future firewall-sensitive domain authored without an exclusion gate → §31.6.1 declares a process: any new firewall-sensitive domain MUST add a row to the §31.6.1 table; Phase 11 Appendix-sweep enforces this for the two projected gates.

**Phase 2b (§4.4 extension: Marketplace Monetization & Seller Onboarding, 2026-04-17):**

- PromotedListing → console-scoped (Seller; paid-surface authoring) with marketplace-domain rendering on Buyer-Console search/category/EOI-response surfaces → §4.4.19 → Phase 2b (Summary §6.16.6 "Enriched Discoverability," §6.27 Monetization Surface, C.131 Second-Price Auction; GTM `forced_vendor_signup` playbook C.136). Plan gating: Seller Scale + Seller Enterprise only (`promoted_listings_enabled` entitlement); rejected at `plan_tier < seller_scale` with `promoted_listing_plan_tier_below_scale` (403). ## Breaking Changes

Every change that is not backward-compatible with v6.0.0. Format: change → affected consumers → migration path → source prompt.

**Phase 4 (§4.8 Billing & AI Accounting Entities, 2026-04-15):**

- **§34 token-denominated billing model superseded by §4.8 outcome-based consumption model.** The v6.0.0 §34 surface (Free / Business $499/mo / Enterprise tiers with token-denominated budgets and `$0.01/1K token` overage) is **conceptually superseded** by §4.8 entities (AIOperation value/cost prices, AIWallet value-dollar budgets, CommittedSpendContract Enterprise commit pools). §34 is **NOT yet rewritten** in this phase to avoid out-of-sequence breakage; it remains in the spec verbatim. Phase 4 explicitly flags §34 for full rewrite in the next pricing-rewrite-track integration phase. Migration path for existing customers per Pricing Strategy §13: existing Business customers grandfather into Business Growth at the current $499 price for 12 months and re-plan at renewal. Affected consumers: every code path that reads `Organization.plan_tier` for AI-budget enforcement (§4.2.1, §5.11 Feature Access Matrix, §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions, §39 Object Size Constraints). Owner: Integration program.
- **`sourcera_owned_cost_center` enum extended from 1 value to 3 values.** The Phase 2 single-value `sourcera_owned` enum is extended to 3 values: `customer_billed`, `sourcera_owned`, `platform_marketing`. Backwards-compatible (Phase 2 callers using `sourcera_owned` continue to work). Affected consumers: Phase 2 page entities (CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport, SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, SellerSignal) that wrote the value `sourcera_owned`. No data migration required.
- **New role `billing_admin` requires §5.2 Org-Level Roles update.** §5.2 currently enumerates `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `member`, `guest`. The new `billing_admin` role authored in §4.8.3 requires §5.2 + Appendix J role enum update + role-assignment migration story. Affected consumers: §5.2, Appendix J Global Organization Roles, §5.11 Feature Access Matrix. Owner: Integration program.

**Pricing Rewrite Track (§34 End-to-End Replacement, 2026-04-15):**

- **§34 Plan-Tier Surface — full rewrite.** Every cell in v6.0.0 §34.1 (Free / Business / Enterprise three-tier, token-denominated budgets, $0.01/1K token overage, max-members caps) is replaced with the v2 outcome-based five-tier-per-console model. Affected consumers: every UI and API surface that reads plan-tier values, every entitlement check, every Stripe billing line-item, every Free-trial onboarding flow, every CSM dashboard. Migration path: existing Business customers grandfather into Business Growth at the current $499 price for 12 months and re-plan at renewal (BPS §13). Existing Free customers transition automatically to the new Free with the $5/mo wallet (drop-in compatible). Existing Enterprise customers convert to a `CommittedSpendContract` per Sales-Ops runbook; the v6.0.0 5M-token annual budget converts to a value-dollar commit at the contract anniversary. Owner: Sales-Ops + Integration program.
- **`Organization.plan_tier` single-enum field → split into `Organization.buyer_plan_tier` + `Organization.seller_plan_tier`.** v6.0.0 holds a single `plan_tier ∈ {free, business, enterprise}` per Org. Per BPS §13 / SPS §11 / MS §2, plans activate per-console; an Org may hold any combination (e.g., Buyer Growth + Seller Starter). Migration: backfill all existing Orgs to `buyer_plan_tier=<old plan_tier>`, `seller_plan_tier=seller_free` at the v7.0.0 deploy. New `Plan Tiers` enum values: `buyer_free`, `business_starter`, `business_growth`, `business_scale`, `buyer_enterprise`, `seller_free`, `seller_starter`, `seller_growth`, `seller_scale`, `seller_enterprise`. Old enum values (`free`, `business`, `enterprise`) deprecated with successor mapping per Appendix J convention. Affected consumers: §4.2.1 Organization entity, §5.11 Feature Access Matrix, §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions, §39 Object Size Constraints, every entitlement check, every Stripe subscription, every analytics dashboard. Owner: Integration program.
- **Token-denominated AI budget → value-dollar AI budget.** v6.0.0 budgeted Free at 50K tokens, Business at 500K tokens, Enterprise at 5M tokens. v7.0.0 budgets in **value-dollars** (Free $5, Starter $50, Growth $300, Scale $800, Seller Free $5, Seller Starter $30, Seller Growth $200, Seller Scale $600, Enterprise committed). Migration: token-denominated balances are not migrated; new billing periods start with value-dollar denominations at v7.0.0 deploy. Affected consumers: AIWallet UI, Wallet API, every per-capability cost reporting surface, every customer dashboard. Owner: Integration program.
- **Per-token overage pricing ($0.01/1K) → outcome-accounted per-capability rate card.** Old per-token model is replaced with `value_price = cost_base × 10` / `cost_price = cost_base × 1.05` per capability, surfaced in the Public Pricing API. Migration: existing customers with active overage spend on the old model finalize at v6.0.0 rates through the end of the current period; v7.0.0 rates apply at the next billing anniversary. Affected consumers: Wallet UI, Public Pricing API, Stripe metering integration, customer cost forecasting tools. Owner: Integration program.
- **Seat-cap plan-gate becomes informational-only.** v6.0.0 §39 enforced `max_members` per plan tier (Free 10, Business 100, Enterprise unlimited) as a hard gate. v2 explicitly rejects per-seat charging across all tiers (BPS §2.1 / SPS §2.1). The v7.0.0 surface preserves `max_members` field on BillingSeatSnapshot for legacy compatibility but treats `plan_gate_breach_flag` as informational-only — no invoicing or feature-access block on seat count. Migration: hard-gate enforcement removed at v7.0.0 deploy; no customer remediation required. Affected consumers: §5.2 RBAC, §5.11 Feature Access Matrix, member-invite flows. Owner: Integration program.
- **API plan-tier-keyed `agent_budget_exceeded` error code semantics changed.** v6.0.0 returned this on token-budget exhaustion. v7.0.0 returns `wallet_hard_capped` (HTTP 402) on customer-billed AIOperation when the wallet is hard-capped. The old `agent_budget_exceeded` code is preserved as an alias that maps to `wallet_hard_capped` for backward compatibility through v7.x but is deprecated. Affected consumers: API integrations, customer error-handling middleware. Owner: Integration program.
- **Vendor Pro Trial Seat (M17) is a net-new cross-Org billing primitive.** Buyer Scale and Buyer Enterprise plans now include monthly Pro Trial Seat allocations issuable to vendors. v6.0.0 had no equivalent; this is additive (no deprecation), but introduces the new audit-event kinds, Stripe meter events, and entitlement-matrix rows enumerated in §34.13. Affected consumers: vendor-invite flow (§14), Wallet UI, audit log, Ops Console anti-spam surface. Owner: Integration program.
- **Five-tier plan model on each console.** v6.0.0 had three tiers per console (Free / Business / Enterprise); v2 has five per console (Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise on buyer; Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise on seller). Migration: existing Business customers grandfather into Growth ($499/mo for 12 months); existing Free / Enterprise customers transition at the v7.0.0 deploy. Affected consumers: pricing page, billing pages, plan-comparison UX, Sales motion. Owner: Sales-Ops + Integration program.

- **§34.1 cell `Organizational Intelligence` plan gating (Starter: Vendor History only; Growth: Full; Enterprise: Full + Suggestions).** BPS §5–§6 silent on Org Intelligence sub-tiering. v6.0.0 §34 had similar gating; preserved with explicit sub-feature naming. Reviewer: Product owner.
- **§34.1 cell `API Keys` count caps (Free 1, Starter 5, Growth 25, Scale 50, Enterprise 100).** Preserved from v6.0.0. Reviewer: Engineering + Sales-Ops.
- **§34.1 cell `KB Document Library` (Free 50 docs, Starter 500, Growth 5,000).** Preserved from v6.0.0; distinct from KB Entries (KB Documents are larger raw files; KB Entries are normalized question/answer pairs). Reviewer: KB owner.
- **§34.1 cell `Audit Log Retention (UI)` (Free 30 days, Starter/Growth 1 year, Scale 3 years, Enterprise 7 years).** Preserved from v6.0.0; distinct from financial/billing audit retention which is always 7 years per §40.2. Reviewer: Compliance owner.
- **§34.1 cell `Custom Branding` Enterprise-only.** Preserved from v6.0.0; not in BPS. Reviewer: Product + Sales-Ops.
- **§34.1 cell `Vendor File Retention` (Free/Starter/Growth 12 months, Scale 24 months, Enterprise 36 months).** Preserved from v6.0.0; not in BPS. Reviewer: Product + Compliance.
- **§34.1 cell `Default User Role` Free is "Member (fixed)"; paid is configurable.** Preserved from v6.0.0; not in BPS. Reviewer: Product owner.
- **§34.3.3 5% drift band (operational floor below the BPS-stated 10% Finance trigger).** Authored to provide finer-grained alerting before the Finance trigger fires. Why: 10% drift in a single capability can compound into multi-capability margin pressure quickly; the 5% operational floor surfaces drift to the Cost-Base Recalc dashboard for Ops review without escalating to Finance. Reviewer: Finance.
- **§34.3.3 25% drift band (auto-publish block).** Authored to prevent catastrophic auto-publishes from cost-base swings >25%. Why: a single bad Anthropic invoice or Convex-allocation parsing bug could swing cost_base 50%+ and produce silent customer overcharges if auto-published. The 25% floor forces explicit Ops Finance approval. Reviewer: Finance.
- **§34.10.3 Free + Free pool collapse rule ($5 total, not $10).** Two-side Free Org pool is $5, not $10. Source documents (BPS §4 + SPS §4) each list $5 individually but do not address the cross-side pooling case for Free + Free. Why: $5 is the PLG hook to drive a single ceiling-hit event; doubling it would delay the upgrade moment. Reviewer: Sales-Ops + Founder.
- **§34.10.3 Free + Paid pool collapse rule (paid budget only, Free contribution dropped).** When one console is Free and the other is paid, the Free $5 is collapsed (not added). Source documents silent. Why: prevents Free side from effectively topping up the paid side; preserves the paid plan's commercial value. Reviewer: Sales-Ops + Founder.
- **§34.13.2 Ops Pricing Admin override path for Pro Trial Seat allocation.** Authored: Ops Pricing Admin may temporarily increase a buyer's Pro Trial Seat allocation for a defined window (e.g., specific evaluation cohort). Source SPS §15.5 silent on Ops overrides. Why: Sales-Ops needs an emergency lever for high-priority customer scenarios. Reviewer: Sales-Ops + Founder.
- **§34.13.5 Anti-probing rule (vendor non-redemption does NOT refund the buyer's allocation).** Source SPS §15.5 silent on refund mechanics. Why: prevents buyers from systematically issuing Pro Trial Seats to large vendor cohorts to "probe" which vendors will sign up; the no-refund rule makes issuance a real commitment. Reviewer: Sales-Ops + Anti-Spam owner.
- **§34.13.7 #3 Multiple-buyer queued-grant handling.** Authored: when a vendor receives multiple concurrent Pro Trial Seat grants from different buyers, only the first redeemed grant takes effect; subsequent grants queue with a 7-day acceptance window and refund the buyer's allocation if the queued grant expires unaccepted. Source silent. Why: the rare edge case of a vendor receiving simultaneous grants must have deterministic behavior to avoid double-attribution and audit confusion. Reviewer: Sales-Ops.
- **§34.13.5 Vendor Billing Admin grant rejection audited but no refund.** Authored: vendor-side rejection of a Pro Trial Seat grant is audited; the buyer's allocation is NOT refunded. Source silent. Why: same anti-probing rationale; rejected grants represent a real cost (buyer effort + vendor friction) and should not be free to re-issue. Reviewer: Sales-Ops.
- **§34.5.2 In-flight Pro Trial Seats continue under their original 30-day window regardless of buyer downgrade.** Source SPS §15.5 silent on what happens to issued-but-not-yet-day-31 trials when the buyer downgrades. Why: trials are a vendor-side commitment; revoking on buyer downgrade would be customer-trust violations on the vendor side. The buyer downgrade is captured in audit; the trial completes normally. Reviewer: Sales-Ops + Trust.
- **§34.5.1 No in-period budget catch-up on plan upgrade.** Authored: upgrade increases the next billing cycle's `included_budget_remaining` to the new tier; the in-flight period's budget is NOT topped up to the new tier mid-period. Source silent. Why: aligns with §4.8.3 period-based wallet model; preserves billing-cycle simplicity. Customers can fund overage if they exhaust the prior tier's budget mid-period. Reviewer: Sales-Ops.
- **§34.10.2 `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars` ceiling of $500K/mo.** Reaffirmed from Phase 4 AE; remains pending Sales/Finance review. Reviewer: Sales/Finance.
- **§34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix — `policy_parsing` and `deep_comparison` set to `soft` enforcement on Free.** BPS §4 says Free has "Policy Parsing: Budget-metered, Opus-gated" — interpretation: Free can use these via Free Allowance + wallet, but the upgrade CTA should remind them. Authored as `soft` mode (visible, with upgrade CTA on use). Reviewer: Product owner.
- **§34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix — `kb_to_capability_suggestion` minimum at Seller Starter.** BPS / SPS silent on this specific capability's plan gating. Authored at Seller Starter as the natural pairing with the KB capacity uplift. Reviewer: Product owner.
- **§34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix — `vendor_pro_trial_seat_grant` capability listed.** Source documents do not enumerate this as a billable capability per se; it is a non-AI billing primitive (subscription absorption). Authored as a `hard`-gated capability for entitlement-matrix completeness; the issuance UI is gated by the buyer plan tier (Scale/Enterprise). Reviewer: Sales-Ops.
- **§34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix — non-AI features (MFA, SSO, SCIM, IP allowlist, custom branding, API add-on) listed as capabilities.** These are non-AI features but are entitlement-gated; including them in the matrix gives a single source of truth for runtime gating. Source documents partially list these; the unified matrix is the AE. Reviewer: Engineering + Product.

**Phase 4d — Billing-Domain Webhook Catalog (2026-04-15):** (all pending reviewer sign-off)

- **§31.8 namespace decision — `billing.` prefix on all 13 events.** Integration prompt provided shorthand identifiers (`ai_operation.settled`, `wallet.cap_warning_80`, etc.) without a namespace. Authored prefix to match the existing §32.8 / §11266 pattern (`billing.wallet.overage_cap_changed`, `billing.contest.filed`). Why: the pre-existing four interim events established the namespace convention; departing from it would fragment subscriber filtering. The prompt shorthand is preserved in §31.8.1 as the human-readable alias and in the RECONCILIATION Webhook Additions table. Reviewer: Engineering + Integration program.
- **§31.8.2 envelope — 6 new fields beyond §31.2.** Added `event_class`, `delivery_attempt`, `legal_entity`, `billing_currency`, `signature_algorithm`, `webhook_secret_version`. None of these appear in §31.2; authored as the minimum information needed for accounting-system integration (legal_entity for Sourcera-side accounting partition; billing_currency for FX-rate locking; secret_version to support per-Org rotation). Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§31.8.2 webhook secret rotation — 30-day overlap window.** Source documents silent on rotation semantics. Authored 30-day overlap (previous secret valid for 30 days post-rotation) by analogy with §32 API token rotation patterns. Why: typical consumer-side migration takes 1–4 weeks; 30 days is the conservative budget. Reviewer: Engineering + Security.
- **§31.8.3 `billing.ai_operation.contested.contest_origin` — system-late-signal path made first-class.** §4.8.1 Failure Mode #2 describes the late-signal auto-contest behavior; the webhook payload field that lets subscribers triage these is an Authored Extension. Why: customer-filed contests need customer-side notification (Billing Admin sees their filing reflected); system-filed contests need Ops-side alerting (the customer is not yet aware). Without origin partition, a single contest event would conflate the two pathways. Reviewer: Ops Finance.
- **§31.8.3 `billing.ai_operation.reversed.audit_severity` — `standard` vs `elevated` partition.** §4.8.1 names "elevated audit severity" for `ops_emergency` reversals; authored as a webhook payload field so consumer-side log routing can elevate accordingly. Reviewer: Compliance + Ops.
- **§31.8.4 `billing.wallet.cap_warning_*` re-arm rule on top-up — re-firing requires a new threshold crossing.** Authored: a manual top-up that drops utilization back below 0.80 does NOT re-arm `cap_warning_80` for the current period; the next period rolls over the arming. Why: prevents notification flood from a customer who tops up partially and crosses the threshold a second time. Reviewer: Product + Sales-Ops.
- **§31.8.4 `billing.wallet.cap_warning_100.hard_cap_imminent` — derived 5%-overage-remaining threshold.** Authored as a Boolean flag; threshold of 5% of overage cap. Why: gives subscribers a deterministic upgrade-CTA trigger before the wallet rejects operations. Reviewer: Product + Sales-Ops.
- **§31.8.4 `auto_topup_failure_category` — 8-value enum.** Source documents silent on Stripe-failure taxonomy. Authored to cover the realistic Stripe decline_codes plus three Sourcera-side categories (`monthly_cap_would_be_exceeded`, `auto_topup_disabled_mid_attempt`, `payment_method_removed`). Why: subscribers building remediation flows need to route on category. Reviewer: Engineering + Sales-Ops.
- **§31.8.4 `auto_topup_failed.customer_action_required` — derived flag from `failure_category`.** Authored: `true` when the category requires customer-side action (update PM, increase cap); `false` when category is system-side (network error). Why: lets subscribers selectively surface CTAs without parsing the failure_category enum. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§31.8.4 audit elevation rule — two consecutive `auto_topup_failed` per period elevates wallet to `payment_method_at_risk`.** Authored cross-row aggregation. Why: two consecutive failures correlate strongly with imminent hard-cap; elevating the wallet's audit severity tag aids Ops triage. Reviewer: Ops Finance.
- **§31.8.5 `transaction_correlation_id` — cross-console plan-change correlation primitive.** Pricing Strategy §11 implies the dual-console upgrade pattern (Buyer Growth + Seller Starter as one transaction) but does not author a correlation primitive. Authored a UUID shared across companion `billing.plan.upgraded` events. Why: subscribers building Org-tier dashboards must group dual-console upgrades to avoid double-counting MRR impact. Reviewer: Sales-Ops + Analytics.
- **§31.8.5 `feature_access_diff` — bounded summary of capabilities unlocked/locked.** Authored to support partner-side activation messaging without requiring a separate API call to enumerate capabilities. Bounded at ~32 KB even at maximum cardinality. Reviewer: Product.
- **§31.8.5 `billing.plan.downgrade_scheduled` two-phase delivery (no separate `downgrade_canceled` event).** Authored: cancellation of a scheduled downgrade produces a `scheduled` event with no companion `downgraded` event. Subscribers infer cancellation from absence after `scheduled_effective_at + 1h`. Why: avoids polluting the event stream with negative events; matches the §34.5.2 cancel-by-timeout pattern. Future enhancement (`billing.plan.downgrade_canceled`) flagged as Pending Follow-Up. Reviewer: Product.
- **§31.8.6 `billing.committed_spend.renewal_due_60.renewal_proposal.consumption_velocity_recommended_band`.** Authored: when prior-period consumption suggests the next discount band would still be utilized, the proposal includes the next band as a Sales-Ops upsell payload. Why: enables Sales-Ops to drive expansion at renewal without a separate workflow. Reviewer: Sales-Ops.
- **§31.8.7 `billing.free_allowance.exhausted.next_invocation_will_bill_against` — 4-value enum.** Authored to give subscribers a deterministic next-state signal (wallet, commit pool, overage, hard-cap reject). Why: lets PLG-CTA dashboards prioritize the highest-conversion-pressure scenarios. Reviewer: Product + Sales-Ops.
- **Appendix C `notification_override_billing_critical` flag — DND override for 4 events.** Pricing Strategy §6 implies wallet exhaustion and payment failure must reach the customer; authored explicit override flag for `cap_warning_100`, `auto_topup_failed`, `plan.downgraded`, `committed_spend.renewal_due_60`. Customer MAY appeal to Ops to disable per-event. Why: notification fatigue is real, but wallet exhaustion that interrupts work without warning is worse. Reviewer: Product + Sales-Ops.
- **Appendix F §F.2 financial-impact retry curve — 5s / 1m / 15m / 1h.** Authored tightened curve for 3 event-types (`billing.ai_operation.reversed`, `billing.wallet.auto_topup_executed`, `billing.wallet.auto_topup_failed`). Source documents silent. Why: SOC-2 internal-control timing claims require ≤ 2-minute observation latency; standard 1-minute first retry produces 16-minute worst case. The authored curve produces 65-second worst case across attempts 1–3 (covering ~99.5% of transient failures per Phase 2 reliability data). Cited reliability-data percentage is itself an Authored Extension assumption — actual Phase 2 data was not available to this prompt; figure flagged for validation. Reviewer: Engineering + Compliance.
- **Appendix G `upgrade_completed_trigger` 4-value enum mapping to `upgrade_cta_viewed.cta_surface`.** The 4 trigger values are taken verbatim from the integration prompt; the upstream surface mapping (`evaluation_limit ← ui_capability_paywall`, `ai_budget_exhaustion ← ui_wallet_exhaustion_modal | ui_free_allowance_exhausted`, `opus_gated_capability ← ui_opus_gated_tooltip`, `vendor_limit ← ui_capability_paywall (subset)`) is an Authored Extension to support funnel correlation. Reviewer: Analytics + Product.
- **Appendix G orphan `upgrade_completed` event handling.** Authored: orphan events (no prior CTA view in 30 days) are flagged for investigation; expected to correspond to Sales-Ops manual provisioning. Reviewer: Analytics.

**Phase 22-Rewrite — §22 KB Rewrite (2026-04-15) (all pending reviewer sign-off):**

- **§22.1 Scope inventory (in-scope vs out-of-scope bullets).** v6.0.0 §22.1 stated the KB's purpose; an explicit scope inventory is authored to draw clean boundaries against §21.4 Capability Registry, §4.8 Billing entities, and §5.11/§34.1 plan gating. Why: the KB rewrite spans 4 prior subsections; the scope inventory keeps engineering from ambiguously interpreting whether plan-gate caps live in §22 or §39. Reviewer: Engineering + Product.
- **§22.2.2 Capability mapping table.** KB Spec §2.3 listed Managed Agents-suited capabilities qualitatively. The Master Spec mapping table aligns each KB-capability to its §21.4 `capability_id` for cross-link integrity. Why: §21.4 is the Capability Registry's authoritative surface; without explicit mapping, the §22 references could drift. Reviewer: Capability Registry owner.
- **§22.2.3 5%-canary rollout procedure for Anthropic beta header bumps.** KB Spec §2.4 said beta version bumps are "rolled out deliberately" without a procedure. Authored 5%-cohort, 7-day metric window, 2pp parity threshold, 30-day prior-version support. Why: a beta version bump in production without a rollback gate could break in-flight long-running sessions; the canary procedure mirrors §22.4.5 embedding-version bump discipline. Reviewer: Engineering + Ops.
- **§22.3 Ghost-Bid Importer registered as the fourth ingestion channel.** v6.0.0 §22.2 listed three channels. Per §21.4.2 `ghost_rfp_ingestion` and §4.4.14 GhostBidImport, the Ghost-Bid Importer materializes as KB ingestion at scale (Summary C.73). Why: omitting it from the §22 channel list would leave a discoverability gap for downstream readers. Reviewer: KB owner.
- **§22.3.1 KBEntry full field table.** v6.0.0 §22 implied many of these fields textually but never authored a field table. The full table is required by Authoring Convention #1. Why: engineering needs the schema to build against. Reviewer: Engineering + Data.
- **§22.3.1 `embedding_v2` parallel column field.** Required for §22.4.5 embedding-version bumps. Authored as part of the schema rather than added on bump-day. Why: schema migrations are easier when the field is reserved upfront. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§22.3.1 `recent_usage_count` rolling 30d field.** Drives §22.5.1 `usage_boost`. Authored for explicit storage rather than computed-on-read. Why: a daily-job-maintained denormalized count avoids per-retrieval scan over a high-cardinality `KBRetrievalEvent` table. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§22.3.1 `historical_dismiss_rate` (referenced by §22.5.1 `win_rate_modifier`).** Field exists implicitly via OutcomeContract (§21.4.5) signal aggregation; the explicit storage is authored to cap retrieval-time computation. Why: same as above. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§22.3.2 KBDocument `attach_ref_secret` field.** Server-side handle used to mint short-lived `attach_ref` tokens for `doc_attach`. KB Spec §3.4.4 implied tokenization but did not author the secret store. Why: rotating attach refs without rotating the underlying file requires a derivable but separate secret. Reviewer: Engineering + Security.
- **§22.3.3 KBFirecrawlSource `is_paused` Boolean.** v6.0.0 §22.5 silent on pausing without deletion. Authored to support seller-side experiment / debugging without losing config. Why: deleting and re-creating a source loses crawl history; pausing preserves it. Reviewer: Product.
- **§22.4.2 `vectorization_unrecoverable` flag-stale path after 5 failed retries.** KB Spec §5.2 named the repair worker but did not author the terminal state. Authored automatic transition to `flagged_stale` with reason `vectorization_unrecoverable`. Why: leaving the entry permanently in `embedding IS NULL` BM25-only state silently degrades retrieval quality without alerting the seller. Reviewer: KB owner.
- **§22.4.3 Re-index debounce window (5 seconds).** KB Spec §5.3 silent on rapid-edit handling. Authored debounce. Why: a seller saving 10 keystroke-edits in a row should not produce 10 re-vectorize calls (which would exhaust Voyage rate quota). Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§22.4.4 Webhook `kb.namespace.migrated` and notification `kb_namespace_migration_required_review`.** KB Spec §5.4 named the audit event but did not author webhook or notification surfaces. Authored both for downstream consumer integration and seller awareness. Why: a 0.7× rank penalty is invisible without explicit notification; sellers will have no idea why retrieval quality dropped. Reviewer: KB owner + Notification owner.
- **§22.4.5 Rollback procedure with 5-minute feature-flag gate (`embedding_path_v2`, `anthropic_beta_version_v2`).** KB Spec §5.5 named the parallel-column approach without authoring the rollback path. Why: every embedding bump must have a rollback path; 5 minutes is a reasonable detection-to-rollback latency for ops-driven incidents. Reviewer: Engineering + Ops.
- **§22.5.1 Boundary-behavior table (decay curve at `days_since_review = 0`, `cadence`, `2× cadence`, `> 2× cadence`).** v6.0.0 §22.4 had the formula but no boundary check. Authored explicit table. Why: developer who reads only the formula without inspecting the cadence transitions might miss the implicit step at `2× cadence`. Reviewer: KB owner.
- **§22.5.1 `win_rate_modifier` 5-surfacing statistical-significance guard.** v6.0.0 §22.4 had `-20%` for "low win rates" without specifying the count threshold. Authored the 5-surfacing minimum. Why: a brand-new entry with 1 surfacing and 1 dismissal would otherwise be permanently penalized by `-20%`; the guard prevents single-event judgments. Reviewer: KB owner + Analytics.
- **§22.5.3 KB Health Dashboard Contract.** v6.0.0 §22.7 mentioned the dashboard implicitly via "groups all entries by status." Authored the explicit contract (status counts, top-10 usage, top-10 dismiss, confidence histogram, decay-job staleness alert). Why: design and engineering both need the explicit contract; v6.0.0 was insufficient. Reviewer: Product + Design.
- **§22.6 Domain-ownership verification gate for Firecrawl sources.** v6.0.0 §22.5 silent on whether sellers may crawl arbitrary URLs. Authored: HTTPS only, eTLD+1 ownership verified via `SellerOrgPage` or TXT record. Why: a malicious seller could otherwise weaponize Sourcera's Firecrawl bot to scrape competitors or trigger DDoS-adjacent traffic to third parties. Reviewer: Trust & Safety + Security.
- **§22.6 `firecrawl_dedupe_action` seller-preference field (default `skip`).** v6.0.0 §22.5 listed dedupe behavior but did not give the seller a config knob. Authored. Why: some sellers (especially those whose source content updates frequently) want `replace` behavior; others want `skip` to preserve curated entries; making the choice explicit prevents surprise. Reviewer: Product.
- **§22.7 `auto_attach_policy` per-Bid-Workspace setting (`always`, `propose`, `never`; default `propose`).** v6.0.0 §22.6 mentioned auto-attach as configurable. Authored the explicit enum. Why: bid-by-bid auto-attach risk varies (some bids need exact-match doc selection); the per-workspace policy supports nuance. Reviewer: Product + Sales-Ops.
- **§22.8.3.1 MCPSessionTokenRecord — full new entity.** KB Spec §3.3 mentioned `jti` one-time-use enforcement and 1h TTL but did not author the record store. Authored complete entity with retention, residency, revocation enum, and audit fields. Why: one-time-use enforcement requires a store; the record also serves as the SOC-2 audit trail for KB MCP access; without it, incident-response (vault compromise) has no fast-revocation path. Reviewer: Engineering + Security + Compliance.
- **§22.8.3 JWT `parent_capability_id` and `parent_aioperation_id` claims.** KB Spec §3.3 listed JWT claims but did not include parent-AIOperation linkage. Authored. Why: per-tool spans must roll up to the parent AIOperation for §4.8.6 cost-base recalculation; without these claims, the rollup is impossible. Reviewer: Engineering + Finance.
- **§22.8.4 Cross-link table (MCP tool ↔ parent capability ↔ settlement signal).** KB Spec §3.4 listed tools without explicit upstream capability mapping. Authored. Why: cross-link integrity is essential for the QA test `mcp_tool_capability_link_audit` referenced in §22.9 #19. Reviewer: Capability Registry owner.
- **§22.8.4.1, §22.8.4.2 concrete request/response examples.** KB Spec §3.4 has schemas but no concrete examples. Authored end-to-end JSON examples. Why: developers integrating against the MCP server benefit from copy-paste-able examples; reduces onboarding time. Reviewer: Engineering + DX.
- **§22.8.4.7 `cite_verify` reason-code enum extension.** KB Spec §3.4.7 listed `valid: true/false, reason: "..."` without enumerating reasons. Authored the explicit set: `entry_modified_after_offset_capture | offsets_out_of_range | excerpt_does_not_match | entry_not_found | entry_archived | entry_flagged_stale`. Why: deterministic reasons enable agent-side recovery logic (re-retrieve vs report-back) without parsing free-form strings. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§22.8.5 Submission Gate (citation completeness, citation validity, firewall) at the orchestrator layer.** KB Spec §3.5 covered MCP-server permission policy. Authored a defense-in-depth orchestrator gate. Why: the agent could in principle return a draft with missing/invalid citations even with `cite_verify` available; the orchestrator gate is the last line of defense before AIOperation settlement. New error codes `agent_output_uncited_sentence`, `agent_output_invalid_citation` added to Appendix I via the audit-event-action enum. Reviewer: Engineering + Capability Registry owner.
- **§22.8.6 Failure-Modes-Addressed paragraph for vault-JWT expiry mid-session.** KB Spec §3.6 silent on JWT-rotation behavior for sessions that outlive the JWT. Authored proactive refresh 5 minutes before expiry. Why: long-running First-Pass sessions (~3 minutes per 100 reqs, but 100K-req batches exist) routinely outlive the 1h JWT; without proactive refresh, sessions die mid-batch. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§22.9 Acceptance Criteria expansion from 6 to 20.** v6.0.0 §22.7 had 6 criteria covering only the product-level surface. v7.0.0 needs criteria covering the 20+ subsections introduced. Authored 14 new criteria covering JWT validation, firewall, citation gate, lifecycle state machine, vectorization repair, namespace migration, embedding bump, residency, cross-link integrity. Why: every new feature needs testable acceptance criteria per Authoring Convention #2; absence of criteria for new sections would make QA unfeasible. Reviewer: QA Lead.
- **§22.9 #11 `kb_embedding_v_bump_canary_rollback` simulation test.** Embeddings bumps are quarterly; without a simulated rollback test, the rollback path itself is untested until a real incident. Why: chaos-engineering discipline. Reviewer: SRE.

Reviewer: Legal + Ops.

Source material is silent on appeals and cooling-off. Why: absent the appeal window, sellers would cycle rejection-resubmission indefinitely burning Ops reviewer capacity; absent cooling-off, sellers would re-request immediately after rejection bypassing the review's efficacy. Reviewer: Legal + Ops.

On SLA breach, the request is auto-rejected with `verification_review_sla_breach_auto_rejected` to signal the capacity shortage and trigger P1 Ops alert. Source material does not author SLAs. Why: unbounded review queues silently accumulate; auto-rejection forces capacity-planning conversations and prevents seller-trust erosion from indefinite pending state. Reviewer: Ops + Product.
- **§4.4.21 90-day quarterly re-review cadence.** Authored: every approved VerificationReviewRecord triggers a quarterly re-review 90 days later, gated on whether referenced KBDocument attestations remain non-expired. Source material (Summary §6.15.9) references "ongoing verification" but does not author the cadence. Why: stale verification badges erode buyer trust; quarterly cadence is a reasonable balance between Ops cost and trust-signal freshness. Reviewer: Ops + Product.

Source material (Summary §6.15.9) references "Ops review" without authoring the role structure. Why: the role split supports senior-reviewer dual sign-off on `verified_enterprise` tier elevations and separation-of-duties enforcement. Reviewer: Ops.
- **§4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession entity — full authoring.** Summary §6.28.2 authors the seven-stage onboarding narrative; C.132 authors the Seller Hero Moment; C.133 authors Three Conversion Moments; C.136 authors the Forced-Vendor-Signup Playbook. No source document authors the session entity itself as an observable, durable, query-able record. Why: without the session record, the Seller Activation Metric (p50 < 20min) cannot be derived, measured, or alerted; the PLG seller-onboarding motion is unobservable. Source material (Summary §6.28.2) references "activation metric" without authoring the formula. Why: the formula is the definition of the metric; downstream observability and SLO enforcement require a canonical derivation. Reviewer: Growth + Engineering.
- **§4.4.22 Stage-3 population latency P0 alert threshold.** Authored P0 alert at p90 > 10s on the `stage_3_population_latency_ms` field. Source material (Summary §6.28.2) names the 10-second threshold but does not author the alert severity or the p90 aggregation. Why: Stage 3 population is the moment the seller first sees Sourcera's KB retrieval and first-pass drafting value; p90 regression beyond 10s predicts onboarding abandonment and is the earliest observable symptom of PLG funnel damage. Reviewer: Growth + SRE.
- **§4.4.22 Abandonment classifier 7-day no-activity window and 8-value reason taxonomy.** Authored: a SellerOnboardingSession is classified as `abandoned` after 7 days of no-activity; the reason is attributed to one of (no_email_open | email_opened_no_signup | signup_no_stage_3 | stage_3_no_first_draft | first_draft_no_kb | kb_no_bid | bid_no_win_loss | null). Source material (C.136) authors the playbook narrative but not the attribution primitive. Why: forced-vendor-signup invites are buyer-driven mid-workspace pressure; attributing the SellerOnboardingSession back to the buyer's EOI enables buyer-side reporting ("this buyer has activated N previously-unregistered sellers") and seller-side narrative context ("you were invited by a buyer in a specific RFP"). Reviewer: Growth + Product.
- **§4.4.22 `seller_org_disambiguation_required` 409 flow.** Authored: when a SellerOnboardingSession Stage-1 identifies a domain that collides with an existing unverified or placeholder Seller Org (e.g., ghost-bid-materialized placeholder vs. legitimate new-seller signup), the session transitions to a disambiguation state with HTTP 409 and manual Ops resolution. Source material does not address multi-domain collision. Why: ghost-bid-materialized placeholder Seller Orgs are common (per §4.4.17 GhostBidImport); without explicit disambiguation, a legitimate new seller at the same domain would be silently merged into or blocked by the placeholder. Reviewer: Ops + Product.

Source material does not author degradation tracking. Why: without the field, post-hoc analysis of a cohort of slow activations cannot distinguish authentic seller-side activation slowness from Sourcera-side capacity-induced slowness; the field supports activation-metric adjustment and SLO debiting. **Phase 4e (§4.8.12–§4.8.13 Billing Entity Additions, 2026-04-17):** (all pending reviewer sign-off)

- **§4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord — full entity authoring.** Summary §2.10 / §6.16.6 / C.131 and Seller Pricing §12 author the non-AI marketplace monetization concept (promoted listings, verification-tier reserve, featured-placement reserve) at the strategic level, including the ≈ 95%+ gross-margin target and the accounting-isolation requirement. No source document authors the line-item record itself. Full entity authored with scope isolation, field table, state machine, accounting-isolation invariants, FX-locking per C.84, residency-locked invoicing per §4.8.1 mapping, append-only refund discipline via companion rows, 7-year SOC-2 retention, DSAR redaction preserving monetary fields under legal hold, dual-console firewall read gating, and 14 acceptance criteria. Why: MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord is the margin-reporting integrity defense — without the entity-level cost-center invariant, media revenue could silently mix into `rev_ai_wallet` (inflating the AI-wallet margin) or into `rev_subscription` (muddying the subscription margin). The source strategy documents name the invariant; Master Spec fidelity requires authoring the schema-and-validator surface that enforces it. Reviewer: Finance + Engineering + Sales-Ops.
- **§4.8.12 `sku_variant` SKU-level variant field.** Authored: free-form low-cardinality string captured alongside the three-value `sku` enum to support intra-SKU variants such as `promoted_listing.category_tier_a`, `promoted_listing.seasonal_q4`, etc., without requiring an enum migration per variant. Source material does not specify variant granularity. Why: downstream marketplace-ops need per-variant revenue attribution (e.g., Q4 seasonal lift within `promoted_listing`) without the release friction of an enum change; the field is constrained to 64 characters and SNAKE_CASE. Reviewer: Finance + Sales-Ops.
- **§4.8.12 `attribution_bucket_id` k-anonymity-preserving attribution handle.** Authored: 64-char opaque bucket identifier that maps to a ≥ 3-buyer cohort at the attribution-layer. Source material (C.131) names the k ≥ 3 floor for promoted-listing attribution but does not author the attribution-layer primitive. Why: without a bucket-id primitive, per-row DSAR redaction would need to correlate `buyer_org_id_hashed` across rows to ensure cohort size never drops below k, which is impractical at read-path scale. The bucket-id lets DSAR redactors drop a single bucket atomically while preserving aggregate k for the remaining cohort. Cross-ref: §4.4.18 SellerSignal `distinctiveness_score` pattern. Reviewer: Privacy + Engineering.
- **§4.8.12 `refund_parent_id` self-FK companion-row discipline.** Authored: refunds are modeled as append-only companion rows with a negative `amount_cents` and a `refund_parent_id` self-FK pointing at the original `paid` row. The original row is retained unchanged (`status` stays `paid`). Source material does not specify refund accounting mechanics. Why: mutating the original `paid` row would violate 7-year SOC-2 audit immutability; companion-row discipline preserves the audit trail while enabling correct general-ledger reversal of the original revenue. Mirror of the §4.8.1 AIOperation append-only-via-field-level-redaction pattern. Reviewer: Finance + Compliance.
- **§4.8.12 Hard-delete prohibition (`deleted_at` always NULL).** Authored: DB CHECK constraint asserts `deleted_at IS NULL` for every MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord; hard-delete attempts rejected with `marketplace_discovery_hard_delete_forbidden` (HTTP 422). Source material does not address deletion. Why: financial records require indelible retention for the 7-year SOC-2 window per §40.2; unlike behavioral data classes where soft-delete is acceptable, finance-system-of-record rows must never be removed in any form within the retention window. Reviewer: Compliance + Finance.
- **§4.8.12 Accounting-isolation QA test `finance_dashboard_cost_center_isolation`.** Authored: QA test asserts that no finance-dashboard query UNIONs across `cost_center IN ('rev_marketplace_discovery', 'rev_ai_wallet', 'rev_subscription')` and that gross-margin aggregations partition by `cost_center`. Source material (Summary §6.16.6) names the three-way margin-reporting separation (≈ 95%+ / ≈ 4.5% / ≈ 85–90%) but does not author the query-layer enforcement. Why: the invariant is worth testing explicitly because a well-meaning analyst writing an "all revenue" rollup query would otherwise silently collapse the three cost centers and inflate the AI-wallet margin by 10+ percentage points. Reviewer: Finance + QA.
- **§4.8.12 `k_anonymity_cohort_size_at_sale` snapshot field with 30-day `pending` timeout.** Authored: promoted-listing sales below the k=3 cohort floor remain in `status=pending` with `status_reason=k_anonymity_pending` until either the cohort reaches k=3 (→ `invoiced`) or 30 days elapse (→ `voided` with `void_reason=k_anonymity_timeout`). Source material (C.131) names the k=3 floor but does not author the holding-pen or timeout. Why: without the holding-pen, the first seller in a category would be retroactively billed on the day the third seller joined — poor UX and accounting-latency. Without the 30-day timeout, inventory would accumulate indefinitely in `pending`, muddying revenue-recognition for closed periods. Reviewer: Finance + Product.
- **§4.8.12 `dual_console_firewall_buyer_denied` (HTTP 403) cross-console read gating.** Authored: buyer-console users attempting to read MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows for their own dual-console Org are rejected with HTTP 403 (explicit denial rather than §7.2's typical 404 non-leak). Source material does not address the read-path. Why: the rows are seller-console-originated seller-invoiced records; buyer-side presence of the same Org in the dual-console configuration does not grant visibility into the seller-side billing ledger. The 403 (vs. 404) is the correct semantic because the resource's existence is not itself confidential to the buyer's own Org — only the row contents are — and 403 signals the permission boundary without suggesting the row does not exist. Reviewer: Engineering + Security + Compliance.
- **§4.8.13 SellerOutcomeSignalConfig — full entity authoring.** Summary §2.9 / C.130 and Seller Pricing §10 author the per-capability accepted/rejected signal semantics and the `timeout_default = rejected` invariant at the strategic level. §4.8.4 OutcomeContract is the platform-scoped base contract layer. No source document authors the seller-console-specific binding entity that attaches each of the 12 seller capabilities to its rule, window, alt-boundary event, and timeout default. Full entity authored with 12-row seed requirement, versioning state machine, partial unique index on `(capability_id) WHERE state='active'`, version-locked rule-schema semantics, `console_scope='seller'` DB CHECK, `timeout_default='rejected'` DB CHECK, late-signal grace with auto-filed ContestRecord, k-anonymity cohort-aware deferral, and 12 acceptance criteria. Why: the base OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) does not natively express (a) alt-boundary event terminations ("14d or on bid submission") or (b) cohort-aware deferral for attribution-sensitive signals like `seller_match_score_numeric`. Folding these into OutcomeContract generically would over-complicate the base layer for the 50+ buyer-side capabilities that don't need either. The seller-specific extension is the cleaner architectural split. Reviewer: Engineering + Capability Registry owner + Finance.
- **§4.8.13 `window_alt_boundary` downstream-event termination.** Authored: 5-value enum (`bid_submission`, `eoi_submission`, `kb_publication`, `response_submission`, `none`) capturing the downstream marketplace event that terminates the evaluation window before `window_seconds` elapses (whichever fires first). Source material (Seller Pricing §10) describes "14d or on bid submission" semantics narratively; the enum-and-field is Master Spec fidelity extension. On simultaneous time-and-event firings at `t = window_seconds`, tie-breaks to the event to preserve event-primary semantics. Why: without the enum, each of the 12 capabilities would have to encode its own termination logic in `rule_expression`, fragmenting the evaluator implementation. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§4.8.13 `k_anonymity_floor` per-config k-floor.** Authored: per-SellerOutcomeSignalConfig integer field allowing capabilities like `seller_match_score_numeric` to assert `k_anonymity_floor ≥ 3` per Summary C.131; sub-floor cohorts defer signal firing and then time out to `rejected`. Source material (Summary C.131) names the k=3 floor for buyer-identity protection but does not author the per-config knob. Why: some capabilities (e.g., `seller_qa_suggestion`) don't have k-anonymity requirements at all; forcing a uniform floor would either over-restrict non-sensitive capabilities or under-protect sensitive ones. The per-config knob gives Ops the lever. Reviewer: Privacy + Capability Registry owner.
- **§4.8.13 Version-locked rule-schema semantics.** Authored: each SellerOutcomeSignalConfig row is locked to a `rule_schema_version` captured at publication; the evaluator consults the locked version, not the currently active schema. Schema migrations require a new config version per capability. Source material does not address schema evolution. Why: without version locking, an in-flight AIOperation whose rule was authored against `rule_schema v1` could silently evaluate against `v2` after a schema migration, producing outcome-resolution drift that customers would perceive as a bait-and-switch. Reviewer: Engineering.
- **§4.8.13 Late-signal grace with auto-filed ContestRecord.** Authored: late `accepted` signals arriving after the window has expired and the AIOperation has settled as `rejected` (by timeout default) MUST auto-file a ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal`. Parallels §4.8.4 OutcomeContract behavior. Source material does not address the parallel for the seller-signal extension. Why: the `timeout_default=rejected` invariant deliberately biases toward cost protection, but resolver-latency bugs would produce systematic customer over-charging if late signals were silently ignored. The auto-filed ContestRecord is the counterweight that ensures customers are not silently harmed by platform-side bugs. Reviewer: Finance + Customer Trust.
- **§4.8.13 `ops_finance_admin` role reuse (§4.8 cross-cutting role; no new role).** SellerOutcomeSignalConfig management is gated to `ops_finance_admin` (authored in Phase 4 cross-cutting authored extensions) rather than a new `ops_seller_signal_admin` role. Source material does not specify role ownership. Why: the existing `ops_finance_admin` role already carries OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) management responsibility; SellerOutcomeSignalConfig is the seller-specific extension of OutcomeContract, so role inheritance is the minimum-surprise design. A separate role would fragment the outcome-resolution administration surface. Reviewer: Security + Ops.

## Self-Challenge Log

Findings from the Opus-mandatory self-challenge pass (Authoring Convention #16) and counterfactual pass (#17). Format: section → finding → resolution.

**Phase 1 (2026-04-15) — Self-Challenge Pass (9 findings; all resolved in-place before save):**

1. **§4.3.16 Buyer Referral — double-credit on duplicate referrals.** Two Orgs could refer the same email; first to activate collects credit. Original draft did not specify arbitration. **Resolved:** Added Referee Exclusivity Rule (first-to-activate wins; duplicates forfeit with `insufficient_activity` reason). Enforced at application layer (DB unique constraint would block legitimate `pending` concurrency).

2. **§4.3.17 Pro Trial Seat Grant — `buyer_billing_cycle_month` semantics.** Original "first-day-of-month (UTC)" implied calendar month. Stripe billing anniversary may not align to calendar month. **Resolved:** Field now stores billing-anniversary cycle start; constraint text corrected.

3. **§4.3.17 Pro Trial Seat Grant — buyer downgrades mid-trial.** Behavior for in-flight grants on buyer downgrade was undefined. **Resolved:** Added grandfathering rule (in-trial grants continue to day 31), auto-revocation rule for `issued` grants, and new-grant block while sub-Scale. Pool-accounting on upgrade clarified as not retroactive.

4. **§4.3.18 Usage Event — Dual-Console Firewall read rules.** Original draft allowed Org Owner to read all events across both consoles, which violates §7.2 firewall. **Resolved:** Added console-filter rule — a buyer-console session reads only `console=buyer` events; seller-console reads only `console=seller`; Ops reads across. Role gating layered on top per console.

5. **§4.3.18 Usage Event — polymorphic `workspace_id` validation.** DB FK cannot enforce polymorphic FK. **Resolved:** Added application-layer validation rule and `usage_event_console_mismatch` error code (new; HTTP 422; to be added to Appendix I in Phase 2).

6. **§4.3.18 Usage Event — PostHog outage behavior.** `posthog_delivery_status=pending` rows could accumulate indefinitely. **Resolved:** Added retry policy (exponential backoff per §31), DLQ routing after 5 failures, DLQ queue-depth alert threshold, Convex source-of-truth preservation on `failed`.

7. **§4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit — aggregation semantics on reversal.** Reversal model was ambiguous about whether aggregate queries should SUM(credit) - SUM(reversal) or use a NULL filter. **Resolved:** Specified invariant — reversal rows carry `minutes_saved=0` and exist only to set `reversed_by_credit_id` on the original row. Aggregates are single-indexed SUM WHERE `reversed_by_credit_id IS NULL`.

8. **§4.3.14 Presence Record — cross-Org guest `org_id`.** A guest from Org B in an Org A workspace had ambiguous `org_id` resolution. **Resolved:** `org_id` = auth anchor (guest's home Org); workspace_id = hosting workspace; visibility rules authored so Org A workspace owners see all Presence Records for that workspace, but Org B guests see only their own Org's teammates in that workspace.

9. **§4.3.15 Unread Marker — `has_unread_mention` derivation for Q&A threads.** Original draft blurred the semantics because Q&A mentions are not normalized. **Resolved:** Added per-`thread_type` derivation rules. Authored `qa_post_mentions` denormalized index as an authored extension (flagged in Known Gaps for future normalization of Q&A posts).

**Phase 1 — Counterfactual Pass (≥3 failure modes per entity; summary):**

**Phase 2 (2026-04-15) — Self-Challenge Pass (11 findings; all resolved in-place before save):**

1. **§4.4.7 Marketplace Category — deletion of referenced node.** Original draft permitted soft-delete without checking references. **Resolved:** Added hard precondition (zero referencing SellerSoftware rows) and migration-via-successor path; hard-delete is forbidden; deprecation is terminal.

2. **§4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record — race between page render and opt-out write.** **Resolved:** Authored 60s snapshot-staleness rule + 15-minute cache-bust SLO + `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhook fan-out.

3. **§4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record — Ops-imposed vs. seller-originated opt-out asymmetry.** Sellers could revoke Ops-imposed opt-outs. **Resolved:** `reason_code=ops_imposed` is Ops-only to create and Ops-only to revoke; seller revocation rejected.

4. **§4.4.9 SellerSoftware — capability_declaration_ids cross-Org leakage.** Array field could reference a Capability Declaration from another Org. **Resolved:** Added write-time validation `seller_software_cross_org_capability_ref` (HTTP 422); nightly reverse-reference drift check.

5. **§4.4.9 SellerSoftware — slug immutability timing.** Original draft said "slug is immutable once published"; did not specify whether slug could change after un-publishing. **Resolved:** Slug is immutable once any `published_at` has ever been stamped (not just current state). Un-publishing does not unlock slug; rename creates an alias/301.

6. **§4.4.10 SellerOrgPage — `pending_enrichment_draft_json` leak.** Draft field could be serialized into public responses by default. **Resolved:** Whitelist-only serializer; explicit QA test asserts field never appears in public or buyer-console payload.

7. **§4.4.12 CategoryPage — minor-update bypass abuse.** A seller-coordinated effort could force many minor changes to avoid editorial review. **Resolved:** Bypass is scoped to `category_faq_generation` refresh paths only (not manual edits); minor-update threshold governed via C.97; bypass usage metrics tracked so Ops can tighten if abused.

8. **§4.4.14 ComparisonPage — Schema.org leak of opted-out product.** Default Schema.org serializer would include all products in `compared_seller_software_ids`, leaking opted-out identities. **Resolved:** Schema.org builder reads `suppressed_seller_software_ids` and omits those `Product`s entirely; QA test asserts this.

9. **§4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport — cross-region signal leak at generation.** Global reports could inadvertently include EU-residency-restricted signals. **Resolved:** `residency_region_scope` enforced at generation with `market_intel_residency_violation` error; anomaly detector runs nightly against contributing signal sources.

10. **§4.4.17 GhostBidImport — first-import-free race condition.** Two imports from the same Org could both believe they were the "first free" import. **Resolved:** Atomic check at publish time; retroactive billing for loser via post-publish reconciliation worker; dispute path via §34.14 Outcome Resolver.

11. **§4.4.18 SellerSignal — delivery of a signal whose contributing cohort later shrinks below k.** A signal delivered to a seller via weekly digest or CRM Sync could not be "unsent" after DSAR shrinks the cohort. **Resolved:** DSAR recompute runs within 24 hours; delivered signals that retroactively fall below k are flagged in Seller Dashboard with a "Data revoked" note; CRM Sync pushes a correction event marking the record as retracted. Prior email digests remain immutable (accepted residual risk; flagged for §44 legal review).

**Phase 3 (2026-04-15) — Self-Challenge Pass (10 findings; all resolved in-place before save):**

1. **§4.5.4 Taxonomy Node — projection pairing drift with §4.4.7 Marketplace Category.** Without a reconciliation mechanism, the shared-registry projection and the specialized row could silently diverge on `slug`, `name`, `state`, `parent_id`, or `successor_id`. **Resolved:** Nightly `taxonomy_projection_drift` reconciliation worker + write-time `taxonomy_marketplace_category_projection_mismatch` (HTTP 409) rejection on divergent writes.

2. **§4.5.4 Taxonomy Node — merge worker crash mid-batch causing duplicate FK rewrite.** **Resolved:** Idempotent batches keyed by `(source_node_id, successor_node_id, batch_sequence)`; restarted workers resume at the next unprocessed batch; 10-minute bounded-lag SLO with `taxonomy.merge.slo_breach` alert.

3. **§4.5.5 Controlled-Vocabulary Tag — seller proposes a tag whose canonical slug matches an internal_ops_only row.** Original draft did not reject this distinctly. **Resolved:** Uniqueness is `(taxonomy_dimension, slug)` regardless of visibility; a seller proposal colliding with an internal_ops_only tag is auto-rejected with `vocab_tag_duplicate_of_existing` and the Ops reviewer is alerted that an internal tag may need to be promoted to public.

4. **§4.5.6 Vendor Opt-Out — opt-out targets a hard-purged entity.** Render contract could dereference a dead FK. **Resolved:** The opt-out entity transitions to `revoked` with reason `scope_target_purged` per §4.4.8; render contract reads of the purged target return HTTP 410 regardless of opt-out state.

5. **§4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report — coordinated false-flag campaign against a competitor.** Original draft had rate limits only per reporter. **Resolved:** Added reporter-org-level clustering detection via Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100); duplicate detection groups `(subject_kind, subject_id, reason)` tuples; Ops queue surfaces per-reporter-org velocity.

6. **§4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report — subject receives magic-link, intercepted by non-admin.** **Resolved:** Magic link requires logged-in session match to `subject_org_id` with `seller_org_admin` role; unauthenticated click routes to sign-in; magic links expire at `appeal_deadline_at`.

7. **§4.5.8 EOI Acceptance — bulk batch contains EOIs across multiple phases.** Per-record phase guard originally not specified for batches. **Resolved:** Per-record validation in the bulk handler; individual rejection with `eoi_acceptance_phase_restricted`; batch continues for non-rejected records; response surfaces per-record results.

8. **§4.7.1 Console Bridge Event — concurrent edits produce out-of-order apply.** **Resolved:** `last_write_wins` with supersede semantics; superseded events transition to `superseded` rather than applying; `idempotency_key` unique index prevents duplicate apply; `source_entity_version` preserved in ordering queries.

9. **§4.7.1 Console Bridge Event — firewall redaction validator false-negative.** A malformed payload could theoretically slip past write-time validation. **Resolved:** Defense-in-depth seller serializer applies a secondary kind-specific whitelist at read; QA test `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` asserts compliance across every event kind.

10. **§4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification — soft reversal after Scoring phase ended.** Original draft did not resolve what happens to historical scoring. **Resolved:** Known Gap flagged (reversal reinstates vendor to shortlist but not to historical Scoring — preserves Phase-12 Selection Report immutability per §12 Scoring semantics); post-Phase-12 disqualification is permitted but annotates the Selection Report rather than rewriting the report body.

11. **§4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification — global ban overlapping with open soft disqualifications.** **Resolved:** Global ban supersedes; existing soft records stay in place (audit integrity) annotated `superseded_by_global_ban=true`; surfaces reduce to Ops-only to avoid confusing the vendor or the buyer with two overlapping disqualification banners.
