### 6K. Self-Challenge Log

| # | Finding | Resolution |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SC-1 | Aggregation mid-revoke race — opt-in record could be revoked between bucket assignment and materialization. | Authored §27.9.15.1: materialization-time re-read of opt-in record; invalidate contributions on state change; Ops-only PostHog signal. |
| SC-2 | Distinctiveness temporal leakage — cohort suppression in a subsequent period reveals that a distinctive contributor dropped out. | Authored §27.9.15.2: `suppression_render_mode` enum is deliberately anonymous; `cohort_suppressed` event does NOT carry prior-period delta. |
| SC-3 | Direct Invite double-spend on retry — flaky client retry could double-consume rate limit. | Authored §27.9.15.3: `Idempotency-Key` header required on POST `/seller-signals/direct-invites`; 24h idempotency table. |
| SC-4 | Nightly reconciliation drift without recovery semantics. | Authored §27.9.15.4: `review_pending` boolean (new field); halt de-anonymization webhook fan-out until Ops clears; surface cohort as `placeholder_distinctiveness_vetoed`. |
| SC-5 | Cross-residency de-anonymization leakage on Direct Invite accept. | Authored §27.9.15.5: enforce Buyer Org's `region_inclusion_policy` at cohort composition AND at acceptance click gate. |
| SC-6 | Seller plan downgrade mid-delivery channel change. | Authored §27.9.15.6: delivery-time channel re-evaluation; no re-routing in flight; 14-day downgrade grace does NOT apply to channel eligibility. |
| SC-7 | CRM Sync activity ordering violation under retries. | Authored §31.9.17.1: per-source-entity serialization via monotonic `sequence_number`; added as authored extension to CRMSyncActivityEvent. |
| SC-8 | Plan downgrade mid-connection — what happens after 14-day grace? | Authored §31.9.17.2: transition to `paused_manual` with `pause_reason=plan_tier_insufficient`; 90-day terminal to `disconnected`. |
| SC-9 | Customer-custom field mapping deletion cascade. | Authored §31.9.17.3: explicit resolution query param; platform-defaults cannot be deleted. |
| SC-10 | Bidirectional conflict resolution latency. | Authored §31.9.17.4: 60-second `last_write_wins` window; `manual_review` → `conflict_pending` state (new authored extension). |
| SC-11 | Review Queue saturation alert storm at threshold. | Authored §31.9.17.5: hysteresis band — lift at 800 rows (not 1,000). |
| SC-12 | OAuth scope upgrade at Sourcera version upgrade — immediate pause too harsh. | Authored §31.9.17.6: 30-day grace with escalating notification cadence; daily → hourly in last 72h. |
| SC-13 | Provider 5xx outage cascade risk. | Authored §31.9.17.7: quadratic backoff cap at 60min; shared circuit-breaker at 50% provider-affected. |

## Phase 7 — §27.10 Vendor Opt-Out Global Registry (2026-04-17)

**Owner:** Opus authoring agent (this run).
**Source documents consulted:** `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` (full, with focus on §4.4.8 `VendorOptOutRecord`, §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read & Render Contract, §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall, §27.1–§27.9 structure, §31 Webhook Transport, §32 API Patterns, §34.10 AI Wallet Service, §39 Object Size Constraints, §40.2 Retention, §42.1 Data Residency, Appendix C / F / G / I / J / K); `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` §C.123 (Vendor Opt-Out Registry).
**Authoritative target:** `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` §27.10 (new; inserted between the end of §27.9.15.6 and the `---` separator preceding `# 28. The Markdown Editor`).
**Pre-edit snapshot:** `_versions/Sourcera_Master_Spec_pre-27.10-vendor-opt-out-global-registry.md` (2,312,868 bytes).
**Spec version before Phase 7:** v6.10.x (post-Phase-6 state).
**Spec version after Phase 7:** v6.11.x (pending Master Spec version header update in the final integration phase).

### 7A. Change Summary

§27.10 Vendor Opt-Out Global Registry authored end-to-end per Summary C.123. Section binds three previously-isolated facets into a single ≤60-second end-to-end SLO:

1. **Storage** (existing §4.4.8 `VendorOptOutRecord`) — the row-level suppression entity.
2. **Render** (existing §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read & Render Contract) — 60-second snapshot TTL invariant.
3. **Authority + API + Webhook + Enforcement Pipeline** (new §27.10) — the control-plane surface that validates opt-out submissions (DNS TXT challenge OR Seller Owner attestation), exposes public REST endpoints, emits `vendor.opted_out` / `vendor.opted_in` webhooks, and orchestrates the hot-registry + edge-purge + search-index sync fan-out that delivers the ≤60s P99 latency across all rendering surfaces (M2, M9, M11, M12, M13, SellerOrg/Software pages, search, sitemap, embeds, exports, OG/meta tags, RSS, AI responses, Managed Agent outputs).

§27.10 is additive. §4.4.8 and §4.5.6 are unmodified at the authoritative-source layer (one amendment is queued as a Known Gap — adding an `authority_attestation_id_ref` field to `VendorOptOutRecord`).

**Event-naming dual-family resolution:** the user-prompt-required `vendor.opted_out` / `vendor.opted_in` events (lifecycle, once-per-commit) are registered under new event class `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle`. The existing §4.4.8 `vendor_opt_out.applied` / `vendor_opt_out.revoked` events (per-page sweep) are preserved under new event class `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep`. Both families are disjoint — lifecycle subscribers receive the canonical once-per-commit signal; page-sweep subscribers retain the operational visibility into materialized backfill progress. Documented at the top of §27.10.7.

| User prompt required webhook events `vendor.opted_out` / `vendor.opted_in`. Existing §4.4.8 emits `vendor_opt_out.applied` / `vendor_opt_out.revoked`. | **Both authored as disjoint event families.** Registry-lifecycle events (`vendor.opted_out` / `vendor.opted_in`) fire once per commit under new class `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle`. Page-sweep events (`vendor_opt_out.applied` / `vendor_opt_out.revoked`) are preserved under new class `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep`. | Preserves backward compatibility with §4.4.8 subscribers while delivering the canonical once-per-commit signal integrators expect. Documented in §27.10.7 preface. |
| User prompt required ≤60-second enforcement SLO. Existing §4.4.8 AC-1 states 15-minute retroactive backfill SLO. | **Spec tightening, not conflict.** 60s applies to live-render enforcement via hot-registry + edge-purge (the primary user-visible surface). 15-min retro backfill remains for materialized row-state reconciliation (Selection Report snapshots, CSV exports, cached PDF renders, Managed Agent output transcripts). Framed as orthogonal SLO tiers: "read-path live" vs "write-path materialized". | Documented in §27.10 intro and §27.10.4. §4.4.8 AC-1 unchanged. |
| User prompt specified `POST /v1/opt-outs`. Spec §32 uses `/api/v1/` prefix convention. | **Mapped to `/api/v1/opt-outs`.** The prompt's short form is treated as API shorthand. | Documented at top of §27.10.6. |
| §4.4.8 existing storage entity vs. whether §27.10 should redefine it. | **§4.4.8 remains authoritative for storage.** §27.10 consumes §4.4.8 and adds authority model, API, webhook, and enforcement pipeline. One amendment to §4.4.8 is queued as a Known Gap (`authority_attestation_id_ref` field) — not performed in this phase to preserve §4.4.8 ownership. | See Known Gaps §7N. |
| §4.5.6 existing render contract vs. whether §27.10 should redefine render behavior. | **§4.5.6 remains authoritative for render invariants.** §27.10.3 enforcement-surface matrix references §4.5.6 snapshot-TTL invariant as a sub-requirement; does not restate it. | §27.10.1 cross-reference table cites §4.5.6 as Source-of-Truth row. |

### 7K. Authored Extensions (Require Human Sign-Off)

| # | Extension | Rationale | Sign-off Owner |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AE-1 | **Authority model** — DNS TXT challenge + Seller Owner attestation + Ops-imposed methods. | Summary C.123 requires opt-out to be Seller-Org-scoped but is silent on who is authorized to submit. Without an authority model, anyone with an `org_owner` role on a spoofed Org could suppress a legitimate Seller's presence. Authored for abuse-resistance. | Security Lead + Trust & Safety Lead. |
| AE-2 | **Fail-closed default on registry unavailability.** | Summary C.123 does not specify failure-mode policy. Authored fail-closed: if the hot-registry is unreachable, render-time invariant check blocks the surface rather than leaking. Tradeoff: transient availability regression vs. privacy-forward leakage avoidance. | Eng Lead + Privacy Lead. |
| AE-3 | **Anti-circumvention protections.** | Seller attempting to re-emerge as new `seller_software_id` under the same Org, or transferring Org ownership to dodge opt-out, are realistic failure modes. AC-22 and AC-27 author the enforcement; SellerSoftware-re-creation check is at domain level via hashing. | Trust & Safety Lead. |
| AE-4 | **5-stage enforcement latency budget decomposition (S1–S5).** | Summary C.123 states "≤60 seconds" but does not decompose. Without decomposition the SLO is not engineering-testable. Authored S1 commit ≤2s, S2 global replication ≤10s, S3 edge-purge fan-out ≤20s, S4 search-index sync ≤15s, S5 live-render slack ≤10s with Honeycomb trace span naming. | Eng Lead. |
| AE-5 | **Sweep manifest + CI allowlist-invariant test.** | Summary C.123 lists enforcement surfaces but does not mandate a mechanism for catching newly-added surfaces. Authored `/ops/surfaces/vendor-opt-out-allowlist.yaml` with CI regression guard that fails any build which introduces a new seller-identity-rendering surface not enumerated in §27.10.3. | Eng Lead + Platform Lead. |
| AE-6 | **Public Suffix List (PSL) deny-list for shared-use domains.** | A malicious actor could submit DNS TXT from a shared-use domain (e.g., `github.io/malicious-co`) and claim authority. PSL check at submit-time rejects shared-suffix domains. | Security Lead. |
| AE-7 | **Multi-resolver anti-split-horizon DNS check.** | DNS split-horizon attacks — where an attacker controls a resolver the submitter queries but not public resolvers — bypass single-resolver verification. Authored 3-resolver quorum (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9 + Seller-selected custom) with `split_horizon_inconsistency` probe result. | Security Lead. |
| AE-8 | **K-anonymity inheritance from Seller Signals pipeline.** | Webhook payloads and PostHog events include `seller_org_id` — on its own a direct identifier. Opt-out lifecycle visibility to Ops is unbounded (Ops audit requirement); external webhook subscribers (buyer-side if any) receive only k-anonymized fields. Inherited from §27.9 Seller Signals `k=5` floor. | Privacy Lead. |
| AE-9 | **Cross-residency enforcement via globally-replicated read index.** | Summary C.123 says the registry applies retroactively across all Orgs. Residency rules (§42.1) normally localize Seller Org data. Authored: write-path remains residency-local; read-path hot-registry replicates `{seller_org_id, scope_ref, state=active}` tuples globally (no PII). This is safe because the tuple is the Seller's own opt-out declaration, not Buyer PII. | Legal + Privacy Lead. |
| AE-10 | **Dual event-class webhook arrangement.** | Preserves backward compatibility with §4.4.8 subscribers while adding the canonical once-per-commit signal. New event classes `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle` and `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep` registered in Appendix J. | Platform Lead. |
| AE-11 | **`VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation` entity append-only semantics with DSAR redaction (not delete).** | GDPR right-to-erasure conflicts with audit-log immutability. Resolution: PII fields (`submitter_email`, `submitter_name`) redact to `redacted_by_dsar`; `method`, `state`, `verified_at`, `scope_ref` remain for enforcement audit. Legal framing: the opt-out record itself is the data subject's expressed wish to suppress; deleting it would effectively revoke the opt-out against the data subject's interest. | Legal + Privacy Lead. |
| AE-12 | **§4.4.8 `VendorOptOutRecord.authority_attestation_id_ref` field amendment (queued, not applied).** | §4.4.8 `VendorOptOutRecord` should link to the attestation that authorized the opt-out. Authoring the field amendment here would mutate §4.4.8 outside its authoring ownership. Queued as a Known Gap for §4 consolidation. | Eng Lead. |

### 7L. Self-Challenge Log (§27.10.11)

10 hostile-staff-engineer findings, all resolved in-place:

| # | Finding | Resolution |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SC-7.1 | Opt-out lifecycle webhook could fire before edge-purge completes → subscribers see stale cached pages moments after the webhook. | Authored §27.10.4 S3 requirement: edge-purge completion confirmation is a precondition to `vendor.opted_out` webhook emission. `enforcement_latency_budget_seconds=60` field in payload binds subscriber expectations. |
| SC-7.2 | Seller Owner attestation could be performed by an attacker who briefly compromises an Owner account, then reverts. | Authored §27.10.2.1: MFA step-up required at attestation time; `revoked_on_role_change` semantics revoke attestation automatically if the attesting user's role is removed within 24h. |
| SC-7.3 | DNS TXT probe rate-limiting could be abused to deny a legitimate Seller's attestation. | Authored per-attestation rate limit (5 verify attempts/hour) rather than per-domain; legitimate Seller retries within an attestation are bounded but multiple attestations are not blocked. |
| SC-7.4 | Ops-imposed opt-out without audit trail creates legal exposure. | Authored `method=ops_imposed` requires DPO-reason annotation (`ops_imposed_dpo_reason` field, enum + free-text, retained 7 years); `seller_cannot_revoke` semantics preserve the Ops-imposed state against Seller DELETE. |
| SC-7.5 | ≤60s SLO could be violated silently if observability is not end-to-end. | Authored `vendor_opt_out_enforcement_latency_measured` event with per-stage S1–S5 breakdown; PagerDuty P1 escalation at P99 > 60s over 15-min window; Honeycomb dashboard with 5-stage waterfall. |
| SC-7.6 | Hot-registry cache could drift from canonical row-state under partial replication failure. | Authored fail-closed default (§27.10.4) + `vendor_opt_out_registry_unavailable_fail_closed` event; every render read does canonical-row check at the replica lag threshold >15s. |
| SC-7.7 | Newly-launched surface (future feature) would silently leak until someone remembers to add enforcement. | Authored allowlist-invariant CI test (§27.10.3 AE-5) — build fails if a new seller-identity-render code path is introduced without §27.10.3 enumeration. |
| SC-7.8 | Opt-in re-surface after opt-out could expose prior Buyer-saved Selection Reports that cached the Seller's content pre-opt-out. | Authored §27.10.5: on opt-in re-surface, no automatic re-hydration of prior buyer-saved snapshots — Buyer must re-trigger fetch. Prevents ghost data from opt-out window. |
| SC-7.9 | Attestation could be issued for a `seller_software_id` that is later deleted → orphaned attestation. | Authored cascade: `SellerSoftware` soft-delete → attestations referencing it transition to `expired` with `failure_reason=scope_ref_deleted`. |
| SC-7.10 | Seller Org ownership transfer could bypass opt-out via new Owner revoking attestation. | Authored §27.10.9 AC-22: Org ownership transfer does NOT automatically revoke prior attestations; new Owner must explicitly revoke with 48h cool-down + Ops notification. |

### 7M. Counterfactual Pass (15 Failure Modes — §27.10.10)

| # | Failure Mode | Handling |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FM-7.1 | Registry unreachable at render-time | Fail-closed; surface blocks with HTTP 503 or content placeholder. §27.10.4. |
| FM-7.2 | Hot-registry replication lag exceeds 15s | Render does canonical-row check; fail-closed if confirm fails. §27.10.4. |
| FM-7.3 | Edge POP purge straggler | `vendor_opt_out_edge_purge_slow_pop` event; Ops PagerDuty at P99 >20s. §27.10.4 S3. |
| FM-7.4 | DNS split-horizon attack | 3-resolver quorum; `split_horizon_inconsistency` probe result rejects verification. §27.10.2 AE-7. |
| FM-7.5 | Attestation submitted from compromised Owner account | MFA step-up at attestation time; `revoked_on_role_change` within 24h. §27.10.2.1 SC-7.2. |
| FM-7.6 | Seller re-creates SellerSoftware with same domain to dodge opt-out | Domain-hash check on SellerSoftware create; active opt-out for domain blocks re-creation. §27.10.9 AC-27. |
| FM-7.7 | Seller Org ownership transfer to dodge opt-out | Prior attestations survive; new Owner revocation has 48h cool-down + Ops notification. §27.10.9 AC-22 + SC-7.10. |
| FM-7.8 | Shared-use domain (github.io) submitted for DNS TXT | PSL deny-list rejects at submit-time. §27.10.2 AE-6. |
| FM-7.9 | Ops-imposed opt-out without audit trail | `ops_imposed_dpo_reason` required; `seller_cannot_revoke` preserved. §27.10.2.1 SC-7.4. |
| FM-7.10 | Webhook subscriber fails idempotency under retry storm | `event_id` idempotency + HMAC-SHA256; DLQ at 5. §27.10.7. |
| FM-7.11 | Selection Report PDF cached pre-opt-out leaks Seller identity | §27.10.5: in-flight Managed Agent outputs and AI-response caches invalidated on opt-out commit; buyer-saved snapshots re-render on next read. |
| SC-equivalent FM-7.12 | Newly-added enforcement surface not in §27.10.3 | Allowlist-invariant CI test (AE-5); build fails. §27.10.3. |
| FM-7.13 | Cross-residency leakage | Write-path remains residency-local; read-path hot-registry replicates suppression tuples globally (no PII). §27.10.8 AE-9. |
| FM-7.14 | DSAR right-to-erasure on submitter vs. opt-out enforcement record | Append-only redaction: PII redacts to `redacted_by_dsar`; enforcement record preserved. §27.10.8 + AE-11. |
| FM-7.15 | Opt-in re-surface exposes pre-opt-out Buyer-saved snapshots | No auto re-hydration on opt-in; Buyer must re-fetch. §27.10.5 SC-7.8. |

### Authored Extensions (flagged; requires human sign-off)

1. **Loops.so dispatch fallback terminal state (L.3 row 2 and AE Error `trial_seat_loops_dispatch_unrecoverable`).** Collapses a 5-retry exponential backoff exhaustion into `fraud_blocked` with `anti_spam_hold_reason = loops_dispatch_unrecoverable`. The rationale: an invite never delivered is functionally equivalent to an SIM-blocked grant from the buyer's perspective (pool refunds either way), and using `fraud_blocked` as a catch-all terminal avoids adding a new enum value (`loops_dispatch_failed`) that would not be distinguishable to Ops without the reason field. If human reviewers prefer a dedicated status value, Appendix J `trial_seat_status` would need to be extended and L.3 updated accordingly.

2. **Invite-not-accepted pool refund (L.3 `expired_unaccepted` transition).** Refunds the pool counter when a grant times out unconsumed. Rationale: buyer issued the grant in good faith; vendor never engaged; the buyer should not bear the pool cost. Requires human sign-off because the prompt/M17 source is silent on whether `expired_unaccepted` should refund. Current implementation: refund atomically on state transition.

3. **Supersede-chain traversal limit (L.5 acceptance criterion 4).** `supersede_chain_too_long` at 50 hops. The Master Spec and KB Engineering Spec do not set this limit; 50 is chosen as a practical ceiling for version chains (e.g., SOC 2 annually for 50 years is absurd). Requires human sign-off; Ops may prefer a lower or higher limit depending on enterprise-customer reality.

4. **Retroactive-safety invariant error code (`referral_activity_threshold_policy_drift_rejected`).** Covers the case where the `activity_threshold_policy_version` stamped at referral create has been hard-deleted from the Ops policy registry. Rationale: rather than silently applying the current live policy (which could retroactively disqualify a referral that would have qualified under the stamped policy), hold the credit issuance for Ops review. Requires human sign-off on the hold-and-review path.

5. **Dual-projection read rule (L.3 acceptance criterion 6).** Buyer and seller consoles see different projections of the same ProTrialSeatGrant row. Requires human sign-off on the exact field-level split (buyer-facing vs. vendor-facing). Authored at the principle level in L.3; the precise field partition belongs in a §5.11 Feature Access Matrix addendum that this closeout did NOT author.

6. **`trial_seat_buyer_revoke_post_provisioning_forbidden` (HTTP 403).** Forces Ops-mediated post-provisioning revocation. Requires human sign-off on whether to widen to allow buyer-self-serve post-provisioning revocation with a compensating vendor-protection mechanism (e.g., mandatory 7-day notice).

### Counterfactual Pass

Three or more failure modes considered per new state machine:

**L.1 Internal Comment Thread:**

1. Attacker in a seller-console session attempts thread read → rejected with `internal_comment_cross_console_access` 404 (non-leak). ✓
2. Workspace archived mid-thread-authoring → cascading archive forces thread to `archived` atomically (acceptance criterion 4). ✓
3. Thread `archived → open` requested by Ops for DSAR recovery → rejected; Ops must use backup-restore per §40.2, not a direct transition. ✓

**L.2 Buyer Referral:**

1. Two referrals claim the same referee Org concurrently → second one rejected with `referral_referee_already_bound` 409. ✓
2. Nightly credit-issuance job runs twice on the same day → idempotency key `(referral_id, credit_issued_at::date)` deduplicates. ✓
3. Ops overrides SIM flag, then SIM re-flags later → Appendix C emits `referral_ops_overridden` audit; second SIM flag re-enters `flagged_fraud`. ✓

**L.3 Pro Trial Seat Grant:**

1. Two buyer admins issue grants simultaneously with pool at 1 remaining → Convex transaction serializes; one commits, the other returns `trial_seat_pool_exhausted`. ✓
2. Vendor signs up on grant after converting to paid plan concurrently → `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid` raised at `provisioned` transition, not at `issued`. ✓
3. Buyer revokes grant after vendor has already provisioned → `trial_seat_buyer_revoke_post_provisioning_forbidden` 403; escalation to Ops. ✓

**L.4 KB Entry:**

1. Source document body changes between vectorization and BM25 index → §22.4.2 per-transaction rollback; entry never half-indexed. ✓
2. Daily Convex job misses run for 48h → backfill catches `review_due` and `review_overdue` transitions on next run; on-call paged at 2h missed. ✓
3. Seller un-archives an entry whose embedding model was deprecated → §22.4.3 triggers re-vectorize with the current active model; old embedding coexists until the new is written. ✓

**L.5 KB Document:**

1. Seller uploads renewal but forgets to set `prior_version_doc_id` → both documents are `active` concurrently; no automatic supersede chain. Acceptance criterion 2 enforces this: `superseded` requires `prior_version_doc_id` establishment. ✓

3. Hard-delete cascades on an archived document referenced by `evidence_doc_refs` → `evidence_doc_refs` array on the referring KBEntry rows is nulled in the same Convex transaction. ✓

## Phase 4e — §4.8 Billing-Entity Additions (MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord, SellerOutcomeSignalConfig) (2026-04-17)

**Date:** 2026-04-17
**Prompt:** Phase 4e — add two new §4.8 billing-accounting entities at Master Spec fidelity to surface the third (non-AI) revenue class per Summary §2.10 / §6.16.6 / C.131 and to bind the 12 seller capabilities to their Summary §2.9 / Seller Pricing §10 accepted-signal contracts with `timeout_default = rejected`. Strictly additive to §4.8; defers §34 rewrite work to Phase 2.
**Status:** Complete (authored; self-challenge findings resolved in-place; awaiting human review for flagged Authored Extensions).
**Operator:** Claude Opus 4.7 (working as Sourcera staff-engineering agent).

### Scope and Motivation

Summary §2.10 / §6.16.6 declares that Sourcera operates a third revenue class — non-AI marketplace-discovery SKUs (promoted listings; verification-tier reserve; featured-placement reserve) — that MUST be accounted for independently of both AI Wallet cost-of-goods (`rev_ai_wallet`, ≈ 4.5% gross margin) and subscription revenue (`rev_subscription`, ≈ 85–90% gross margin). The third class is targeted at ≈ 95%+ gross margin and MUST surface separately in every finance dashboard so that margin-reporting does not silently inflate the AI-wallet margin by comingling media revenue. Prior to this phase, no §4.8 entity carried that accounting isolation.

Parallel to this, Summary §2.9 / C.130 / Seller Pricing §10 describe 12 seller-side capabilities that each resolve under an accepted-signal rule with `timeout_default = rejected` (the cost-protection stance: silence = refund to the seller). The base OutcomeContract entity (§4.8.4) handles the platform-scoped contract layer but does not natively express (a) alt-boundary event semantics ("14d or on bid submission") or (b) k-anonymity deferral for attribution-sensitive signals like `seller_match_score_numeric`. Phase 4e authors the seller-specific extension entity, `SellerOutcomeSignalConfig`, that binds each of the 12 capabilities to its window, alt-boundary, rejection semantics, rule-schema version lock, and `timeout_default='rejected'` (DB-CHECK-enforced).

### Actions

1. **§4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord authored (Sourcera_Master_Spec.md line 5514).** Seller-org-scoped; accounting-isolated line-item record for non-AI monetization. 27 fields; DB-CHECK-enforced `cost_center='rev_marketplace_discovery'`; integer-cents monetary discipline; FX-locked-at-purchase per C.84; `legal_entity` residency-locked invoicing (four-entity ceiling: `sourcera_us_llc`/`sourcera_eu_gmbh`/`sourcera_uk_ltd`/`sourcera_apac_pte`); append-only refund via companion rows with `refund_parent_id` self-reference; hard-delete forbidden (`deleted_at` ALWAYS NULL); 7-year SOC-2 retention; k-anonymity cohort-size-at-sale capture (k≥3 floor with 30-day pending window before void); explicit no-AIWallet-linkage invariant; explicit no-AIOperation-write invariant; Dual-Console Firewall blocks buyer-console reads on shared Orgs; 5-state machine (`pending`/`invoiced`/`paid`/`voided`/`refunded`); 15 Failure Modes Addressed (12 original + 3 added during Self-Challenge Pass); 18 Acceptance Criteria.

2. **§4.8.13 SellerOutcomeSignalConfig authored (Sourcera_Master_Spec.md line ~5616).** Platform-scoped (Ops-managed); seller-console-only (DB-CHECK-enforced `console_scope='seller'`); versioned per `capability_id`; exactly-one-active enforced via partial unique index on `(capability_id, state) WHERE state='active'`; `timeout_default='rejected'` DB-CHECK-enforced; `window_seconds` bounded [3600, 7776000] (1 hour to 90 days); alt-boundary event enum (`none`/`bid_submission`/`eoi_submission`/`kb_publication`/`response_submission`) supports "14d or on bid submission" semantics from Seller Pricing §10; per-row `k_anonymity_floor` for attribution-sensitive signals (≥3 mandated for `seller_match_score_numeric` per Summary C.131); rule-schema-version-locked at publication; late-signal grace mirrors §4.8.4 OutcomeContract with `auto_filed_late_signal` ContestRecord materialization; 4-state lifecycle (`draft`/`active`/`superseded`/`retired`); 12 Failure Modes Addressed; 15 Acceptance Criteria (acceptance criterion #1 revised during Self-Challenge Pass to enum-cardinality-driven parity rather than hardcoded 12).

### Phase 4e (2026-04-17) — Self-Challenge Pass (5 findings; all resolved in-place before save)

1. **§4.8.12 state machine was silent on the refund companion row's own state-machine identity.** Acceptance criterion 11 declared records append-only post-`invoiced` and the state machine row for `paid → refunded` described "companion negative row created with `refund_parent_id` set," but did not specify the companion row's `status` value, field-inheritance rule, or immutability posture. A downstream reader could reasonably assume the companion row is `status='paid'` with a negative amount (invalid — it would claim payment of a negative), or `status='pending'` (invalid — no invoice), or inherit `void_reason` from the parent (undefined). **Resolved in place:** the state-machine row for `paid → refunded` now specifies companion row `status='refunded'`, `amount_cents` = negative of parent, full field-inheritance of `cost_center`/`legal_entity`/`billing_currency`/`fx_rate_locked_to_usd`, `void_reason` populated when the origin is legal hold, and explicit companion-row immutability (refund-of-refund forbidden). A new Failure Mode #15 (`marketplace_discovery_refund_chain_forbidden`, HTTP 409) backs this at the write layer.

2. **§4.8.12 state machine had an ambiguous `(any) → voided` row for legal hold that conflicted with the `paid → refunded` row.** A legal hold arriving post-payment could either take the `paid → voided` path (no Stripe interaction, per the `(any)` row's "Does not require Stripe interaction" wording) or the `paid → refunded` path. These two paths produce materially different Stripe ledger positions and SOC-2 settlement traces. **Resolved in place:** the state machine row is split. Pre-payment legal holds take `pending/invoiced → voided` with `void_reason=legal_hold_void`. Post-payment legal holds MUST take `paid → refunded` with the companion row carrying `void_reason=legal_hold_void`. The `voided` terminal is now explicitly reserved for pre-payment voids to preserve SOC-2 settlement integrity.

3. **§4.8.12 `pending → voided` for k-anonymity timeout named no trigger.** Acceptance criterion 10 declared the 30-day pending window for k-anonymity cohort threshold but the state machine did not name the actor or schedule. A production engineer reading only the state machine would have to infer that a sweep job exists. **Resolved in place:** the state-machine row names the trigger as `marketplace_discovery_k_anon_sweep`, a nightly job running at 02:00 UTC (consistent with the §4.8.6 billing cron footprint) evaluating `billing_period_start + 30d` as the horizon. Ops can page on missed sweep per the §4.8.6 alerting pattern.

4. **§4.8.12 had no failure mode for seller `data_residency` outside the four-entity ceiling.** The `legal_entity` enum holds four values. A seller whose `data_residency` has no matching entity would silently fail at invoice-finalization time with the `marketplace_discovery_legal_entity_mismatch` 422, after having already completed the purchase UX flow. **Resolved in place:** Failure Mode #13 added. Purchase attempt from an unsupported residency rejects at row-create time with HTTP 403 `marketplace_discovery_unsupported_residency`; the customer is directed to Sales-Ops; expansion requires a coordinated Appendix J enum addition and a Stripe-invoicing-entity provisioning runbook. This makes the geographic operating scope explicit rather than silently implicit.

5. **§4.8.13 acceptance criterion #1 hardcoded "exactly 12" rows.** When a future release extends `seller_outcome_signal_capability` to, say, 13 or 14 values, the seed-count assertion would fail and block deploy — but the intent of the assertion is parity between the enum cardinality and the count of active configs, not a fixed 12. **Resolved in place:** acceptance criterion #1 rewritten to `|seller_outcome_signal_capability|` parity. QA test renamed from `seller_outcome_signal_seed_count_12` to `seller_outcome_signal_seed_count_matches_enum_cardinality`. Forward-compatibility with future enum extensions is now an invariant, with the requirement that any enum extension ships a same-release migration that seeds the new active row.

### Phase 4e — Counterfactual Pass (≥3 realistic failure modes per new entity; summary)

Per authoring convention #17 and the Opus-mandatory Counterfactual Pass, each new entity enumerates realistic failure modes with resolution. Floor of 3 per entity exceeded 5× for MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord and 4× for SellerOutcomeSignalConfig.

**§4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord — 15 failure modes addressed (12 original + 3 added during Self-Challenge Pass):**

Cost-center drift into AI Wallet ledger (DB CHECK + write validator + finance-dashboard partition alert); plan downgrade mid-period from Scale to Pro (purchase-time plan gate with `marketplace_discovery_sku_unavailable_on_plan` 403 and Ops-mediated void path via `plan_downgrade_void` reason); per-seller monthly cap breach at 5th promoted listing (atomic counter with `marketplace_discovery_monthly_cap_exceeded` 409); per-category concurrent-slot cap breach at 4th slot (atomic counter with `marketplace_discovery_category_cap_exceeded` 409); k-anonymity cohort below floor of 3 at sale time (deferred placement + 30-day pending window + `marketplace_discovery_k_anon_sweep` void); multi-currency invoice from EU seller buying in USD (FX-rate-locked-at-purchase per C.84 with no re-opening at invoice time); refund issued after SOC-2 7-year retention (hard-delete forbidden + companion-row discipline with retention clock on newer row); DSAR right-to-erasure from seller contact (PII fields redacted, monetary fields preserved under SOC-2 legal hold); accidental AIWallet linkage (schema forbids `ai_wallet_id` FK + QA test `marketplace_discovery_no_ai_wallet_linkage`); buyer-console read on dual-console Org (Dual-Console Firewall rejects with HTTP 403 `dual_console_firewall_buyer_denied`); finance-dashboard cross-cost-center UNION attempt (QA test `finance_dashboard_cost_center_isolation` + template-engine config-load rejection); Stripe invoice legal-entity mismatch (derived from residency with `marketplace_discovery_legal_entity_mismatch` 422 and §6.8 / C.84 correction protocol); unsupported seller residency (rejected at row-create with `marketplace_discovery_unsupported_residency` 403 and Sales-Ops escalation path — added during Self-Challenge Pass); DSAR during pending state (PII redacted, monetary preserved, transitions remain permitted under tombstoned contact — added during Self-Challenge Pass); refund-of-refund attempt via chained companion rows (rejected with `marketplace_discovery_refund_chain_forbidden` 409 — added during Self-Challenge Pass).

**§4.8.13 SellerOutcomeSignalConfig — 12 failure modes addressed:**

Operator attempts `timeout_default='accepted'` to game resolution stats (DB CHECK + QA test `seller_outcome_signal_default_rejected_12`); rule authored for non-seller capability (DB CHECK `console_scope='seller'` + capability-id validation); config publishes referencing a retired OutcomeContract (state gate rejects with `seller_outcome_signal_contract_retired` 409); `window_seconds` out of bounds (range constraint + `seller_outcome_signal_window_out_of_range` 422); concurrent publication of two draft versions for same capability (partial unique index + `seller_outcome_signal_version_conflict` 409); k-anonymity leak via `seller_match_score_numeric` when cohort = 1 (`k_anonymity_floor=3` + evaluator deferral to timeout-default-rejected); alt-boundary event fires before `window_seconds` elapses (whichever-first resolution with tie-break to alt boundary); late signal arrives after `window_seconds` has elapsed and `rejected` recorded on AIOperation (no-op for resolution, but auto-filed ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` if late signal is `accepted` — mirrors §4.8.4 grace window); seller attempts to read platform-scoped rule JSON via API (RBAC + sanitized projection for seller-console endpoint); version drift — AIOperation resolves under wrong config version (resolution uses config version active at AIOperation `created_at`, not current active); seed migration missed a capability (QA test `seller_outcome_signal_seed_count_matches_enum_cardinality` blocks deploy); rule-schema version drift (each row locked to rule-schema version at publication; evaluator consults locked version; schema migrations require a new config version per capability).

### Verification

- **Master Spec heading syntax preserved.** `### 4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord (Seller-Org-Scoped, Accounting-Isolated, Non-AI Revenue Line) {#4.8.12-marketplacediscoveryrevenuerecord}` and `### 4.8.13 SellerOutcomeSignalConfig (Platform-Scoped, Seller-Console-Only, Versioned) {#4.8.13-selleroutcomesignalconfig}` follow the Master Spec anchor-slug convention (verified against §4.8.1–§4.8.11).
- **Field table schema-completeness.** Both entity field tables include `id` (UUID), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` per Authoring Convention #1; scope-isolation block, indexes, retention, state machine, failure modes, and acceptance criteria blocks present per the §4.8.1 authoring pattern.
- **No enum drift.** Appendix J enum blocks registered in Phase 4e (`marketplace_discovery_sku`, `marketplace_discovery_revenue_status`, `marketplace_discovery_void_reason`, `legal_entity`, `seller_outcome_signal_capability`, `seller_outcome_signal_rule_type`, `seller_outcome_signal_alt_boundary`, `seller_outcome_signal_timeout_default`) cover every enum value referenced in the §4.8.12 / §4.8.13 bodies. `marketplace_discovery_cost_center` is a single-value enum used solely as a DB CHECK anchor.
- **Error-code coverage.** Every error code referenced in §4.8.12 / §4.8.13 bodies is registered in Appendix I. The two codes added during the Self-Challenge Pass (`marketplace_discovery_unsupported_residency`, `marketplace_discovery_refund_chain_forbidden`) are registered in the Phase 4e Appendix I subsection.
- **No cross-console firewall regression.** `§4.8.12` acceptance criterion 17 asserts buyer-console reads on a dual-console Org are blocked; `§4.8.13` scope-isolation block locks `console_scope='seller'` at the DB layer and restricts writes to Ops `ops_finance_admin`.
- **No AIWallet coupling.** `§4.8.12` schema forbids an `ai_wallet_id` FK; QA test `marketplace_discovery_no_ai_wallet_linkage` asserts. No row creation in MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord touches AIWallet balance; no `rev_marketplace_discovery` value appears on any AIOperation or AIWallet ledger row.
- **Integer-cents monetary discipline preserved.** `amount_cents` is a non-negative integer; fractional values rejected with 422; companion-row negative amounts are in the same cents unit; FX-rate-locked-at-purchase per C.84; all USD conversion uses the locked rate.
- **Seed-count invariant enum-driven.** `§4.8.13` acceptance criterion #1 now ties active-config count to `seller_outcome_signal_capability` cardinality, not to a fixed 12. The v1 seed is 12 rows but future enum extensions ship a same-release migration per the invariant.
- **Line-number integrity.** §4.8.12 and §4.8.13 inserted after §4.8.11 and before §5; §5.2 / §5.2.1 (Billing Admin) unaffected; §4.8.1 AIOperation state machine unaffected; §4.8.4 OutcomeContract unaffected. Master Spec insertion additive; no content deleted.
- **§34 rewrite scope.** Explicitly deferred to Phase 2 per Phase 4e Known Gaps. No inline §34 numerical values duplicated; §4.8.12 / §4.8.13 acceptance criteria cite Summary C.131 / Seller Pricing §10 / §12 rather than restating.

Completed. Key observations addressed in-place prior to delivery:

1. **Target Account stub vs Phase 5 full spec — fields can only expand, not contract.** The §4.3.20 stub explicitly states "fields listed here constitute the minimum locked schema" so Phase 5 cannot remove fields. Additions are permitted.

4. **`contest.abandoned` webhook back-fill flood on v7.0.0 deploy.** Mitigated by Phase 4 Stripe retry-curve class `pricing_api_publish` back-fill chunking (500/batch, 10-minute interval). Will be re-audited at Phase 4 integration per KG-P1-V14.

## Pricing Rewrite Track — §34 End-to-End Outcome-Based Rewrite (2026-04-18)

**Date:** 2026-04-18
**Prompt:** Pricing Rewrite Track — §34 Rewrite. REPLACE §34 end-to-end with the outcome-based consumption model per BPS v2 (2026-04-13), SPS v2 (2026-04-14), and MS §2.7–§2.12. Preserve §34.X anchor conventions; expand to 20 subsections.
**Status:** Complete (authored; awaiting Ops Finance + Sales Ops + VP Finance + VP Marketing + VP Legal sign-offs on flagged Authored Extensions).

### Scope of Rewrite

The pre-rewrite §34 had 14 subsections (§34.1 Plan Tier Definitions through §34.14 Acceptance Criteria). The rewrite:

- Preserved §34.1 through §34.13 content semantics (Plan Tiers, Pricing, Outcome-Based AI Operation Pricing, No Per-Unit Metering, Plan Upgrade/Downgrade, Downgrade Excess Data Handling, Billing Seat Count, Entitlement Enforcement, Onboarding and Trial Carry-Over, AI Wallet Service, Outcome Resolver, Cross-Side Billing Rules, Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat).
- Renumbered the old §34.14 Acceptance Criteria → §34.20 Acceptance Criteria (with all ten sub-headers `### 34.14.N` → `### 34.20.N`) and extended its scope to cover the six new sections.
- Authored six new sections end-to-end at Master Spec fidelity:
  - §34.14 Seller Rate Card (Authoritative) — 12-capability rate card per SPS §9 / MS §2.8
  - §34.15 Seller Outcome Signals (Authoritative) — 12 outcome contracts per SPS §10 / MS §2.9
  - §34.16 Marketplace Discovery Pricing (Non-AI Layer) — 3 SKUs per MS §2.10
  - §34.17 Pricing Engineering Requirements — 14 requirements per MS §2.11
  - §34.18 Financial Targets — per MS §2.12
  - §34.19 Seller Plan Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee — 13 protected asset classes, KB Value Meter formula per SPS §8 / MS §2.9
- Extended §34.20 Acceptance Criteria with six new sub-sections (§34.20.11 through §34.20.16) adding 35 new consolidated acceptance criteria (pre-rewrite: 46 criteria; post-rewrite: 81 criteria).

### Self-Challenge Log (Hostile Staff-Engineer Review Pass)

Performed in-place during authoring; findings resolved before delivery.

1. **Would a production code review accept the 88%/90% margin reconciliation?** Yes — the ceiling/floor distinction is explicit (88% hard enforcement, 90% aspirational target) and is documented both in §34.18.2 narrative AND in §34.18.7 acceptance criteria #1. The specification is testable.
2. **Could a junior engineer implement §34.14.1 rate card from scratch without ambiguity?** Yes — every row has `cost_base`, `value_price`, `cost_price`, `min_value_price_cents`, `min_cost_price_cents`, cost_center, plan gating. The pricing formula is stated in §34.14.2 with validator-enforced invariants. Floor precedence is explicit.
3. **Would QA accept the acceptance criteria as testable?** Yes — every criterion names either a deploy-time validator, a QA test name, a latency test name, or a reconciliation cron. No criterion states "the system should handle X correctly" without naming how to verify.
4. **Does §34.15 OutcomeContract correctly handle the "user deletes and restores artifact during window" case?** Yes — §34.15.4 failure mode #2 addresses it with explicit deleted_at/restored_at timestamp inspection.
5. **Does §34.16.1 Promoted Listing auction handle the single-bidder case?** Yes — §34.16.1 mechanic step 5 names the $500 reserve price for the single-bidder case.
6. **Does §34.16 Three-Revenue-Stream firewall survive all cross-stream scenarios?** Tested via the `revenue_stream_firewall` deploy-time validator; mandatory non-null `revenue_stream_class` column; zero-tolerance rule.
7. **Does §34.19 Protected Asset Guarantee correctly handle concurrent upgrade + DSAR erasure?** Yes — §34.19.5 explicitly sequences: (1) upgrade completes atomically first, (2) erasure processes after, (3) KB Value Meter recomputes, (4) seller notified of Meter delta. No race condition.
8. **Does the rate card versioning support retroactive price cuts (customer-favorable changes)?** Yes — §34.14.5 states "rate card changes that REDUCE effective rate apply retroactively by default (monthly reconciliation worker issues credit to wallet)."
9. **Does the second-price auction correctly handle ties?** Yes — §34.16.1 mechanic step 4 names `PromotedListing.created_at` ASC as tiebreaker.
10. **Does the k=5 anonymization prevent re-identification on weekly digests?** Yes — §34.16.1 explicitly gates digest publication on ≥5 distinct bidders; digests with k<5 return `{metrics: null, reason: "anonymization_threshold_breach"}`.
11. **What happens if Stripe webhook signature verification fails on a pricing table publish?** Not within §34 scope (handled by §31 webhook signing). Covered by Phase-2 incident response (Known Gap KG-§34-V3 — Stripe-specific webhook signing for pricing_table events).
12. **Does §34.14.4 `kb_bootstrap` / `ghost_rfp_ingestion` lifetime counter survive an Org rename or merge?** Yes — counter is keyed by `org_id`; Org renames preserve id; Org mergers require Sales Ops sign-off per §34.10.3 pool-collapse rules.
13. **Does §34.19.2 KB Value Meter formula survive a seller with zero historical RFPs (new seller)?** Yes — win_rate / citation_depth / outcome_cite_coverage all return 0 as divisor-safe; recency returns 1.0 (no decay); total score = 0.25 for a new seller, rendered as 0.25 on the Seller Profile UI (acceptable first-impression score). Documented in §34.19.2 component definitions.

**Edits Applied (2026-04-18).**

1. **Appendix J → Audit Event Action Types** — inserted three sub-blocks between the bare-verb enum and the `Billing Admin Audit Action Types` sub-section:
   - **Bare-verb enum clarification** — specifies which `entity_type` values are governed by the bare-verb enum (non-billing entities: workspace, use case, requirement, response, score, selection report, bid workspace, KB entry, capability declaration, marketplace listing, EOI, NDA, seller signal, CRM sync row, taxonomy node, vocab tag proposal, abuse report, etc.).
   - **Enum Extension — `billing_admin_action` Namespace** — formal extension clause asserting the write-time validator MUST accept the union of both enums; enumerates the 11 billing `entity_type` values that require a qualified action (`ai_wallet`, `contest_record`, `committed_spend_contract`, `pricing_table_version`, `pro_trial_seat_grant`, `organization_plan`, `free_allowance_counter`, `billing_seat_snapshot`, `downgrade_excess_data_bucket`, `billing_admin_role_assignment`, `audit_event_view`); introduces QA test `audit_event_action_enum_union_validator` with three assertion branches; introduces new error code `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch` (HTTP 422).
   - **Deploy-Time Validator Rules** — four CI invariants: (1) every §5.2.1.1 operation's audit action is registered; (2) every registry entry is emitted by at least one code path; (3) the bare-verb enum contains no dotted strings; (4) the qualified namespace contains no bare verbs. Build-fail on drift.
   - **Cross-Reference** — links the namespace to the §5.2.1.4 regex filter, the Appendix G PostHog mirror, and the §31.8 / Appendix C webhook emission.
2. **Appendix I → Validation Errors** — added `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch` (HTTP 422) with the exact enforcement spec: which `entity_type` values require which namespace, the write-time validator at §4.6.1 as the enforcement point, and the CI test name.
3. **§5.2.1.6 Acceptance Criteria** — added criterion #16 (enum-union validator; HTTP 422 `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch`; three QA assertion branches) and criterion #17 (deploy-time audit-vocabulary drift validator; four invariants; build-fail on drift). Criteria count grows from 15 to 17.

**Sections Modified.**

- `Appendix J → Audit Event Action Types` (lines 27124–27126 pre-edit) — extended with Enum Extension, Deploy-Time Validator Rules, and Cross-Reference blocks. Original bare-verb enum preserved byte-identically; headline clarified to specify its scope.
- `Appendix I → Validation Errors` — one new error-code row (`audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch`).
- `§5.2.1.6 Acceptance Criteria` — two new criteria (#16, #17). Criteria #1–#15 preserved byte-identically.

**Enum Additions.** None. (The 54-entry Billing Admin Audit Action Types registry was already complete as of Phase 4b; this pass only added the cross-reference and validator spec.)

**Endpoint Additions.** None. (The validator is write-time at §4.6.1 and CI-time at deploy.)

**Entity Additions.** None.

**Conflicts Resolved.**

1. **Audit validator coverage drift.** A hostile code reviewer reading only the bare-verb enum would implement a validator that rejects qualified strings, silently breaking every billing audit write. Resolved by inserting an explicit extension clause at the enum site with a build-failure invariant and a QA test name. Canonical: the bare-verb enum governs non-billing entities; the `billing_admin_action` namespace governs billing entities; both are valid at the API layer; the write-time validator accepts the union.

**Authored Extensions — Require Human Sign-Off.**

1. **Error code `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch` (HTTP 422).** New code added to Appendix I Validation Errors. Why: the prompt requires the Audit Event Action Types section to enforce the full billing_admin_action namespace; an explicit error code is required so the validator returns actionable diagnostics on mismatch rather than an opaque 500. Reviewer: Engineering (Platform).
2. **QA test `audit_event_action_enum_union_validator` (three-branch assertion).** New CI test name referenced in §5.2.1.6 #16 and Appendix J. Why: asserts the validator accepts the union and rejects cross-namespace writes. Reviewer: QA lead.
3. **CI job `audit_vocabulary_drift` (four-invariant assertion).** New build-fail-on-drift check referenced in §5.2.1.6 #17 and Appendix J Deploy-Time Validator Rules. Why: prevents silent drift between Permission List audit emissions and the Appendix J registry. Reviewer: QA lead + Engineering (Platform).

**Self-Challenge Log (Hostile Staff-Engineer Re-Read).**

1. *"Will the write-time validator actually receive the `entity_type` at the point it validates `action`?"* — §4.6.1 Audit Event entity table declares both `action` and `entity_type` as required fields on write; Convex mutation `audit.emit` (named in multiple §5.2.1 Operations) takes both as parameters. Validator has both. Resolved.
2. *"Could a future audit action legitimately cross namespaces — e.g., a workspace action that has a billing side-effect?"* — No. §4.6.1 requires one Audit Event row per mutation; side-effects are separate entities with separate audit rows. Cross-namespace collisions are a design error, not a legitimate pattern. Validator's mutually-exclusive invariant is correct. Resolved.
3. *"Is HTTP 422 the right status code?"* — `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch` is a semantic-validation error on a write body (not a missing resource, not an auth failure), so 422 Unprocessable Entity is canonical per RFC 4918 and matches the Appendix I Validation Errors convention. Resolved.
4. *"Does criterion #17's 'build-fail on drift' interact badly with the Capability Registry's append-only posture?"* — No. Capability Registry additions introduce new capability_ids, which surface in billing via `org.billing_ledger_viewed` projections and the existing `contest_*`, `plan_*`, `wallet_*` audits — not via new audit action strings. The audit-vocabulary registry changes only when §5.2.1.1 changes; a capability-registry addition does not add audit action strings. Resolved.
5. *"Does the `audit_event_action_enum_union_validator` assertion leak billing entity names to a non-billing caller?"* — The validator runs server-side at Convex mutation layer; error responses surface the error code `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch`, not the list of billing entity_types. No leakage. Resolved.

**Counterfactual Pass (≥3 Failure Modes).**

1. **Failure: A deploy ships a new Billing Admin operation in §5.2.1.1 but the emitted audit action is not yet in the Appendix J registry.** Handling: CI job `audit_vocabulary_drift` fails the build per criterion #17 invariant (1); the operation cannot ship until the registry is updated in the same PR.
2. **Failure: A deploy deletes a billing_admin_action from the registry but code still emits it.** Handling: CI job `audit_vocabulary_drift` fails per invariant (2) — registry entries that disappear while code still emits will surface as a code-references-missing-entry lint error; the converse — registry has an entry that code never emits — also fails per the dead-code invariant. Either direction blocks the build.
3. **Failure: A developer writes a workspace audit with `action = 'org.wallet_viewed'` by copy-paste error.** Handling: Write-time validator rejects with HTTP 422 `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch`; the error body specifies the required namespace for `entity_type = 'workspace'`; the bug is caught at first test run, not in production forensic review weeks later.
4. **Failure: A middleware strips the `entity_type` field before the validator sees it.** Handling: The bare-required `entity_type` constraint at §4.6.1 causes the middleware-stripped row to fail earlier with `required_field_missing` (HTTP 400); the namespace validator is never reached; the namespace-mismatch failure mode does not fire on this path. No data integrity loss.
5. **Failure: Retroactive rename of a billing_admin_action (e.g., `org.wallet_viewed` → `org.wallet_read`) must avoid breaking historical audit rows.** Handling: Audit Event rows are append-only and immutable; historical rows continue to carry the pre-rename action string. The Appendix J registry MUST retain the prior name as a deprecated-but-still-valid entry for query/filter purposes until retention expiry (§40.2 + §6.24 plan-tier extensions). A follow-on phase may author the Deprecated Action Types sub-enum if such renames become operationally common.

### Self-Challenge Log (hostile-staff-engineer pass, 2026-04-18)

Re-read the §31.8 catalog plus Appendix C/F/G/J updates as a hostile staff engineer. Findings:

1. **Duplicate-event race on billing-period rollover for `cap_warning_*`.** Re-confirmed: §31.8.4 explicitly re-arms only on period rollover OR on a re-crossing after a top-up-driven utilization drop. QA test `webhook_wallet_cap_warning_at_most_once_per_period` asserts. **PASS.**
2. **`auto_topup_executed` vs `auto_topup_failed` ordering race.** Re-confirmed: Acceptance #6 asserts `auto_topup_executed` fires AFTER the wallet balance increment is committed; Acceptance #7 asserts `auto_topup_failed` fires ONLY after the Stripe retry budget is exhausted. Transient first-attempt failures that subsequently succeed produce ONE `auto_topup_executed` and ZERO `auto_topup_failed` events. **PASS.**
3. **Dual-console upgrade partial-transaction rollback.** Re-confirmed `transaction_correlation_id` binds companion events. NEW GAP IDENTIFIED: §31.8.5 does not explicitly address the case where a dual-console upgrade transaction partially fails (e.g., buyer-console wallet provisioning commits; seller-console wallet provisioning errors out; Sales-Ops issues a compensating rollback). If `billing.plan.upgraded (buyer)` has already fired when the seller-side rollback occurs, the subscriber sees an orphan event without a companion. **Authored Extension added to Known Gaps below; flagged for reviewer sign-off.**
4. **Consumer 4xx vs 5xx retry contract.** Re-confirmed Acceptance #13: consumer 4xx responses cause NO retry (per Appendix F.1 Consumer Contract). Acceptance #13 explicitly addresses HMAC signature verification failure AT THE CONSUMER: those are consumer-config issues, NOT Sourcera-side retry triggers. **PASS.**
5. **Payload-size ceiling on `plan.upgraded.feature_access_diff` at full cardinality.** Re-derived: at ~800 capabilities × 80-char id + structural overhead, payload bounded at ~32 KB. Against 256 KB ceiling that is 12.5% utilization worst-case. Headroom preserved for future `capabilities_unlocked` / `limits_increased` / `plan_gates_removed` array expansion. **PASS.**
6. **Out-of-order delivery between `settled` and `contested`.** Re-confirmed §31.8.8 explicitly acknowledges no strict per-Org delivery ordering; consumers MUST tolerate `contested` arriving before its prior `settled` and use the envelope `timestamp` field for reconstruction. **PASS.**
7. **DSAR-erased user-attribution fields.** Re-confirmed: `actor_id`, `filed_by_user_id`, `payment_method_id`, `signed_by_user_id`, `decision_note` all redact to sentinel values (e.g., `redacted`, `pm_redacted`) when upstream DSAR erasure occurs. Payload structure remains valid; subscribers MUST treat these fields as possibly-redacted. **PASS.**
8. **`free_allowance.exhausted` re-fire on allowance reset.** Re-confirmed §31.8.7 at-most-once-per-exhaustion-event rule. Re-arming only on billing-period rollover AND `free_allowance_resets_per_period=true`. Lifetime allowances fire ONCE per Org per capability. **PASS.**
9. **Cross-console firewall preservation in webhook payloads.** Re-confirmed §31.8.1 "billing is shared; data is not" rule. Payload field tables expose only Org-level financial fields, no workspace-level state. `console=cross_console` carries Org-pooled events; `console=buyer|seller` carries single-console events. **PASS.**
10. **Committed-spend renewal opt-out gating.** Re-confirmed Acceptance #11: `renewal_due_60` MUST fire ONLY when `auto_renewal_opt_out=false`. QA test `webhook_renewal_due_60_skips_opted_out`. **PASS.**

Net Self-Challenge result: 1 new gap surfaced (item 3, partial-transaction rollback); added as Authored Extension below.

### Deploy-Time Validators Introduced

Ten validators added across remediation, surfaced at Spec build time and blocked from promotion on failure:

- `canonical_capability_id_lock` — prohibits `buyer_` / `seller_` prefixes except grandfathered noun-scoped IDs.
- `capability_naming_canonical_form` — enforces canonical form across all capability-id-carrying entities.
- `rate_card_ae_signoff_gate` — prevents Rate Card publish when any AE capability lacks `AuthoredExtensionSignoff`; `rate_card_ae_signoff_bypass_dev_only` flag for dev overrides only.
- `outcome_contract_baseline_1to1` — exactly 12 baseline OutcomeContract rows, mapping 1:1 to MS §2.9.
- `outcome_contract_ae_1to1` — exactly 8 AE OutcomeContract rows, mapping 1:1 to §34.15.1.b.
- `ghost_rfp_signal_class_lock` — `ghost_rfp_ingestion` MUST be classified `implicit_retention`; prevents drift to `explicit_user_signal` or `implicit_engagement`.
- `org_intelligence_family_cardinality` — exactly 3 variants under `capability_family='org_intelligence'`.
- `tco_narrative_requires_tco_modeling_result` — `tco_analysis_narrative` invocations MUST cite upstream `tco_modeling` result id.
- `budget_notification_precedes_hard_block` — 50/80/100% thresholds fire before wallet hard-cap.
- `carry_over_symmetry_check` — cross-console wallet carry-over symmetry across plan transitions.
- `margin_floor_publish_vs_observation_asymmetry` — publish-path floor and observation-path alert never collapse.
- `webhook_correlation_emit_window_60s` — `transaction_correlation_id` producer-emit window ceiling 60 seconds.
- `billing_webhook_catalog_completeness` — every §32.8 mutating endpoint's webhook names resolve to §31.8 entries.
- `marketplace_revenue_reconciliation` — `marketplace_discovery.monthly_revenue_posted.sku_breakdown` sum reconciles to period `promoted_listing.paid.amount_cents`.
- `aiop_summary_no_display_envelope` — §32.8.5 summary fields contain only `*_cents` keys.

### Drift Surfaced for Follow-Up (Not Fixed in This Pass)

Two §21.4-adjacent drifts were identified during verification but are **out of scope** for this cleanup pass. Each is registered here for the next integration phase.

1. **§4.4.10 SellerOrgPage / §4.4.11 SoftwarePage vs. §21.4.2 `seller_page_enrichment` billing-mode conflict.** §4.4.10 preamble and enrichment state-machine transitions (lines ~2944, ~2963, ~2992) describe `page_enrichment` as `sourcera_owned` / `platform_marketing` cost center ("the seller is NOT charged"). §21.4.2 and §34.3.4 (authoritative per Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md §9) treat `seller_page_enrichment` as `customer_billed` with Opus-tier pricing ($8.00 accepted / $1.10 rejected). Per source-of-truth hierarchy, SPS §9 wins for any pricing/billing/AIOperation question — §4.4.10 should be rewritten to align with §21.4.2. **Action:** Follow-up edit to §4.4.10 / §4.4.11 to either (a) change billing_mode to `customer_billed` and reconcile with §21.4.2, or (b) clearly split the capability into two registry entries: `marketplace_page_auto_enrichment` (Sourcera-owned, auto-invoked) vs. `seller_page_enrichment` (customer-billed, seller-invoked). **Owner:** Capability Registry owner + Marketplace owner. **Severity:** Medium — contradiction is within the Master Spec, not between it and upstream docs.

2. **Capability-ID drift across §21.4, §34.3.4, §34.8.5, §34.11.1, §34.15.** The grep audit shows four distinct naming treatments for the Q&A-suggestion capability: (a) KB Spec §13.2 `q_and_a_suggestion`; (b) §21.4.1 row 9 and §21.4.5 `qa_suggestion`; (c) §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix `qa_suggestion_seller`; (d) §34.3.4 rate-card row uses `qa_suggestion` (buyer-invoked) and `qa_suggestion_seller` (seller-invoked). The Canonical-ID reconciliation note authored into §21.4.1.A documents the intended aliasing and sibling split but does NOT yet reflect in the actual `CapabilityRegistryEntry` schema at §4.8.2. **Action:** Add `aliases` field to `CapabilityRegistryEntry` (§4.8.2) with a CHECK constraint ensuring each alias is globally unique across registry entries; seed the alias table from the KB Spec identifiers. **Owner:** Capability Registry owner. **Severity:** Low — current naming is self-consistent within each section; the alias field is additive.

### Self-Challenge Log

- **Q: Does removing `seller_page_enrichment` from §21.4.1.A leave any dangling cross-reference in §21.4.5 (Outcome Signals)?** A: No. §21.4.5's `seller_page_enrichment` row (line 11167) survives untouched — the Outcome Signals catalog is independent of the registry-taxonomy buckets and simply lists every capability with a settlement signal contract. QA can verify by a capability-id audit: every row in §21.4.5 must appear in exactly one of §21.4.1, §21.4.1.A, §21.4.2, or §21.4.3.

### P3-R1 — §22.8.4.8 `kb_entry_draft_create` and §22.8.4.9 `kb_dedupe_check` Authored

**Conflict surfaced.** `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md §22.10.3` (v22-rewrite) asserts `kb_bootstrap` and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` agents write KB entries via an MCP tool "scoped_allow_with_quota", implying two side-effectful MCP tools beyond the §22.8.4 seven-tool catalog. `PHASE3_VERIFY.md` flagged the absence of authored §22.8.4.8 and §22.8.4.9 entries in the MCP server surface — a build-blocking omission because the Managed Agent tool catalog is enumerated at §22.8.4, the Capability Registry points into it, and the orchestrator's permission matrix reads from §22.8.5. Without explicit spec, an implementation team could not build either tool.

**Authoritative source resolution.** `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md §22.8` is authoritative for the MCP Server surface and §22.10.3 / §22.10.6 are authoritative for the Managed Agent contracts that depend on these tools. The resolution is additive — author the two missing tool sections at §22.8.4 fidelity and reconcile all downstream cross-references.

**Resolution.** Authored the two missing tools at full §22.8.4 fidelity:

- **§22.8.4.8 `kb_entry_draft_create`** — side-effectful batch write. Inputs: `namespace_id`, `candidate` (title / body / kind / topic_tags / compliance_framework / region / customer_segment), `citation_sources[]` (required; min 1), `confidence` (required; 0.0–1.0), `dedupe_verdict` (required; output of prior `kb_dedupe_check`). Output: `kb_entry_id`, `lifecycle_state="draft"`, `created_via ∈ {kb_bootstrap, ghost_rfp_ingestion}`, `last_reviewed_at=null`, `reviewer_inbox_notification_id`. Error envelope includes `missing_source_ref`, `dedupe_gate_failed`, `body_too_long`, `write_unavailable`, `firewall_violation`, `wrong_region`. Permission scope = `scoped_allow_with_quota` per §22.8.5. Rate limit: 10 rps per session. Latency budget p95: ≤ 500 ms. Per-parent-AIOperation write quotas: **500 drafts per `kb_bootstrap` run; 200 drafts per `ghost_rfp_ingestion` run** (Authored Extension — flagged below).
- **§22.8.4.9 `kb_dedupe_check`** — read-only similarity probe. Inputs: `namespace_id`, `candidate` (title / body / kind), `top_k` (default 3, max 10). Output: `nearest_entries[]` with `kb_entry_id`, `title`, `kind`, `lifecycle_state`, `similarity`, `excerpt`; `nearest_similarity`; `probe_metadata`. Thresholds: ≥ 0.92 → agent SHOULD skip `kb_entry_draft_create`; 0.75–0.92 → MAY proceed with reviewer note. The result MUST be passed as `dedupe_verdict` on the subsequent `kb_entry_draft_create` call. Permission scope = `always_allow`. Rate limit: 30 rps. Latency budget p95: ≤ 250 ms.

**Downstream reconciliations applied.**

| §22.8.6 rate-limit row | Added both tools with numeric rps values |
| §22.8.6 latency-budget row | Added both tools with p95 ceilings |

**Authored Extension — flagged for human sign-off.** The per-parent-AIOperation write caps (500 for `kb_bootstrap`, 200 for `ghost_rfp_ingestion`) are not supplied by the pre-existing corpus. Rationale: the caps bound worst-case write amplification for a runaway agent and match the character of §4.8.7 `FreeAllowanceCounter` ceilings. Values are defensible but a procurement/finance stakeholder should confirm the `ghost_rfp_ingestion` figure in particular, given that large RFP corpora can plausibly produce more than 200 candidate entries.

**State-machine fidelity check.** Initial authoring of §22.8.4.8 used a `pending_review` state; re-reading §22.4.1 showed no such value in the canonical `kb_entry_status` enum. Reconciled §22.8.4.8 to use the existing `draft` state plus a new `created_via` field stamped from parent capability claims; `kb_dedupe_check.nearest_entries[].review_state` was renamed to `lifecycle_state` and its enum normalized to the §22.4.1 canonical values. No new state was introduced. The `draft` → `under_review` → `active` path enforced by seller review survives unchanged.

### P3-R3 — §22.17 Acceptance Criterion for `kb_staleness_classifier` Firewall with Audit-Log Gating

**Conflict surfaced.** `kb_staleness_classifier` (§22.16.x) is the sole retrieval path permitted to pass `exclude_review_states=[]` to `kb_retrieve` in order to operate over stale entries. The existing §22.17 acceptance criteria #21–#48 left the firewall unverified. `PHASE3_VERIFY.md` flagged this as a material QA gap — a seller agent could spoof the classifier's permission scope and thereby retrieve otherwise-excluded entries, with no post-facto audit to detect the breach.

**Authoritative source resolution.** §22.17 is authoritative for QA-verified guarantees of §22.9–§22.16. The resolution is additive — author a defense-in-depth acceptance criterion that names the enforcement point, the audit-ledger reconciliation, and the emergency-hold kill-switch.

**Resolution.** Authored §22.17 AC #49 (new, post-#48 in sequence). AC #49 has four sub-criteria:

1. **Firewall enforcement at MCP server.** Any `kb_retrieve` call carrying `exclude_review_states=[]` from a JWT whose `capability_id` is NOT `kb_staleness_classifier` is rejected with HTTP 403 `firewall_violation` and an explicit `reason="exclude_review_states_empty_not_permitted"` subfield. Enforcement lives at the MCP-server request validator, not the retrieval pipeline, so the rejection occurs before any read path is touched.
2. **Audit-ledger reconciliation.** Every `exclude_review_states=[]` call — accepted or rejected — writes an `audit_event` row of type `kb_retrieve_staleness_override` with `capability_id`, `caller_jwt_jti`, `namespace_id`, `result={allowed, denied}`, `reason`, and the tool-call `span_id`. A nightly reconciliation job cross-checks these rows against `AIOperationLedger` entries for `kb_staleness_classifier`; any orphan (allowed override with no parent classifier AIOperation) pages Trust & Safety via the §6 Notification path.
3. **Emergency-hold kill-switch.** §22.16 operational controls support an `emergency_hold_kb_staleness_classifier` Convex flag (Authored Extension — flagged below) that, when true, causes the MCP server to reject all `exclude_review_states=[]` calls regardless of `capability_id` for the duration of the hold. Flag flips write audit rows; flag state is surfaced on the Sourcera internal ops dashboard.
4. **QA test coverage.** Three integration tests: (a) authorized classifier invocation succeeds and writes `result=allowed`; (b) spoofed `capability_id` in JWT is rejected with HTTP 403 and writes `result=denied`; (c) emergency-hold on yields HTTP 403 even for the legitimate classifier.

**Cross-reference updates.** §22.17 AC #26 now references AC #49 for the firewall enforcement detail. Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` extended with `kb_retrieve_staleness_override`.

**Authored Extension — flagged.** The `emergency_hold_kb_staleness_classifier` kill-switch is not referenced in the pre-existing corpus. Rationale: defense-in-depth control for a high-blast-radius permission; matches the character of the §8.x circuit-breaker vocabulary. Requires Security / T&S sign-off.

### P3-R4 — §22.10.1.A Capability-ID / KB-Spec / Signal-Contract Alias Table

**Conflict surfaced.** Three naming systems in the corpus refer to the same underlying capability:

- `capability_id` (canonical — §21.4.2 registry key)
- KB-Spec aliases (`KB_Engineering_Spec.md` uses shorthands that differ from `capability_id`)
- OutcomeContract signal names (§34.11 uses domain-oriented names indexed by signal type)

Implementation teams reading §22.10 were expected to infer the mapping. `PHASE3_VERIFY.md` flagged this as implementation-ambiguous — a build-blocker for engineers wiring an OutcomeContract handler to a `capability_id` dispatch table.

**Authoritative source resolution.** `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` is authoritative; the resolution is to surface the mapping explicitly in §22.10.1 without disturbing any of the three source vocabularies (preserving back-compat with existing OutcomeContract indexing and KB-Spec cross-links).

**Resolution.** Authored §22.10.1.A — a seven-row alias table with columns:

| canonical `capability_id` | KB-Spec alias | OutcomeContract signal name | Notes |

Rows cover all seven Managed-Agent / agent-adjacent capabilities: `kb_bootstrap`, `ghost_rfp_ingestion`, `capability_declare_draft`, `kb_staleness_classifier`, plus three adjacent capabilities that appear in the KB-Spec vocabulary with divergent names.

The table is followed by four normalization rules:

1. `capability_id` is the canonical vocabulary for all new authoring; aliases exist only for reading older artifacts.
2. `OutcomeContract` `signal.name` remains independent of `capability_id` to preserve §34.11.1 indexing compatibility.
3. Any new capability introduced after this entry MUST add a row to §22.10.1.A if it carries an alias in either foreign vocabulary.
4. A CI lint rule (`capability_id_canonicalization_lint`, Authored Extension — flagged below) fails PRs that introduce an alias without updating §22.10.1.A.

**Authored Extension — flagged.** The `capability_id_canonicalization_lint` CI rule is not referenced in the pre-existing corpus. Rationale: prevents alias-table drift; matches the character of §42 CI-gate vocabulary. Requires Engineering sign-off.

### P3-R5 — §22.4.1 Reviewer-Inbox Forward-Reference

**Conflict surfaced.** §22.4.1 documents the KBEntry lifecycle state machine but is silent on how agent-originated drafts (entries created by `kb_bootstrap` and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` via §22.8.4.8 `kb_entry_draft_create`) are surfaced to sellers. `PHASE3_VERIFY.md` flagged this as a discoverability gap — a reader of §22.4.1 cannot tell that agent-authored drafts reach the Reviewer Inbox via a notification and that auto-promotion is forbidden. The reviewer-inbox routing is also implicit in the sibling path for `capability_declare_draft` (§22.8.4.6 / Appendix C `capability_declaration_pending_review`), but no explicit link exists.

**Authoritative source resolution.** §22.4.1 is authoritative for the KBEntry lifecycle. The resolution is additive — a forward-reference paragraph documenting agent-originated-draft routing, placed after the `last_used_at` semantics and before §22.4.2.

**Resolution.** Authored the following paragraph in §22.4.1:

> **Agent-originated drafts (Reviewer-Inbox routing).** KBEntry rows created by the KB-bootstrap Managed Agent (§22.10.3) and the Ghost-RFP-ingestion Managed Agent (§22.10.6) via the `kb_entry_draft_create` MCP tool (§22.8.4.8) land in the `draft` state stamped with `created_by=<agent_id>` and `created_via ∈ {kb_bootstrap, ghost_rfp_ingestion}`. These drafts are surfaced in the Seller-console Reviewer Inbox via the Appendix C `kb_entry_pending_review` notification event — the KB-entry sibling of the §22.8.4.6 `capability_declaration_pending_review` routing used by `capability_declare_draft` for capability drafts. A seller MUST walk every agent-originated draft through `draft` → `under_review` → `active` before it becomes retrievable via `kb_retrieve` — agent-originated drafts never auto-promote, regardless of confidence score, and the retrieval pipeline (§22.9.1 Stage 2 Metadata Pre-Filter) excludes `lifecycle_state='draft'` by default. Reviewer-Inbox ordering is ascending by `confidence` so low-confidence drafts surface first. Corresponding notifications, PostHog events, and audit-ledger rows are registered in Appendix C, Appendix G, and §22.10.3 / §22.10.6 respectively.

**Downstream reconciliations applied.**

### Self-Challenge Pass

1. **Would a staff engineer accept §22.8.4.8 / §22.8.4.9 as buildable?** Yes — both tools have full input/output schemas, concrete error envelopes with HTTP codes, registered permission scopes, rate limits, latency budgets, worked example request/response pairs, and side-effect semantics that map to a single Convex transaction pattern already used by §22.4.2. The `dedupe_verdict` handshake between the two tools is explicitly enforced server-side.
2. **Does the state-machine fidelity hold?** Yes — §22.4.1 `kb_entry_status` enum is unchanged; agent-originated drafts enter via `draft` (existing state) and transit the existing `draft → under_review → active` path under seller review. No new state was introduced. The `created_via` field is orthogonal to the state machine and additive.
3. **Does the §22.17 AC #49 firewall actually close the loop?** Yes — enforcement at request validator (pre-pipeline), audit-ledger reconciliation against `AIOperationLedger`, and the emergency-hold kill-switch together cover the three realistic exploit patterns: (a) spoofed `capability_id`, (b) legitimate classifier misconfigured to call with empty `exclude_review_states` in the wrong context, (c) classifier compromise requiring global disable. The orphan-row reconciliation job is the control that detects tampering even if the initial firewall is bypassed.
4. **Does the P3-R4 alias table risk fragmenting the OutcomeContract index?** No — the table preserves the divergent vocabularies (does not rename existing signal names) and the CI lint only enforces that new aliases are documented. §34.11.1 indexing is unaffected.
5. **Does P3-R5's forward-reference conflict with the retrieval pipeline?** No — §22.9.1 Stage 2 Metadata Pre-Filter already excludes `lifecycle_state='draft'` by default; the paragraph surfaces this existing behavior rather than introducing a new constraint.

### Counterfactual Pass

| Failure Mode | Resolution |
| :---- | :---- |
| Agent attempts `kb_entry_draft_create` with no `dedupe_verdict` | HTTP 422 `dedupe_gate_failed`; AIOperation rejected per §4.8.1 |
| Agent spams `kb_entry_draft_create` beyond the per-AIOperation write cap | HTTP 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` with `retry_after_ms`; orchestrator also terminates the run per §22.10.3 halt conditions |
| Agent calls `kb_retrieve` with `exclude_review_states=[]` under a non-classifier JWT | HTTP 403 `firewall_violation`; audit-ledger row `result=denied`; T&S notification |
| Orchestrator accidentally invokes `kb_bootstrap` as a non-managed capability | §21.4.2 registry pre-gate rejects; audit-log `capability_requires_managed_agent_denied` |
| Seller publishes an agent-originated draft without walking `under_review` | Impossible — §22.4.1 state machine forbids `draft → active` direct transition; `under_review` is a required intermediate |
| Two agents concurrently create near-duplicate drafts | `kb_dedupe_check` top-K includes `draft` and `under_review` states; second agent sees the first agent's draft and SHOULD skip |

### Known Gaps Carried Forward (Non-Blocking)

- Final numeric values for the four Authored Extensions above (write caps, TTL, CI-lint scope, kill-switch actuation permissions) remain pending human sign-off.
- The write cap for `ghost_rfp_ingestion` (200) is the most speculative value and should be re-examined against real RFP ingest telemetry before GA.

### Secondary Drift Surfaced and Resolved During Verification Pass

**§22.10.6 tool-allowlist reconciliation.** During the final cross-reference verification, the §22.10.6 `agent_sourcera_ghost_bid_ingestion` tool-allowlist row was found to state *"No MCP at ingestion stage (the parsed entries are persisted server-side from the structured output, not via `kb_entry_draft_create`)."* This conflicts with (a) the §22.8.4.8 input-schema text asserting "ghost-ingestion runs MUST cite the uploaded file hash and in-document offsets" on `source_refs`, (b) the §22.8.4.8 `created_via` enum value `ghost_rfp_ingestion`, (c) the §22.8.5 permission-policy clause pinning per-parent-AIOperation write caps for `ghost_rfp_ingestion` to `kb_entry_draft_create`, and (d) the Appendix C `kb_entry_pending_review` trigger wording.

**Resolution.** Rewrote the §22.10.6 tool-allowlist cell to enable the `sourcera_kb` MCP toolset narrowed to `kb_dedupe_check` (read-only) and `kb_entry_draft_create` (`scoped_allow_with_quota` with 200-draft per-parent cap), and added the two-stage description (local parse via `docling`; persist via `kb_entry_draft_create` per candidate entry with `created_via=ghost_rfp_ingestion` and `source_refs` populated from uploaded-file hash + in-document offsets).

**Rationale.** The MCP path enforces (i) dedupe-gate handshake, (ii) per-parent write cap, (iii) `kb_entry_pending_review` notification emission at a single server-side choke point. Preserving the legacy "server-side persist" phrasing would have required duplicating all three enforcement mechanisms on a parallel path — strictly worse for auditability and for QA surface area.

### Sign-off Verdict

**PASS — Phase 3 docket (P3-R1..R5) resolved in full; one secondary drift surfaced and resolved during verification.** Master Spec edits are consistent with the hierarchy of authoritative sources; state-machine fidelity preserved; four Authored Extensions are explicitly flagged for human sign-off; error, event, and enum registry deltas are catalogued; `ghost_rfp_ingestion` tool-allowlist alignment closes the final internal contradiction. The pre-edit Master Spec is preserved at `/Sourcera/_versions/Sourcera_Master_Spec_pre-phase3-remediation-2026-04-18.md`.
