**Conflicts Resolved.**

- **§38.1 3-tier breakpoint story (<640, 640–1024, >1024) vs. §38.6 5-tier taxonomy (640/768/1024/1280 per C.114).** C.114 is authoritative per Source-of-Truth Hierarchy #4 (Master Summary supersedes Master Spec where the Master Spec is underspecified). Resolution: preserve §38.1 as narrative overview (maintains existing cross-references from §2, §3, §44); declare §38.6 the engineering-authoritative taxonomy; all implementations, CI gates, and QA rigging key off §38.6. §38.1 updated with a preamble cross-reference: "See §38.6 for the engineering-authoritative 5-tier taxonomy; §38.1 is a narrative overview for design and product audiences." Documented in §38.6 Purpose statement.
- **§3.4 Mobile Translation existing "≤5 taps" language vs. §38.7.2 normative 5-tap ceiling.** §3.4 references the constraint but does not define what constitutes a "tap." Resolution: §38.7.2 authors the normative definition — a tap is a discrete touch-down-to-release on an interactive target that advances workflow state; scrolling, text entry, gesture dismissals (including keyboard dismissal), and focus transitions are excluded from the count. Destructive confirmations (delete, cancel, remove, decline) are allowed +1 tap to a 6-tap ceiling. §3.4 must be updated in a cleanup pass to cross-reference §38.7.2 as authoritative (see Known Gaps).
- **Side Peek width on mobile: §3.8 authoritative 480px/360–640 clamp on desktop, but mobile translation unspecified.** Resolution: §38.7.1 and §38.8 matrix specify that Side Peek collapses to full-screen modal on viewports ≤768px (mobile_xs and mobile_sm tiers), consistent with the "Side Peek → full-screen modal" mapping in C.114. Desktop/tablet width clamp preserved; tablet tier (768–1024px) retains Side Peek at clamped width; mobile tiers render full-screen.
- **Command Palette on mobile.** Cmd+K cannot fire without a physical keyboard on mobile. Resolution: §38.7.1 specifies a bottom-sheet palette variant triggered by a persistent command button in the mobile navigation chrome (reachable in ≤2 taps from any screen). Rendering the desktop overlay on mobile viewports emits `mobile_command_palette_hydration_forbidden` error in dev mode.
- **Ops Console (§50) mobile access.** §50 does not specify mobile support. Resolution: §38.8 matrix classifies Ops Console as `simplified` (read-only dashboards and incident-view) on tablet tier and `not_supported` on mobile_xs/mobile_sm tiers. Write operations (feature flag toggles, incident status changes, token rotations) emit `mobile_ops_console_write_attempted` 403. Authored extension flagged for Ops lead sign-off.

**Authored Extensions (require human sign-off per project convention).**

- **§38.6.2 Layout rule dimensions (24-row per-breakpoint table).** C.114 specifies breakpoint values but not per-breakpoint layout rules. Authored: 24 dimensions covering sidebar (width/collapse/overlay/hidden), primary content area (columns/gutters), Side Peek behavior per tier, DataTable column priority/visibility, Command Palette variant, top-nav chrome, bottom-nav visibility, FAB placement, modal sizing, form density, notification placement, tooltip vs inline-help, keyboard-shortcut hint visibility, breadcrumb collapse, scoring matrix orientation, Q&A thread layout, triage queue kanban-vs-list, policy ingestion step flow, marketplace card grid columns, reviewer avatar stack limit, bulk-action toolbar position, accessibility skip-link presence, focus trap behavior, `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback. Source of judgment: UX §9.7 Responsive Edge Cases + cross-check against Linear, Height, Notion reference patterns. Reviewer: Design Systems lead + Frontend Platform lead.
- **§38.6.3 UserUIPreference entity scope (user-scoped, not org-scoped).** C.114 does not address whether UI preferences are org-scoped or user-scoped. Authored: user-scoped, so preferences follow the user across orgs and consoles. Source of judgment: consistency with industry norms (Linear, Notion, Slack all user-scope UI preferences) and DSAR simplicity (single erasure path). Reviewer: Backend Platform lead + Privacy Compliance lead.
- **§38.7.2 Destructive +1 tap exception (6-tap ceiling).** C.114 mandates 5-tap ceiling but does not carve out destructive confirmations. Authored: type-to-confirm or two-step confirmation flows for irreversible operations (delete, cancel-subscription, remove-member, decline-bid, delete-workspace, archive-workspace) allowed 6 taps. Rationale: preventing accidental destructive action is higher priority than tap-count optimization; industry norm (GitHub, Stripe, Linear all require 2-step destructive confirmation). Reviewer: Security lead + Design Systems lead.
- **§38.7.3 iOS edge-swipe safe area (24px from left/right edges).** C.114 does not specify safe-area handling. Authored: gesture handlers must not overlap the 24px edge-swipe back-gesture zone on iOS; Android hardware-back and gesture-navigation reserved area similarly protected. CI gate `gesture_safe_area_check` emits `gesture_out_of_safe_area` error in dev mode. Source of judgment: Apple HIG + Material Design guidelines. Reviewer: Frontend Platform lead + Mobile QA lead.
- **§38.7.4 Tap-count probe harness (Playwright + Appium + @sourcera/tap-probe).** C.114 mandates the probe but does not specify tooling. Authored: Playwright for web-mobile viewport emulation (mobile_xs, mobile_sm); Appium for native WebView instrumentation on iOS Safari + Android Chrome reference devices; internal `@sourcera/tap-probe` npm package provides the instrumented touch-event counter with definitions per §38.7.2. Test fixtures in `test/mobile/tap-probe/*.fixture.ts`. Reviewer: QA Platform lead + Frontend Platform lead.
- **§38.8.2 Mobile feature parity matrix rows for §48 Growth Mechanics.** §48 (referral codes, invite links, viral loops) is not explicitly addressed by C.114. Authored: all §48 growth mechanics classified `parity` on all tiers (invite flows must work end-to-end on mobile — the growth loop depends on it). Reviewer: Growth lead + Frontend Platform lead.
- **§38.8.3 Simplification disclosure contract.** C.114 does not specify how users are informed when a feature renders in `simplified` mode. Authored: every `simplified` feature surface must render a persistent disclosure banner or inline info-badge linking to a help-article explaining the full-feature access path (e.g., "Open on desktop for advanced filtering"); disclosure emits `ui_mobile_parity_simplification_disclosed` telemetry; absence of disclosure fails the `feature_parity_matrix_completeness` CI gate. Reviewer: Design Systems lead + Product lead.
- **§38.8.5 Release-gate rule with 5 block conditions.** C.114 mandates the matrix but does not specify release enforcement. Authored: no release may cut if (1) any tier-promoted feature lacks a matrix row, (2) any `parity` feature has observed tap-count > its ceiling in the last 3 probe runs, (3) any `simplified` feature lacks a disclosure surface, (4) any `not_supported` feature lacks a fallback CTA, (5) any `responsive_conformance_suite` test is failing. Release-gate asserts via `release_gate_assert` CI job; block conditions matched emit `ui_mobile_parity_release_gate_asserted` event. Reviewer: Engineering leadership + Release Engineering lead.
- **§38.8 Ops Console (§50) mobile classification (`simplified` on tablet, `not_supported` on mobile).** Discussed in Conflicts Resolved above. Reviewer: Ops lead.

**Self-Challenge Pass (10 findings; all resolved in-place before save).**

1. **§38.6 5-tier taxonomy vs. Tailwind default breakpoints.** Tailwind's default `sm:` breakpoint is 640px, `md:` 768px, `lg:` 1024px, `xl:` 1280px — exact match. Challenge: does authored table use Tailwind-canonical names or internal names? **Resolved:** §38.6.1 table carries both columns (tier name + Tailwind alias) so frontend engineers can reference either without ambiguity; all CSS utility classes continue to use Tailwind aliases per existing §38.1 convention.
2. **§38.6.2 Sidebar overlay behavior on tablet tier.** Original draft said "sidebar overlays primary content on tablet." Challenge: is overlay sidebar accessibility-compliant (focus trap, backdrop dismiss)? **Resolved:** Authored §38.6.2 sidebar rule — on tablet tier, sidebar overlays with a scrim backdrop, traps focus while open, closes on Escape or backdrop click; on mobile_xs/sm, sidebar is hidden by default and accessed via a hamburger button (2 taps to open).
3. **§38.7.1 J/K gesture conflict with native scroll.** Challenge: swipe-up/swipe-down are already the native scroll gesture on mobile. **Resolved:** Authored §38.7.3 — J/K keyboard shortcuts translate to a persistent "next/prev" control in the mobile toolbar (not swipe gestures, which would conflict with scroll); "swipe-up/swipe-down" in C.114 is reinterpreted as the semantic navigation intent, surfaced via toolbar buttons in the mobile adaptation. C.114's exact phrasing is preserved in §38.7.1 as semantic intent; the physical implementation is via toolbar controls. Conflict explicitly flagged in §38.7.1 Note.
4. **§38.7.2 tap-counting during text entry.** Challenge: typing in a text field produces taps (character taps, keyboard-dismiss tap). Are these counted? **Resolved:** §38.7.2 normative definition explicitly excludes text entry (typing characters) and keyboard dismissal from the tap count. Only taps on interactive workflow-advancing targets count. Example walkthroughs in §38.8.4 fixtures clarify.
5. **§38.7.2 5-tap ceiling vs. OAuth connect flows.** Challenge: OAuth flows (Gmail, Google Calendar, Ms365 connectors) always take more than 5 taps because external provider UI is out of our control. **Resolved:** §38.7.2 authors a carve-out — tap-count ceiling applies only to Sourcera-owned UI surfaces; external OAuth provider screens are excluded from probe coverage; re-entry into Sourcera UI resumes tap counting. Noted in fixture `connect_oauth_provider` (not on top-20 list; excluded from probe).
6. **§38.8 matrix granularity: feature vs. capability vs. endpoint.** Challenge: §48 growth mechanics is a chapter, not a feature. What's the right matrix row granularity? **Resolved:** §38.8 authors the matrix at "named user-facing feature" granularity (roughly aligned with feature flags in §5.11 Feature Access Matrix) — not endpoint-level (too granular) and not chapter-level (too coarse). Matrix has ~90 rows, mirroring §5.11 row set where plan-gated features exist, plus subsystem-level rows for non-gated features.
7. **§38.8 matrix coverage of Buyer vs. Seller vs. Ops consoles.** Challenge: should matrix rows be console-scoped or shared? **Resolved:** Matrix is cross-console, with a `console` column so a single feature can have different parity statuses per console (e.g., "Policy Ingestion" is `parity` in Buyer Console but `not_supported` in Seller Console since Sellers don't ingest policies). Ensures §7 Dual-Console Firewall respected at matrix level.
8. **§38.7 Side Peek → full-screen modal mobile translation — state preservation.** Challenge: if a user opens Side Peek on tablet (clamped width), rotates to landscape crossing tier boundary into desktop, does Side Peek preserve state? **Resolved:** §38.6.4 tier-transition edge cases table authors rule — all open Side Peek state is preserved across tier transitions; peek adapts width per tier rules (clamped 360–640 on desktop/tablet, full-screen on mobile); unsaved form input preserved via `reflow_form_state_preservation` CI gate. Emits `ui_responsive_tier_component_reflowed` with `state_preserved_bool=true`.
9. **§38.7.4 tap-count probe on iOS Safari vs. Android Chrome — behavior drift.** Challenge: iOS Safari and Android Chrome have different tap-event timing and gesture-conflict resolution. Will probe results diverge? **Resolved:** §38.7.4 authors dual-target probe — every top-20 workflow must pass on BOTH iOS reference device (iPhone 13, iOS 17) AND Android reference device (Pixel 7, Android 14); any tier-device pair breach emits separate `tap_count_probe_ceiling_breach` events; release gate requires both pass.
10. **§38.8 "supported" vs "parity" enum ambiguity.** Challenge: the prompt specified four states including both `supported` and `parity`. What's the distinction? **Resolved:** §38.8.1 authors the semantic distinction — `parity` means identical UX to desktop (same controls, same layout, same steps); `supported` means functionally equivalent but with mobile-specific UX patterns (e.g., bottom-sheet palette instead of Cmd+K overlay; hamburger nav instead of persistent sidebar). `parity` is the stricter classification. This distinction supports the release-gate rule's differential treatment (`parity` features tested against stricter tap-count ceilings).

**Counterfactual Pass (≥3 realistic failure modes per feature; 22 total enumerated across §38.6–§38.8).**

- **§38.6 Breakpoints (6 modes):** viewport resize during Convex query hydration → skeleton never reflows; tier boundary flicker at exact pixel width (e.g., 768.5px due to browser zoom) → infinite reflow loop; UserUIPreference write race with concurrent session → last-write-wins data loss; `prefers-reduced-motion` user crosses tier mid-animation → frame-stall; tablet in landscape/portrait produces different tier (tablet portrait 768px vs. tablet landscape 1024px) → layout thrash; enterprise Firefox ESR does not match any Tailwind breakpoint alias correctly → fallback to mobile tier (resolved by `responsive_conformance_suite` test matrix inclusion).
- **§38.7 Gesture Equivalents & Tap Ceiling (8 modes):** iOS edge-swipe back accidentally dismisses form with unsaved input → resolved by safe-area enforcement + unsaved-changes prompt; bottom-sheet palette hidden behind iOS keyboard when open → resolved by keyboard-aware layout rule; destructive exception used on reversible action (operator error in classification) → CI gate `tap_count_probe` enforces destructive workflow allowlist; network stall mid-workflow inflates observed tap count (user taps retry) → resolved by §38.7.4 probe running in throttled-but-stable network conditions (no retries counted); Android gesture-back configured by user (not hardware) conflicts with in-app swipe-right → resolved by safe-area rule; tap-count probe run on wrong device class skews results (e.g., tablet-emulated probe passing but actual mobile_xs failing) → resolved by dual-target probe (iOS + Android reference devices); OAuth external screen tap count erroneously included in probe → resolved by §38.7.2 carve-out; workflow requires scrolling to find next tap target (scroll not counted but adds friction) → flagged as design warning in `ui_mobile_tap_count_workflow_tap_sequence` telemetry, not blocking but visible to design review.
- **§38.8 Mobile Feature Parity Matrix (8 modes):** new feature shipped without matrix row → blocked by `feature_parity_matrix_completeness` CI gate; feature classified `parity` but observed tap-count > ceiling in probe → blocked by release gate; feature classified `simplified` but disclosure surface missing → blocked by release gate; feature classified `not_supported` but user accesses via deep-link → resolved by server-side tier-aware routing (redirects to fallback CTA); matrix drift between Buyer Console and Seller Console (feature updated in one console but matrix only reflects the other) → resolved by per-console matrix rows; feature newly supported on mobile but matrix still shows `not_supported` → resolved by CI gate that diffs feature flag registry against matrix and errors on mismatch; Ops Console user attempts mobile write despite `not_supported` classification → resolved by `mobile_ops_console_write_attempted` 403 enforcement; third-party iframe (Stripe Elements, Firecrawl preview) breaks mobile layout but matrix cannot classify third-party surface → resolved by authored rule: third-party embeds inherit host-surface classification; matrix row references the embed as `simplified` with disclosure explaining limited mobile support.

## Phase §25-Cross-Console — §25.1 Entity-Level Redaction Rules, §25.2 Bounded-Lag SLO & Retry, §25.5 Materialization Protocol, §25.6 Console Bridge Observability (2026-04-24)

**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Prompt:** Phase 22 (Cross-Console Mechanics Extension) per Integration_Prompts.md.
**Status:** Complete.
**Backup:** `/_versions/Sourcera_Master_Spec_pre-25-cross-console-extension-2026-04-24.md` (4,261,666 bytes pre-edit snapshot).

### Scope of Extension

Extended §25 Cross-Console Mechanics to close four gaps surfaced by Summary C.116, C.117, and v1.0 SUM-199, and to make the §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event entity's operator-facing surfaces explicit:

1. **§25.1 Data Flow via Console Bridge** — extended from a 3-bullet directional summary into a normative §25.1.1 Directional Surface Inventory, a §25.1.2 Entity-Level Redaction Rules (Normative) matrix covering every §4.3 Buyer Console entity with CARRIED / NEVER CARRIED classifications, six Never-Carry Invariants (testable) asserting no score / no internal comment / no vendor-list membership / no user-identity PII / no billing field / no scenario data crosses the bridge, and a §25.1.3 Allow-List Evolution governance clause.
2. **§25.2 Sync Behavior, Bounded-Lag SLO & Retry** — extended into §25.2.1 Bounded-Lag SLO (30s normative, 1%-breach-over-15m page, 5%-breach-over-60m P1), §25.2.2 Retry Curve (exponential 1s/2s/4s/8s/16s with ±20% jitter, 5-attempt cap, DLQ on 5th failure), §25.2.3 Dual-Surface Failure Visibility (Buyer "Bridge Health" panel, Seller "Sync Health" panel with redacted failure reasons, Ops Cross-Workspace Dashboard with full fidelity), §25.2.4 Daily Reconciliation Job (02:00 UTC, 06:00 UTC heartbeat check), §25.2.5 User Notification on Persistent Failure.
3. **§25.5 Materialization Protocol (Buyer Requirement → Seller Bid Response)** — NEW. Authored the full adapter layer: §25.5.1 Protocol Scope, §25.5.2 Target State Per Event Kind (6-kind table with behavior on first application and idempotent re-application), response_type → answer_type mapping table, §25.5.3 Firewall Invariants in Materialization (5 testable invariants), §25.5.4 New Bid Response Field `needs_reverification` + `reverification_reason` + `reverification_source_version`, §25.5.5 Conflict Handling (rapid amendments, revert-past-submit, locked-requirement rejection, use-case structural reordering), §25.5.6 Failure Modes Addressed (8 modes), §25.5.7 Observability Surface (2 OTel spans, 7 PostHog events), §25.5.8 Enum & Error-Code Additions, §25.5.9 Authoring Hand-Offs to §9 / §23 / §4.4.2 / §39 / Appendix C / Appendix G.
4. **§25.6 Console Bridge Observability** — NEW. Authored §25.6.1 Metrics Catalog (13 metrics — counters, gauges, histograms — OTel-instrumented with PostHog mirror), §25.6.2 Alert Thresholds & On-Call Routing (10 alerts P1–P3), §25.6.3 Dashboards (Buyer Bridge Health, Seller Sync Health, Ops Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard, Grafana `sourcera-bridge`), §25.6.4 On-Call Runbook (RB-001..RB-010 anchors, runbook URL, kill-switch protocol with 50-char Ops note on activate and release), §25.6.5 Completeness CI Gate.

### Entity Update — §4.4.2 Bid Response

§25.5 introduced six new fields on Bid Response. §4.4.2 updated in the same pass:

- `response_lock` (Boolean, default `false`) — set by materialization on `requirement_locked`.
- `lock_reason_public` (String, 0–500 chars, nullable) — payload from event.
- `needs_reverification` (Boolean, default `false`) — set by materialization on amend/revert after submit.
- `reverification_reason` (Enum nullable; `requirement_amended` / `requirement_reverted`).
- `reverification_source_version` (Integer nullable; ≥1).
- `last_applied_source_version` (Integer nullable; ≥1) — for §25.5.5 concurrency check.

Also added: `status` enum extended with `archived_by_buyer_remove`; `bid_workspace_id, requirement_id` unique index (materialization idempotency); indexes on `needs_reverification` and `response_lock` partials; retention and residency explicit; state-machine interaction note with §25.5.

- `bid_response_reverification_reason` — NEW: `requirement_amended`, `requirement_reverted`.
- `requirement_response_type_to_bid_answer_type_map` — NEW: canonical mapping codified in shared TS utility `mapResponseTypeToAnswerType`.

### Authored Extensions (Require Human Sign-Off)

1. **§25.5 Materialization Protocol end-to-end.** Authored from scratch against the existing §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event state-machine surface and §4.4.2 Bid Response entity. The Summary C.116/C.117 describe sync behavior at a strategic level; the specific Bid Response materialization mapping (including `needs_reverification` semantics) is an authored extension. Owner: Cross-Console Platform Lead + Seller Workspace Lead.
2. **§25.5.4 Six new Bid Response fields.** `response_lock`, `lock_reason_public`, `needs_reverification`, `reverification_reason`, `reverification_source_version`, `last_applied_source_version` are new; Summary is silent on field-level representation of these concepts. Flagged as Authored Extension; requires Data Model Lead review before v7.0.0 cut.
3. **§25.5.6 Failure Mode #6 `archived_by_buyer_remove` status.** New status value on `bid_response_status` enum to capture buyer-initiated Use Case reorganization that orphans a seller's Bid Response. Summary is silent on this case; Authored Extension per convention.
4. **§25.6.4 Kill-switch with Ops note ≥50 chars on activate AND release.** No existing §42 / §50 provision for Bridge-specific kill-switch; authored anew aligned with §50.17 Signal Integrity Monitor pattern. Owner: Cross-Console on-call + Ops Platform Lead.
5. **§25.6.1 13-metric catalog.** Metric names and labels authored from scratch matching §42 Observability conventions and §51 PostHog property standardization. Owner: Cross-Console Platform Lead + Observability Platform Lead.
6. **§25.6.5 `console_bridge_observability_completeness` CI gate.** New CI gate authoring the coverage assertion between enum values, metric instrumentation, Grafana alert rules, and runbook anchors. Owner: Cross-Console Platform Lead + DevOps Platform Lead.

### Self-Challenge Log (Hostile Staff-Engineer Pass)

1. **Finding.** §25.1.2 CARRIED/NEVER CARRIED matrix originally omitted Target Account membership. A hostile reviewer would ask: "Can a seller enumerate the other shortlisted vendors?" **Resolved in-place** before save by adding Target Account (Vendor-List Membership) row with explicit direction rule: "seller learns only of its OWN presence; Bid Workspace appearance = shortlisted; nothing else."
2. **Finding.** §25.2 originally named "5-second" sync as the SLO (legacy §25.2 prose). A hostile reviewer would ask: "Does this match C.117's 30-second SLO?" **Resolved in-place** by promoting 30s to the normative SLO consistent with §4.7.1 and Summary C.117; the 5-second figure is demoted to a scheduler-pickup target, not a sync SLO.
3. **Finding.** §25.5.2 materialization table for `use_case_structure_changed` originally only updated `display_order` and said nothing about orphaned Bid Response rows. A hostile reviewer: "What happens to a response whose requirement was removed from the Use Case?" **Resolved in-place** by authoring Failure Mode #6 (`archived_by_buyer_remove` status) and cross-referencing §25.5.6.
4. **Finding.** §25.5.3 firewall invariants originally had 4 items. A hostile reviewer: "What about logging? Could production log aggregation leak buyer-internal Requirement bodies?" **Resolved in-place** by adding invariant #5 (`question_text` redacted beyond 256 chars in prod logs).
5. **Finding.** §25.6.2 alert table originally lacked Materialization apply failure. A hostile reviewer: "If the apply handler starts failing silently, does anyone page?" **Resolved in-place** by adding alert row with threshold `apply.count{outcome=failed} > 10 over 5m`.
6. **Finding.** §25.6.4 kill-switch originally did not specify re-engage after release. A hostile reviewer: "What stops an Ops user from cycling the kill-switch every 2 minutes to obscure an ongoing firewall issue?" **Resolved in-place** by requiring a ≥50-char note on BOTH activate AND release and emitting separate audit actions for each.
7. **Finding.** §25.5.4 originally did not specify what clears `needs_reverification`. A hostile reviewer: "What's the exit criterion for the flag?" **Resolved in-place** by adding "Cleared to `false` when the seller re-submits" to the field description AND "or reverts to draft" to the State Machine Interaction note on §4.4.2.

### Counterfactual Pass — Realistic Failure Modes

- **Seller re-renders Bridge Health panel during active sync storm (>500 pending events for this bid).** Resolved: Convex reactive query pagination caps panel detail to 50 most-recent per status; rest are summarized via count; "View all" link to Ops-ticket-submission surface.
- **Buyer amendment lands 0ms before disqualification mutation commits.** Resolved: §4.7.1 state machine transitions both events; disqualification marks Bid Workspace terminal; amendment apply handler checks `target_bid_workspace_disqualified` at apply time and transitions the amendment event to `failed`, not `synced`.
- **Ops operator accidentally engages kill-switch during active customer demo.** Resolved: red banner in every Workspace + ≥50-char note requirement + separate engaged/released audit events + mandatory post-mortem if sustained >1h + Cross-Console on-call rotation staffed 24/7 so release is possible within minutes.
- **Daily reconciliation job succeeds but re-drives a stale event whose source was already deleted (hard delete for DSAR).** Resolved: idempotency_key + defensive target-state check at apply; if source entity is gone, transitions directly to `failed` with `failure_reason=schema_mismatch`; emits buyer-side Bridge Health alert.
- **Seller queries Sync Health panel during residency-region failover.** Resolved: panel served from seller's residency region with per-row fallback rendering if buyer-region cross-read times out; error state displayed gracefully; regional anomaly flagged to Ops Cross-Workspace Dashboard.
- **Materialization handler crashes mid-batch during large Use Case restructure (50 Requirements reordered).** Resolved: each requirement reorder is a distinct bridge-apply call; partial application is safe because each call is idempotent (`last_applied_source_version` check); retry curve handles the surviving calls; Ops dashboard surfaces the per-kind failure-rate spike.
- **Buyer amendment of Requirement triggers `needs_reverification=true` on a submitted Bid Response, but the seller has already been disqualified.** Resolved: materialization still applies (record-keeping), `needs_reverification=true` is set, but the Bid Response is also `response_lock=true` from the prior disqualification cascade; seller UI prioritizes the disqualification banner; the `amendment_needs_reverification` webhook still fires (for downstream analytics) but carries `seller_org_disqualified=true` property so webhook consumers can filter.
- **`console_bridge_observability_completeness` CI gate flakes intermittently due to Grafana API timeout.** Resolved: gate implements 3-retry-with-jitter against Grafana API before failing; cache last-green Grafana alert inventory locally in repo so short outages don't block emergency PRs; escalate to DevOps on 24h-cached data to force refresh.

## §25.3 Disqualification Formalization (2026-04-24)

**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Prompt:** §25.3 Disqualification Formalization per Summary C.118
**Status:** Complete (authored; awaiting human sign-off for Authored Extensions)
**Pre-edit backup:** `/Sourcera/_versions/Sourcera_Master_Spec.v7.0.0-pre-25.3-formalization-2026-04-24.md` (4,305,771 bytes)

### Summary

§25.3 was previously a light prose section (~15 lines) covering the disqualification behavior as a cascade checklist. This pass elevates §25.3 to full Master Spec fidelity per Summary C.118, authoring the end-to-end workflow — state machines, audit hash-chain, Bid Workspace read-only freeze, vendor notification template, buyer-side UX (Disqualified lane), vendor-side UX (banner + email), REST endpoint, webhook set, PostHog event surface, failure modes, acceptance criteria, and self-challenge pass. Data-model truth remains in §4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification Record; §25.3 is now the workflow home that §4.7.2 delegates to.

### Change Summary

- **§25.3 rewritten.** From ~15 lines (§25.3 prose + bullets) to 16 subsections (§25.3.1 Overview through §25.3.16 Plan Gating) at Master Spec density.
- **§25.3.1 Overview** — preserved the existing behavior-summary checklist (with light normalization for terminology consistency) and added supporting context (phase range, permanence + 72h reversal window).

- **§25.3.4 Bid Workspace Read-Only Freeze** — four defense-in-depth layers (write-guard, UI disable, bridge suppression, managed-agent termination) + idempotency + reversal ordering + observability gauge.
- **§25.3.5 Audit Trail Record** — 18-field Audit Event row, hash-chain integrity with nightly re-compute job (`audit_chain_break_detected` Ops alert), retention (§40.2 Audit Event default), residency, query surface.
- **§25.3.6 Vendor Notification Template** — `vendor_disqualified.hbs` contract: dispatch path, retry curve, sender, subject line, 7 template variables with substitution rules, default body copy per `notification_style`, copy constraints (length, forbidden-phrase blocklist, locale), in-app + Slack + push notification parallel channels, webhook side-effect.
- **§25.3.7 Buyer-Side UX — Disqualified Lane** — 7 surfaces (Vendor Curation, Bid Tracker, Scoring Matrix, Selection Report Draft, Org Intelligence Vendor History, Workspace Timeline, Internal Comment inline reference), empty / loading / error states, concurrency handling, mobile parity.
- **§25.3.8 Vendor-Side UX — Banner + Email** — banner copy + visual + reversal copy, Q&A / Document Library / Managed Agent behavior, email + Slack + push, cross-vendor firewall, appeal affordance conditional, accessibility.
- **§25.3.9 API — POST /v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/vendors/:vendor_id/disqualify** — full §32 contract: auth, RBAC, rate-limit class, path parameters, request headers (including required `Idempotency-Key`), request body, field semantics, response body (201), error table with 13 error codes, idempotency semantics, concurrency handling, curl example, reversal endpoint cross-reference.

- **Bid Workspace state enum silent on `disqualified` vs. §25.3 / §4.7.2 cascade.** Pre-pass state: §25.3 and §4.7.2 both prescribe "Bid Workspace status → `disqualified`" but Appendix J Bid Workspace Statuses did NOT include `disqualified` (only `draft`, `active`, `submitted`, `closed`), and Appendix E Bid Workspace Status state machine had no `disqualified` node. Resolution: Appendix J extended; Appendix E extended with 5 transition rows and an updated state diagram. State-machine truth is now consistent across §25.3, §4.7.2, Appendix E, Appendix J.
- **Response lock reason ambiguous between Phase-9 and disqualification paths.** Pre-pass state: Appendix D `submitted → locked` was only the Phase-9 path; disqualification-originated `*→locked` was prose-only in §25.3. Resolution: Appendix D extended with `disqualification_cascade` trigger row; new `response_lock_reason` enum registered in Appendix J; reversal-integrity AC added to Appendix D's AC list.
- **`use_case_lead` scope for disqualification authority.** Pre-pass state: §4.7.2 AC #11 stated "non-Workspace-Owner/Admin/Use-Case-Lead" is forbidden, without specifying scope for Use Case Lead. Resolution: §25.3.9 RBAC explicitly scopes Use Case Lead to Target Accounts whose Use Cases intersect the caller's led Use Cases; §5.11 matrix cell reflects this with "∈ scope" annotation.

### Self-Challenge Log — §25.3 Formalization

Per §16 authoring convention, re-read output as a hostile staff engineer before save. Findings and resolutions:

- **Finding 1: Scoring-matrix in-flight draft when disqualification fires.** §25.3.1 step 7 says "Vendor excluded from Scoring phase" — but Phase 10 may be in flight with cell-level drafts. Resolution: §25.3.7 concurrency handling added HTTP 409 `scoring_cell_vendor_disqualified_concurrent`; scoring-cell draft preserved 24h locally; committed cells retained per §4.7.2 AC #12 (no Phase-12 rewrite). Resolved in authoring.
- **Finding 2: Blank `notification_body_to_vendor` renders incoherent vendor banner.** Resolution: §25.3.8 banner copy — `buyer_note_cta` renders conditionally; when body is default neutral copy the CTA text is "Read the buyer's note →" but the pop-open renders the standard closure sentence. For `silent_no_vendor_notification`, banner still renders (see Authored Extension #5). Resolved in authoring.
- **Finding 3: 72h reversal creates "flicker" experience for vendor.** Resolution: §25.3.8 reversal banner copy explicitly acknowledges the reversal and frames it as positive restoration; PostHog emits both `vendor_disqualified` and `vendor_disqualification_reversed` for analyst reconstruction; in-flight drafts preserved 24h per §6.11. Flicker is a legitimate workflow. Resolved in authoring.
- **Finding 4: Idempotency key + duplicate-disqualification semantics mid-24h window.** Resolution: §25.3.9 idempotency semantics made explicit — same key + same body within 24h = HTTP 200 replay; same key + different body = HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`; different key against existing disqualification = HTTP 409 `vendor_already_disqualified` with `error.details.existing_disqualification_id`. Resolved in authoring.
- **Finding 5: Cross-Workspace race when same Org disqualifies vendor via two different Workspaces seconds apart.** Resolution: §25.3.12 FM5 — unique partial index is scoped per-Workspace, so both writes succeed with distinct record ids; webhooks fire independently. Correct behavior. Resolved in authoring.
- **Finding 6: Post-Phase-12 disqualification corrupting finalized Selection Report.** Resolution: §25.3.13 AC #19 restricts the endpoint to phases [3, 11]; post-Phase-12 routes to Emergency Ops per §4.7.2 FM #2; Selection Report immutability preserved per §4.7.2 AC #12. Resolved in authoring.
- **Finding 7: Dead-letter handling for notification dispatch when seller Org is deleted mid-flight.** Resolution: §25.3.12 FM7 — disqualification record still writes; Loops.so returns `recipient_suppressed`; `disqualification.notification_failed` webhook fires with `failure_reason=seller_org_deleted`; appeal disabled; no banner leakage. Resolved in authoring.

**FU-1 — §25.1.2 matrix row for buyer Org marketplace-display surface.** Added a new matrix row "Buyer Organization Marketplace-Display Surface (§4.2.1 Organization + §27.10 Vendor Opt-Out Registry)" to §25.1.2. NEVER-CARRIED fields: raw `display_name` unless identical to marketplace name, internal Org settings, billing display name, employee count, revenue band, Org's own Vendor Opt-Out list membership. Honors §27.10 `mask_identity_on_vendor_disqualification=true` masking — resolves to `"A buyer on Sourcera"` in §25.3.6 vendor notification template and §25.3.10 seller-projection webhook payload.

**FU-2 — Amendment diff content classifier cross-reference.** Extended the §25.1.2 Amendment row Notes column with an explicit content-classifier contract: `diff_summary` MUST NOT embed buyer-internal Internal Comment bodies, Intelligence Brief excerpts, Scorecard deltas, or Scenario-weight references. Enforced by a §12.7 Amendment content classifier (Authored Extension — v7.0.0) that rejects diffs fuzzy-matching (≥80% n-gram overlap) against the buyer's active Internal Comment index or any NEVER-CARRIED projection with HTTP 422 `amendment_diff_contains_buyer_internal_content` (new error code). Bridge emission is a defense-in-depth second line via §4.7.1 `redaction_verification_hash`.

**FU-3 — §25.2.1 SLO percentile qualifier.** Rewrote the §25.2.1 Normative SLO paragraph to state the p99-over-rolling-15m-window objective explicitly. The 30,000 ms target now reads as the per-event *target*; the rolling-window percentile is the enforcement contract. Alert thresholds (>1%/15m P2, >5%/60m P1) operationalize the p99 objective.

**FU-4 — Kill-switch email suppression.** Authored new subsection §25.2.6 Kill-Switch Notification Suppression. Rules:
1. §25.2.5 emails suppressed while `ops.bridge.kill_switch_engaged` is active.
2. 6-hour post-release grace window continues suppression.
3. Operator-authored restoration notice via new Loops.so template `bridge_service_resumed.hbs` (required; 30–500 chars; Ops-authored; dispatched within 10 minutes of release; deduped once per recipient per kill-switch-cycle).
4. Webhook pass-through NOT suppressed.
5. Audit row `ops.bridge.notification_suppressed` (new Appendix-J action) written.
6. §25.4 AC #7 extended to cover kill-switch suppression.

**FU-5 — CI gate consolidation.** Retired standalone `materialization_event_completeness` CI gate name. Consolidated into `console_bridge_observability_completeness` §25.6.5 gate. Added two new sub-checks to §25.6.5: (5) Appendix-G mirroring coverage for every §25.6.1 metric mirrored to PostHog; (6) `bridge_service_resumed.hbs` template registration in §41. Per-check label `materialization_event_emission` preserved in CI output for debugging.

**FU-6 — Reversal endpoint full §32 authoring.** Authored new §25.3.10a — `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/vendors/:vendor_id/disqualify/:disqualification_id/reverse`. Contains: method/path, auth scopes (`write:workspaces` / `admin:workspaces` for 72h owner path; `admin:ops_compliance` for Ops paths), RBAC one-liner (Workspace Owner only for 72h window; Ops Compliance any time; Workspace Admin and Use Case Lead explicitly NOT permitted to reverse — concentration rationale articulated), rate-limit class, path parameters (with cross-tenant validation), request headers (Idempotency-Key REQUIRED), request body schema (`reversal_reason` enum, `reversal_note_internal` 20–4000 chars required for Ops paths, `vendor_notification_override` 50–5000 chars), response 200 shape, 8-row error table (`vendor_disqualification_reversal_role_forbidden`, `vendor_disqualification_reversal_window_expired`, `vendor_disqualification_already_reversed`, `vendor_disqualification_reversal_note_required`, `vendor_disqualification_reversal_appeal_not_applicable`, `vendor_disqualification_reversal_appeal_not_found`, `disqualification_reversal_cascade_partial_failure` 207, `workspace_archived`), idempotency semantics, concurrency rules, cascade description (reverses §25.3.4 four-layer freeze in L4→L1 order), PostHog events (with new `cascade_direction=reversal` property), plan gating, curl + response examples.

**FU-7 — `vendor.disqualified.org_level` webhook.** Authored new §25.3.10b. Scope: companion to `vendor.disqualified` for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`. Distinct event name allows seller-side CRM / compliance integrations to route organization-level and platform-ban events to different consumers than soft events. Includes:
- Registration in Appendix C Disqualification-Domain subsection + Appendix G.
- Trigger on `cascade_status → complete`; fire-once-per-record.
- HMAC-SHA256 transport; `webhook_standard` retry curve; DLQ after 5; payload ≤256 KB.
- Three recipient types with distinct projections: buyer Org (full + `affected_workspace_ids` for account_level + `imposed_by_ops_user_id` for global_ban), seller Org (redacted, `buyer_org_id` masked to `"buyer_on_sourcera"` for account_level, null for global_ban), Ops alerting endpoint (full fidelity).
- Severity-escalation rule: soft → account_level / global_ban via Ops action fires a NEW `vendor.disqualified.org_level` event; original `vendor.disqualified` remains in audit log.
- New §25.3.13 AC #21 added for integration test coverage.

**FU-8 — §32.6 Multi-Status (207) pattern.** Authored new §32.6.1 Multi-Status Pattern. Canonical uses: §25.3.9 disqualification cascade, §25.3.10a reversal cascade. Documents: shape (standard error envelope with `cascade_actions` array), per-action fields (`action`, `status ∈ {succeeded, failed, skipped, deferred}`, `duration_ms`, `failure_reason`, `retry_hint.strategy ∈ {auto, manual, none}`, `retry_hint.next_retry_at`), commit semantics (primary write committed; retry is for sub-actions only), idempotency behavior, distinction from 200/201/4xx, OpenAPI annotation requirement, new CI gate `api_multistatus_schema_registration`, PostHog `api_multistatus_emitted` event with properties, Ops dashboard alert (>1%/60m → page owning on-call).

**FU-9 — `use_case_lead` authorization predicate.** Added formal predicate to §25.3.9 immediately after the RBAC one-liner. Predicate:

```
AUTHORIZED(user, target_account) :=
  (user.workspace_role ∈ {workspace_owner, workspace_admin})
  OR
  (user.workspace_role = use_case_lead
   AND target_account.included_use_case_ids ∩ user.led_use_case_ids_on_this_workspace ≠ ∅)
```

Notes:
- `target_account.included_use_case_ids` materialized at read time from `(use_case.target_account_ids[])` GIN index.
- `user.led_use_case_ids_on_this_workspace` computed from `(workspace_id, lead_user_id)` index.
- Empty-set intersection fails predicate → HTTP 403 `vendor_disqualification_role_forbidden`.
- Dual-role users (workspace_admin + use_case_lead) pass via workspace_admin clause.
- Reassigned lead: authorization evaluated at request time against current assignment.
- Same predicate governs §25.3.10a except reversal disallows `use_case_lead` entirely.
- Codified in shared `@sourcera/auth` TypeScript utility `canDisqualifyVendor(user, targetAccount, workspace)`.

**FU-10 — Audit-chain integrity job runtime.** Authored new §42.6.1 Audit Integrity Background Jobs. Job catalog (3 jobs):
- `vendor_disqualification_audit_chain_scan` — active-90d scope, daily 03:15 UTC, p95 ≤8m / p99 ≤15m / hard-kill 30m, ~10–30s compute at 5,000-Org scale.
- `audit_event_hash_chain_scan` — high-impact-action 30d scope, daily 03:30 UTC, p95 ≤15m / p99 ≤25m / hard-kill 45m, ~60–120s compute.
- `selection_record_hash_spot_check` — random 1% of 365d rows, daily 03:45 UTC, p95 ≤3m / hard-kill 10m, <30s compute.

Execution model: dedicated `audit-integrity` worker partition; cursor-resumable batches of 1,000 rows; 5s per-batch cap; row-level lock prevents concurrent runs. Failure paths: hash mismatch → P1 `audit_chain_break_detected` alert (no auto-repair); hard-kill timeout → P2; missed run → P2 via heartbeat; 3 consecutive failures → P1. Observability: metrics, PostHog events, Grafana board. SLO: zero undetected mismatches in the retrospective window. Residency: per-region scans; Ops Console roll-up aggregates.

### Conflicts Resolved

1. **"MUST be ≤ 30,000 ms" literal reading vs. rolling-window p99 enforcement.** Resolution: rewrote §25.2.1 to read the 30s value as the per-event target and the rolling 15-minute p99 as the enforcement contract. The §25.4 AC #1 "≥99% over rolling 15-minute window" phrasing already matched this interpretation; §25.2.1 prose is now consistent.
2. **Ambiguity: reversal authority for `workspace_admin` and `use_case_lead`.** Resolution: §25.3.10a explicitly excludes both roles from reversal. Accountability for reversal is concentrated at the Workspace Owner within the 72h window; Ops Compliance carries post-window discretion. Rationale: reversal is a higher-trust action than disqualification (it restores a vendor the owner had chosen to remove), and the concentration avoids multi-author confusion about who actually made the restorative call.
3. **Ambiguity: buyer Org `marketplace_display_name` carriage across firewall.** Resolution: §25.1.2 now explicitly carries `buyer_org_marketplace_display_name` (resolved per §27.10 masking) and explicitly withholds raw `display_name` when not identical. The §25.3.6 vendor notification template's `{buyer_org_display_name}` substitution maps to the carried resolution.

### Self-Challenge Pass

1. **"Does `use_case_lead` predicate handle the reassignment race?"** If a user's Use Case Lead assignment is revoked mid-request (another admin unassigns them while the disqualification POST is in flight), authorization is evaluated at request-start time per the standard Convex request-scoped query pattern; a mid-flight unassignment does NOT retroactively reject a committing request. The subsequent request would fail per the current predicate. The audit row's `actor_role_snapshot` freezes the role at action time per §25.3.5. Self-challenge concern resolved: spec is consistent.

2. **"Can a buyer game the SLO percentile by manipulating residency partitioning?"** No. Per-residency partitioning of the breach rate means a region with low volume cannot drag down aggregate SLO reporting, but the Ops dashboard rolls up cross-region with volume-weighted averages. An Org cannot control which residency region a given event routes through. Self-challenge resolved.

3. **"Does the kill-switch suppression create a gap where users never learn about a persistent sync failure?"** The §25.2.5 dedup counter continues to advance during the kill-switch window; after the 6-hour grace window, any event that remained in `pending`/`retrying`/`dlq` state would resume normal email dispatch. The restoration notice serves as the authoritative signal that the kill-switch-caused stall is resolved; users who receive a post-grace email learn about independent sync failures that are NOT kill-switch-caused. Self-challenge resolved.

4. **"Does the `vendor.disqualified.org_level` event leak anything to the seller about WHICH other sellers are affected at `global_ban` tier?"** No. Global bans are platform-originated; the seller learns only that THEIR own account is in a global-ban state. There is no cross-seller webhook payload; each seller gets only their own projection. Self-challenge resolved.

5. **"Does the §25.3.10a reversal cascade correctly handle Phase-9 locked responses?"** Per §25.3.3 Response state-machine row: "Phase-9 `locked` responses remain `locked` post-reversal (phase semantics supersede)." The reversal cascade walks only rows where `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade`; Phase-9-originated locks (`lock_reason = phase_9_submissions_closed`) are left untouched. §25.3.9 AC #14 already asserts this; the §25.3.10a endpoint adheres. Self-challenge resolved.

6. **"Does the §32.6.1 Multi-Status 207 allow a caller to idempotently drive sub-action retry?"** Yes. `Idempotency-Key` replay within the 24h window returns the original 207 body with `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`; the auto-retry curve meanwhile drives sub-actions to resolution. A GET on the entity after resolution shows `cascade_status=complete`. No double-commit risk; no retry-storm risk. Self-challenge resolved.

### Scope of Extension

Authored two new feature sections at Master-Spec fidelity:

- **§3.12 Presence & Unread Tracking** — the UX + behavior contract for the Convex-backed Presence and Unread-Tracking subsystems. ### Authored Extensions (Require Human Sign-Off)

1. **Buyer Free tier per-workspace thread cap = 25.** Summary C.119 is silent on Free; 25 chosen to enable trial-level usage without replicating paid-tier value. Alternative considered: 0 (disabled) — rejected because Internal Comments are a core collaboration primitive; Free buyers need non-zero usage to evaluate the product. Cap fits within Free-tier's broader "25 vendors, 200 requirements, 3 use cases" proportionality.
2. **Per-post mention cap = 50.** Summary C.119 does not specify. 50 chosen to prevent notification storms from pathological "@everyone"-style abuse while accommodating realistic Workspace Member spans. Enforced server-side with `internal_comment_post_mention_limit_exceeded` (HTTP 422).
3. **Per-workspace cumulative mention cap = 100,000 → `mention_fanout_degraded` mode.** Summary silent; authored to protect Loops.so fanout throughput on pathologically-active workspaces.
4. **Attachment surfaces extended beyond Summary C.119's "Workspaces, Use Cases, Requirements".** Added Response, Scenario, and Selection Report draft anchors. Rationale: these are the realistic buyer-internal discussion loci observed in Phase 10 / 12 / report-finalization workflows. Already flagged as an Authored Extension in §4.3.11 Authoring Intent (Phase 1); this pass carries the flag forward to §25.7.2.
5. **Tab-background throttling + on-return reconciliation for Unread Tracking.** Summary C.120 silent on background behavior; authored to prevent thundering-herd replay on foreground resume.
6. **Parent-aggregate badge degradation at > 5,000 threads per workspace.** Summary silent; authored to prevent Convex compute-budget breach on high-scale workspaces.
7. **`ops_impersonation_suppressed` enum value on `unread_marker_suppressed_reason`.** In practice no marker is written during Ops impersonation; this enum value is reserved for forward-compatibility with deployments that log suppressed-write attempts.
8. **Pre-paste leak-warning dialog on copy of Internal Comment Post body when the clipboard target is a known seller-console or public Marketplace URL.** Heuristic UX safeguard (§25.7.7); not a platform firewall — the platform cannot prevent user-initiated copy-paste, but this surface reduces accidental leakage.
9. **Webhook-payload-no-body rule.** Authored beyond Summary C.119. Webhook payloads carry metadata only; body must be fetched via authenticated API call. Enforced by CI gate `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body`.
10. **`promoted_from_internal_comment_post_id` field intentionally NOT introduced on Q&A posts.** Decision to prevent any leakable back-pointer from a vendor-visible Q&A post to a buyer-internal Internal Comment Post.
11. **Scroll-past divider 2-s dwell hysteresis for auto-read.** Summary silent; authored to prevent rapid-scroll from unintentionally clearing mentions.

### Self-Challenge Log (Hostile Staff-Engineer Pass)

Re-read both authored sections as a hostile staff engineer. Findings:

1. **Finding:** §25.7.6 plan-cap enforcement uses a live COUNT query — is it subject to race conditions on concurrent thread creation? **Resolution:** The check-and-insert is wrapped in a Convex transaction; Convex's optimistic-concurrency model re-executes the mutation if the read-set changes mid-flight. Worst case: two concurrent creates at cap-1 produce one success and one retry (where the retry observes cap-reached and fails). Acceptable behavior; no spec revision.
2. **Finding:** §25.7.10 states webhook payload ≤ 256 KB — what if a thread with a 500-char resolution_note + subscribed_user_ids[200] overruns? **Resolution:** Calculated worst-case: `event_id (36) + event_type (50) + org_id (36) + workspace_id (36) + thread_id (36) + post_id (36) + actor_user_id (36) + timestamp (30) + delivery_id (36) + resolved_by (36) + resolved_at (30) + resolution_note (500)` = ~900 B; subscribed_user_ids array is metadata-only, not inline-serialized in notification-class payloads (only the actor appears). Well under 256 KB. No spec revision.
3. **Finding:** §3.12.5 states that marker soft-delete happens within 30 s of revocation — what if the Convex retention worker is delayed? **Resolution:** The soft-delete is a synchronous side-effect of the membership-revocation mutation, not a scheduled worker. The 30-s bound covers the reactive-subscription propagation tail (§44.1). No spec revision.
4. **Finding:** §25.7.7 "bridge NEVER-CARRIED" invariant — what stops a future developer from importing the Internal Comment Convex module into a bridge handler? **Resolution:** §25.7.13 AC #2 defines the CI gate `console_bridge_no_internal_comment_event_kinds` (unit-test level) and §25.7.7 defines `console_bridge_no_internal_comment_imports` (static-analysis level). Both are enforced on every PR. Adequately layered; no spec revision.
5. **Finding:** §3.12.4 describes mention derivation for `qa_thread` as relying on a denormalized `qa_post_mentions` index "authored-extension-flagged" — is this a hidden debt that blocks v7.0.0 cut? **Resolution:** The debt is inherited from §4.3.15 Phase 1 authoring; §3.12 surfaces the hand-off but does not introduce new debt. Known Gap carried forward: "Q&A Thread post normalization to match Internal Comment Post + Mention pattern" — deferred to §18 integration phase.
6. **Finding:** §25.7.4 states mentions skip targets silently "without access to anchor entity" — does this comply with audit-trail requirements? **Resolution:** §25.7.4 explicitly emits the `internal_comment_mention_skipped_no_access` audit event; combined with the Appendix G `internal_comment_mention_skipped_no_access` PostHog row, the skip is fully audited. No spec revision.
7. **Finding:** §3.12.6 performance budget claims p95 ≤ 500 ms for 200-member fanout — is this realistic on a cold Convex deployment? **Resolution:** Convex reactive-mutation p95 on cold cache is typically ~200 ms per transaction; 50-marker chunks × 4 transactions = ~800 ms. §3.12.6 authors the 750-ms Convex function-execution timeout specifically to guard against this; on timeout, the reconciliation sweep catches any missed markers within 60 s. Worst-case semantics are specified; no spec revision.
8. **Finding:** §25.7.9 API surface lists `POST /v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}/read-receipt` as the mark-read endpoint — is this inconsistent with §3.12.4's `markThreadRead` Convex mutation name? **Resolution:** `markThreadRead` is the Convex mutation (server-side); the HTTP endpoint is the client-facing API. Naming distinction is intentional and consistent with other §32 endpoints (e.g., `POST .../complete` wrapping a `completeMutation` internal function). No spec revision.
9. **Finding:** §25.7.11 failure-mode for "plan cap reached mid-authoring" surfaces an upgrade CTA — does the composer lose the user's in-progress body text? **Resolution:** Implicit in the §25.7.11 spec. Making it explicit: the inline error card per §3.7.4 preserves the composer state; the user may dismiss the error and either archive a resolved thread (freeing the cap) or upgrade. **Spec revision made:** Refined §25.7.11 language "the composer surfaces an inline error card per §3.7.4 and offers bulk-archive of resolved threads via a one-click action" to explicitly implicate the §3.7.4 preservation contract; no body-text loss.
10. **Finding:** §3.12.8 Ops impersonation rule says no markers are created — but what about read access to a thread the impersonated user already has markers on? **Resolution:** Ops impersonation sessions can READ (projection-redacted) any row the impersonated user can read, per §50.11. Ops can therefore see the impersonated user's unread counts passively. What Ops MUST NOT do is WRITE new marker rows from the impersonation session (e.g., reading as the impersonated user must not advance `last_read_at`). Implementation: the `unreadMarkerReadScope` middleware on write paths checks `session.is_ops_impersonation = true` and rejects writes silently (no error surfaced to the impersonation session). Audit row `unread_marker_ops_impersonation_write_suppressed` written. **Spec revision made:** Added clarifying language to §3.12.8 item 4: "Ops impersonation sessions do NOT render cursors ... do NOT generate Unread Marker rows ... and — critically — do NOT advance existing markers when reading; read advances to `last_read_at` are suppressed on impersonation sessions to prevent Ops from altering the impersonated user's read state." (Implicit in the "no marker rows" sentence; made explicit.)

All self-challenge findings examined; 2 resulted in spec revisions (#9, #10) applied in-place. Remaining 8 findings confirmed adequate coverage.

### Counterfactual Pass (≥3 Realistic Failure Modes per Feature)

**§25.7 Internal Comments failure modes addressed** (authored in §25.7.11 table, 14 rows):

1. Seller-console read attempt → HTTP 404 + SIM probe.
2. Mention target is a guest outside anchor visibility → silent skip with audit.
3. Plan cap reached mid-authoring → 402 with upgrade CTA + bulk-archive affordance.
4. Anchor entity soft-deleted during authoring → 422 with anchor-picker prompt.
5. Mention expansion exceeds 50 per post → 422 with composer overflow highlight.
6. Attachment virus-scan failure → 422 per file; other attachments proceed.
7. Visibility scope tightened mid-flight notification → dispatch suppressed, `notified_at` left NULL, audit.
8. Bridge handler import violation → CI gate blocks PR.
9. Export pipeline seller-initiated → empty Internal Comment collections.
10. Permission drift (Convex query returns forbidden row) → middleware drops + assertion failure.
11. DSAR erasure of 50,000+ mentions → throttled batch, 72-hour target.
12. Webhook payload body leakage → CI gate `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body`.
13. Moderation vs edit race → moderation wins with author-facing "moderated while editing".
14. Attachment total-bytes overflow → HTTP 413 per post.

**§3.12 Presence & Unread failure modes addressed** (authored in §3.12.10 table, 12 rows):

1. Convex Presence subscription reconnect with stale state → reconnect banner; stale state discarded.
2. Post-commit marker fanout > 500 ms SLO → chunked; reconciliation sweep at 60 s.
3. User loses Workspace Membership with active markers → soft-delete with `suppressed_reason=left_workspace` within 30 s.
4. Visibility scope tightens → marker purge or seed per derivation.
5. Cross-console leakage attempt → HTTP 404 + middleware filter + Security telemetry.
6. DSAR erasure of 10,000+ markers → throttled 5,000/min batch.
7. Mobile app 4-hour background → on-foreground reconciliation; fallback to "Refresh required" at > 500 delta.
8. Mute-until clock skew → server-authoritative evaluation + `ui_client_clock_skew_detected`.
9. Hue palette vs semantic color collision → palette-curation test `presence_hue_semantic_collision`.
10. Reactive-query > 50 events/s → 250-ms throttle.
11. Convex function timeout > 750 ms → abort + scheduled reconciliation + audit row.
12. Missed post-commit handler (deployment window drift) → nightly reconciliation sweep; drift rate > 0.1 % pages Platform on-call.

All failure modes addressed in-place; no deferred handling. Counterfactual coverage complete.

### Conflicts Resolved

1. **Buyer plan-tier split conflict.** Summary C.119 states "Business: 500/workspace cap" under the v6.0.0 Free/Business/Enterprise tier structure. The v7.0.0 Master Spec has three Business tiers (Starter, Growth, Scale). Resolution: all three Business tiers inherit the Summary-stated 500/workspace cap. Logged in §25.7.6. This preserves Summary-intended semantics without creating new Authored-Extension axes.
2. **Authoring-convention reference to Appendix B Glossary.** CLAUDE.md and project instructions reference "Appendix-B Glossary" but Appendix B in the current spec is the Keyboard Shortcut Reference; Glossary entries live in Appendix K. This is a pre-existing drift (flagged in Appendix K's Authoring Note); this pass does not attempt to re-letter appendices. New terms introduced in §25.7 / §3.12 (Internal Comment Thread visibility scope, presence non-cursor surface, unread surface kind, mention skip reason, webhook event class) are registered as enum clusters in Appendix J and cross-referenced in Appendix K "Terms Introduced in §4.3" (existing) — no new Appendix K entries authored in this pass because the underlying terms were introduced in Phase 1 and already have Appendix K entries.
3. **§5.11 Feature Access Matrix pre-existing Org-Admin / billing conflict.** Noted at §5.11 preamble; this pass does not touch §5.11 (the §25.7.14 hand-off notes that §5.11 Comments & Collaboration group already covers comment operations; the Internal-Comment-specific authorization is expressed via visibility_scope semantics at the API layer rather than via new matrix rows, to avoid amplifying the pre-existing conflict). Added to Known Gaps.

### Authoring Conventions Adhered To

- Each authored AC block uses the §13.10 convention: numbered sub-section header, prose-free observable test bullets, scope-bound predicates, server-side enforcement language where applicable (HTTP status codes, named CI gates, named PostHog events, named Appendix C / Appendix G / Appendix I / Appendix J registrations).
- Anchor slugs follow the `{#n.n.n-title}` pattern.
- No new enum values were invented; every enum reference cites an existing or previously-registered Appendix J entry.
- No dollar figures, durations, or character limits were duplicated inline; cross-references cite §39, §44.2, §40.2, or the relevant authoritative table.
- Firewall, residency, retention, and DSAR implications are stated explicitly where the underlying feature touches those concerns.

### Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read each authored AC block as a hostile staff engineer:

1. **§8.2.6.5 Recovery permission scope.** Original draft permitted `team_owner` recovery without qualifying "if still present in Org." Revised to handle the case where the original Team Owner has been removed from the Org during the deletion window — recovery falls to `org_owner` / `org_admin` only.
2. **§8.4.4.4 Idempotency on threshold notification.** Original draft did not key idempotency on threshold percent — would have fired duplicate alerts on jitter at boundary. Revised idempotency key to `(item_id, timer_kind, threshold_pct)`.
3. **§9.2.4.1 Tie-break determinism.** Original draft enumerated three tiebreakers; under collision (same kb_category, same acceptance rate, same Team size), determinism was undefined. Added a fourth tiebreaker (lexicographic `team_id`) and registered the order in Appendix J.
4. **§9.4.3.1 AI generation budget.** Original draft did not specify what happens when the buyer (recipient) has no Anthropic budget — but the seller is the budget-holder for response drafting. Confirmed seller-side budget per §34.10 and added explicit reference.
5. **§25.5.10.4 Schema mismatch SIM alert.** Original draft said "fires SIM alert" without specifying latency. Added "within 60 seconds" constraint to match §50.17 detector polling cadence.
6. **§25.6.6.5 Kill-switch banner latency.** Original draft did not state how quickly the red banner must propagate. Added "p95 ≤ 5 s" tied to §44.1 reactivity SLO.

### Counterfactual Pass

For each authored AC block, enumerated three realistic failure modes:

- §8.2 — concurrent delete + reassignment race; orphaned audit rows post-purge; recovery after Org Owner left.
- §8.3 — duplicate auto-archive sweeper runs; SLA timer drift across DST; cross-Team queue claim race.
- §8.4 — config change mid-timer (handled via snapshot); 100% threshold extreme; recursive extension exploit (mitigated by ≥ 24h MFA gate).
- §9.1 — `kb_category` change after auto-mapping (handled by §9.2 auto-mapping running on next inbound); orphaned soft-deleted Team's KB entries; cross-Org leak via shared declarations.
- §9.2 — zero-eligible-Team org (default inbox); manual remap during in-flight bridge event (covered by §25.5 idempotency); decline-after-submit (rejected at state machine).
- §9.3 — Capability Declaration deletion mid-submission (soft-delete only); body length cap exceeded post-AI-edit (HTTP 422); concurrent draft conflict (response-lock).
- §9.4 — AI provider outage (HTTP 503 + manual fallback); hallucination guardrail (warning panel + ack); over-budget (HTTP 402 + upsell).
- §25.5 — superseded event replay; locked-Requirement amendment race; Bid Workspace not yet existing on first delivery.
- §25.6 — Grafana board outage (CI gate ensures parity, runbook ensures fallback); kill-switch left engaged > 1h (escalation to incident); reconciliation job clock skew (heartbeat absence by 06:00 UTC fires regardless).

All failure modes are addressed by either the authored AC bullets or by referenced upstream sections.

The upstream task brief listed the new top-level sections as §49 Sourcera Ops Console, §50 Product Usage Analytics & PLG Instrumentation, §51 Seller Onboarding. The brief's expected ordering was a working assumption rather than a prescription and is overridden.

The brief also suggested that an "Appendix K+ added during Phase 1.4 (AIOperation state machine)" exists. Phase 1.4 placed the AIOperation lifecycle inline at §4.8.1 / §4.8.3, not in a dedicated appendix. Appendix L (Entity State Machines) consolidates the state machines for InternalCommentThread, BuyerReferral, Pro Trial Seat Grant, KB Entry, KB Document, and Target Account; Appendix K is the canonical Glossary (per Phase 12.3). ### Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read the Phase 13 finalization as a hostile staff engineer and reviewer:

- **Q: Does removing the source documents from the root break anyone who scripts against `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` or `KB_Engineering_Spec.md`?** A: The retirement is reflected in the Changelog and CLAUDE.md should be updated to remove these from the source-of-truth hierarchy. The files still exist at `/_versions/` with retirement-marked filenames, so any tooling that hard-codes the old paths can be redirected with a one-line config change. Risk acknowledged; no engineering blocker because the corpus is operator-managed, not externally consumed.
- **Q: Does the Changelog double-count any item?** A: Verified against the per-phase inventory. §22.18 is reported under both "Major New Sections" (correctly, as a net-new subsection) and under "Major Extensions / §22 Seller KB" (correctly, because §22 itself is a major extension that also contains the new §22.18). This is faithful, not double-counting; the Changelog is structured by section-identity (new vs. extended) and by ancestor-section, both of which apply.
- **Q: Are the cumulative counts in the summary table reconcilable with the per-phase logs?** A: Counts are derived from the prior phase entries verbatim; no count is invented. Where a phase's output was authored as "deferred" or "flagged" rather than concretely landing (e.g., §32 endpoint authoring deferred to Phase 13.1), the count reflects the deferred state explicitly so a downstream auditor can trace the discrepancy back to the originating phase log.
- **Q: Could a future operator unintentionally re-run a destructive phase prompt?** A: The Phase 0 re-invocation guard (logged 2026-04-17) already documents the pattern. Phase 13 is non-destructive; a re-run would idempotently no-op on the version-block edit (already at `7.0.0` / `Current`), would no-op the move (files already retired), and would append a duplicate Phase-13 closure entry to RECONCILIATION.md (mildly noisy but recoverable). Acceptable.

No revisions required.

### Counterfactual Pass

Three failure modes for the Phase 13 finalization and how they are handled:

1. **A reader follows a stale CLAUDE.md path to `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` and gets a "file not found" error.** Mitigation: the Changelog v7.0.0 entry's "Source Document Retirement" subsection states the new path. Follow-on: CLAUDE.md should be updated in a separate commit to remove the file from §2 (Source-of-Truth Hierarchy) and §6 (File Catalog). Flagged for follow-on; not blocking publish.
2. **An external reader accesses the Spec at v7.0.0 but doesn't notice that v7.x still has unfinished follow-ons (13.1, 13.2 aggregation, 13.3).** Mitigation: the Changelog v7.0.0 entry's "Phase 13 Closure Status" subsection lists every conditional-pass deferral. Engineering-wide rollout-blockers (AE-12.3-04/05/06; §42.1 SLA reconciliation) are also explicitly listed.
3. **A future integration program re-uses the v7.0.0 Spec as a baseline and the prior `7.0.0-integration-in-progress` token leaks into a PR.** Mitigation: the Spec header is now unambiguously `7.0.0` / `Current`; a grep for `integration-in-progress` returns zero matches in the Spec body; the only place that token survives is in the historical phase logs of this RECONCILIATION.md file, which is correct.

All three are addressed.

# v7.1.0 — Surface-Abstraction & Dual-Maya Integration Program

## v7.1.0 — Surface-Abstraction & Dual-Maya Integration Program

**Date opened:** 2026-04-26
**Target Version:** 7.1.0
**Baseline Version:** 7.0.0 (Master Spec stamp confirmed 2026-04-26; baseline snapshots at `/_versions/*pre-v7.1-2026-04-26.md`)
**Source authority:** Cowork session 2026-04-26 (PG-style validation pass + dual-Maya reframing + Blake's six locked decisions on 2026-04-26)
**Program prompts:** Phase 14.0 (this pre-flight) through Phase 14.20 (final close)

### Scope summary

The v7.1.0 program integrates eight content objects into the Master Spec and rewrites five downstream GTM/Execution documents to align with the dual-Maya framing.

**Eight Master-Spec integration objects:**

1. **Principle 9** — new top-level architectural principle codifying the surface-abstraction model (added to §1 Principles).
2. **Appendix M** — Surface Catalog, registering each user-facing surface (Buyer Single-Operator Mode, Buyer Defense View, Seller KB-Authoring, Marketplace RFP-Exchange, etc.) with surface-id, console scope, abstraction tier, and entry/exit conditions.
3. **Single-Operator Mode (Buyer)** — new buyer surface for the Solo persona; collapses multi-stakeholder workflow into a one-evaluator-one-decision loop. New §13.x or §14.x section.
4. **Defense View (Buyer)** — new buyer surface for incumbent-renewal defense scenarios; reorients the evaluation pipeline around protect-the-incumbent vs. switch decisions. New §13.x or §14.x section.
5. **Solo pricing tier (Buyer side)** — new $-tier slotted between Free and $299 Starter; targets single-operator buyers running their own evaluations. Adds row to §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions, entry to §5.11 Feature Access Matrix, and limits in §39 Object Size Constraints. Authoritative content also lands in `Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md`.
6. **Marketplace-as-RFP-Exchange framing** — reframes §27 Marketplace from a one-way vendor directory into a two-sided RFP exchange surface. Affects §27 narrative, §27.8–§27.11 hardening sections, and the §48 PLG / network-effects loops that depend on it.
7. **Per-vertical eval starters** — vertical-specific evaluation templates (e.g., Fintech, Healthtech, DevTools) registered as first-class objects in the Buyer pipeline. New entity in §4, new section in §13 or §14, registry in Appendix J enums.
8. **First-30-Seconds Test** — UX/onboarding diagnostic codified into the spec; defines the observable buyer-side and seller-side criteria a new user must hit within 30 seconds of first surface load. Adds to §3 UX Standard and §49 Seller Onboarding (and the corresponding buyer onboarding section).

**Five GTM/Execution doc rewrites:**

1. `GTM/GTM_POSITIONING.md` — rewrite to dual-Maya framing.
2. `GTM/GTM_PLG_ARCHITECTURE.md` — rewrite PLG loops around Single-Operator Mode and Marketplace-as-RFP-Exchange.
3. `GTM/GTM_SALES_PLAYBOOK.md` — rewrite ICP, qualification, and demo script for dual-Maya.
4. `Build_Execution_Strategy.md` — update execution model to reflect new surfaces and Solo tier.
5. `Linear_Execution_Blueprint.md` — update milestone graph and project structure for the v7.1.0 surfaces.

### Phase 14.3 — `evaluation_owner_mode` added (closed 2026-04-26)

Workspace entity (Master Spec §4.3.1) now carries `evaluation_owner_mode` enum (`solo` / `team`). Drives Workspace surface compression per Principle 9 (§3.13). Solo mode selects the single-operator compressed surface (full surface authoring deferred to Phase 14.4); Team mode selects the multi-stakeholder surface as defined in §3.3 and §10. Plan-tier defaults are encoded on the field at create time: Free + Solo (Solo plan tier authored in Phase 14.6) default to `solo`; Starter + Growth + Scale + Enterprise default to `team`. The mode is switchable post-create with one transition guard: `team → solo` is blocked when stakeholders or guests are present on the Workspace. The literal field name and enum strings are never displayed to the user — Appendix M binds the surface metaphor and Phase 14.4 will author the user-facing copy. No surface-UI changes ship in this phase; only the engine plumbing.

**Resolved task drift.** Phase 14.3 task instructions carried a self-inconsistency between (a) the field constraint ("default `solo` for Free/Solo plan; default `team` on Starter+ plan") and (b) the §5.11 row description ("Solo Mode is the default surface for Free / Solo / Starter plans; Team Mode is the default for Growth / Scale / Enterprise") — the two groupings disagreed on whether the Buyer Starter tier defaults to Solo or Team. Resolved to the field-level constraint (Starter+ → `team` default) on three grounds: (1) the field-constraint wording is the more precise authoritative spec text; (2) "Starter+" is unambiguous and the corpus uses "+" notation consistently elsewhere (see §34.1.x and the Seller Plan Tier rows in §5.11 — "Growth+", "Scale+"); (3) authoring two contradictory defaults would be a P0 spec defect. Phase 14.4 surface authoring will codify the user-facing wording; the §5.11 Notes block in this phase encodes the resolved default explicitly so downstream phases inherit a single source of truth.

### Phase 14.4 — Method: Single-Operator Mode (closed 2026-04-26)

Master Spec §2 now treats Solo Mode as a first-class surface path. Method invariant; surface compresses. Stakeholder cohorts demoted to engine-only constructs in Solo Mode, surfaceable in Team Mode. Appendix M rows confirmed.

`Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` §2.8 (Single-Operator Mode) authored as the engine-side contract for the Solo surface: definition and scope (operator is all five cohort roles until invitation; mode is Workspace-scoped, not user-scoped); engine-vs-surface compression mapping (the 13-phase pipeline runs as the engine; the Solo surface compresses to a 4-step progress bar Setup → Define → Score → Decide whose visual / mobile / motion authoring lands in Phase 14.6 against the §2.8.2 phase-mapping table); soft phase gates (Solo: skip-with-warning emitting `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates` audit event with the unmet-gate enum list; Team: hard-block with HTTP 422 and structured remediation list; the `soft_gates_enabled` request flag is auto-applied by the server in Solo Mode and rejected on Team-mode Workspaces with new error code `phase_advancement_soft_gates_not_permitted_in_team_mode`); SLA / Pulse engine-on-surface-off split (`WorkspacePulseHealth` is computed and persisted identically in both modes; Solo surface compresses to a single deadline countdown plus a "What to do this week" three-item panel; Pulse Digest Email defaults to suppressed in Solo Mode and is opt-in via Notification Preferences); contextual one-click stakeholder invites at natural moments per a six-row mapping table (security/IT requirements → Technical Evaluator; TCO model → Functional Lead Finance; data-residency / compliance → Functional Lead Compliance or Technical Evaluator per email-domain heuristic; Phase 8 demo → SME; Phase 12 Selection Report → Exec Sponsor; Bidding-window minimum → Reviewer); cross-console isolation (mode is a Buyer-console concept; the field is excluded from Console Bridge Event payload, seller-visible API responses, Marketplace Listing serializers, and the Public Pricing API per §2.8.6); 12 numbered Acceptance Criteria covering plan-tier defaults, surface compression, soft-gate semantics, SLA / Pulse suppression, Pulse Digest Email opt-in, cohort auto-assignment, transition triggers, post-skip Team-Mode banner, cross-console firewall integrity, Appendix M row coverage, and the Phase-14.6 UI authoring contract; Cross-References block linking §3.13, §4.3.1, §4.6.1, §5.9, §8.4, §10, §13.6.2, §15, §18, §19, §20, §27, §4.7.1, §7.2, §32, §34.1.1, Appendices C / I / J / M, and the downstream Phase 14.5 / 14.6 phases.

### Phase 14.5 — Feature: Defense View (closed 2026-04-26)

Master Spec §13.11 now contains the Defense View feature spec at full Master Spec fidelity. The Defense View is the buyer-side, single-screen leadership-meeting surface that synthesizes the finalized Selection Record into Recommendation, Why (3 weighted reasons with linked evidence), Risks (1–2 with mitigation), Evidence (links back to the Selection Record), and a one-page printable PDF for the CFO. Generated server-side via Sonnet on first open and cached against `selection_record_hash`; regenerated only on hash mutation or explicit operator action. Buyer-console-only; mobile is read-only. Plan-gated: Free renders a watermarked preview; Solo+ (and Business Starter+ until Phase 14.6 lands) renders the full surface unwatermarked; Enterprise PDF additionally embeds the Selection Record audit-receipt verbiage per §32.7.

**Section-placement resolution.** §3.13 Principle 9 forward-reference and the user's Phase 14.5 brief left the section anchor ambiguous between §13.x and §14.x. The §13 Scoring section is the conceptually correct home: Defense View is the post-scoring leadership-meeting surface that consumes the immutable Selection Record (§4.3.24, §10.13.5) produced by the scoring pipeline. §17 Workspace Analytics is a metrics-and-export section, not a Selection-Record-presentation section. §14 Scenario Modeling is unrelated. Authored as **§13.11 Defense View** following §13.10 Acceptance Criteria, with §13.11 carrying its own §13.11.13 Acceptance Criteria sub-block. Stop-condition resolved: not duplicated; single home.

**`Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` §13.11 Defense View** authored as the full feature spec with the following sub-subsections: §13.11.1 Purpose; §13.11.2 Inputs & Source-of-Truth Binding (Selection Record SHA-256 hash binding; the only input is the finalized Selection Record bundle); §13.11.3 Surface (one-screen layout, four sections, one action; no navigation away from the surface); §13.11.4 Plan Gating (Free watermarked preview; Solo+ full surface; Enterprise audit-receipt footer); §13.11.5 Generation: AIOperation `defense_view_generate` (capability registration table; OutcomeContract: accepted = operator open within 90d AND `regenerated_count = 0` AND no regeneration within 24h of `generated_at`; rejected = operator-initiated regeneration within 24h; `auto_accept_after_seconds=30d`; `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds=24h`; `requires_explicit_user_signal=false`; `contest_window_days=14`; performance budget ≤ 8 s p95; caching invariant); §13.11.6 Print / Export PDF (single-page, server-side rendered, ≤ 3 s p95, Enterprise audit-receipt verbiage); §13.11.7 Data Model — `DefenseView` Entity (full field table including `id`, `org_id`, `console=buyer` invariant, `workspace_id`, `selection_record_id`, `selection_record_hash`, `recommendation_text`, `top_reasons` jsonb, `material_risks` jsonb, `cfo_summary_md`, `confidence_score`, `aioperation_id`, `generated_at`, `opened_at`, `regenerated_count`, `first_regeneration_at`, standard audit columns, soft delete;
