### Phase 14.6 — Pipeline surface compression (closed 2026-04-26)

13-phase engine renders as 4-step **Setup → Define → Score → Decide** on the Buyer console (Solo Mode) and **Receive → Draft → Review → Submit** on the Seller console in Solo Mode. Buyer Team Mode renders the full 13-phase chip ribbon (§3.3.1) unchanged. Seller console is always compressed — no Team Mode equivalent on the seller side per §2.8.6 / §3.14.4 invariant `pipeline_surface_compression_seller_always_compressed`. UX component spec authored as `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §5.2.19 PipelineSurface with three render modes: `solo-buyer`, `solo-seller`, `team`. The component composes the existing PhaseAdvancer (§5.2.16) and ToastNotification (§5.2.5) for advancement and soft-gate paths.

**Scope re-direction.** The Phase-14.5 close referred to Phase 14.6 as "Solo Pricing Tier Surfaces" (the Buyer Solo plan tier introduction in §34.1.1 + Solo-tier upgrade modal). The Phase-14.6 brief authored in this phase supersedes that scope — Phase 14.6 is now **UX Compression: 4-Step Progress Bar** specifically. The Solo plan-tier introduction (§34.1.1 entry, §5.11 `defense_view` row binding `buyer_solo` as the gate, §34.8.5 entitlement matrix update, §34.19 carry-over guarantee tier wiring, Solo-tier upgrade modal UX surface) is **deferred to a renamed Phase 14.6a (Solo Plan Tier — pricing & entitlement)**, which must precede or accompany the Solo-tier rollout in production. Until Phase 14.6a lands, the Solo gate aliases authored in Phase 14.5 (`buyer_solo` → `business_starter` alias for Defense View access) remain in force per the Phase-14.5 Authored Extension. The forward-reference row in Appendix M previously labeled "Solo Pricing Tier Surfaces (Phase 14.6)" is replaced in this phase by the canonical "Pipeline Surface Compression (§3.14, closed Phase 14.6)" row; a new forward-reference row "Solo Plan Tier — pricing & entitlement (Phase 14.6a)" is **NOT** added in this phase because the Phase-14.6a brief has not been written; the Phase-14.6a scope is captured in Open Follow-Ups below.

**Conflict surfaced and resolved — §2.8.2 step-to-phase mapping.** The Phase-14.4 close authored §2.8.2 with a provisional Buyer Solo step-to-phase mapping placing Phases 2–9 under "Define" (i.e., a four-step grouping of: Setup = 1, Define = 2–9, Score = 10–11, Decide = 12–13) and explicitly noted that the four-step UI authoring would land in Phase 14.6 (§2.8 AC #12: "any divergence between Phase 14.6 UI and §2.8 mapping is a defect against §2.8"). The Phase-14.6 brief authored here re-specifies the mapping as: Setup = 1–3, Define = 4–6, Score = 7–10, Decide = 11–13. This is operationally cleaner — the §2.8.2 placement of "vendor outreach / bidding / refinement / due diligence / Q&A" under Define collapses too much heterogeneous work under one label and obscures the Score-vs.-Define boundary. The Phase-14.6 mapping aligns each step with a coherent work-stage: Setup is foundation-building (req authoring, use case decomposition), Define is the bid-design and outreach phase, Score is the response-and-evaluate phase, Decide is the consensus-and-close phase.

**Resolution.** The Phase-14.6 mapping is the canonical contract per the §3.14.1 / §3.14.2 step-to-phase tables and the §3.14.4 invariant `pipeline_surface_compression_step_to_phase_canonical`. §2.8.2 is updated in this phase to mirror §3.14.1 verbatim; the prior placement is recorded here as superseded. Engineering and QA implement against §3.14.1 (canonical) with §2.8.2 mirroring it; any divergence is a defect against §3.14.

### Phase 14.7 — Buyer Maya Onboarding & Per-Vertical Eval Starters (closed 2026-04-27)

The "What are you evaluating?" intake flow is authored as the canonical Buyer Workspace-creation surface, backed by a new platform-scoped `EvalStarter` registry that maps each `EvalVertical` to a complete pre-population bundle (Use Cases, Requirements, scoring rubric, recommended longlist, default deadline). Selection of one of six default vertical tiles (CRM · ITSM · EDR · Observability · Payroll/HRIS · Other) materializes a Workspace pre-populated with vertical-specific seed content; nothing is locked. The "Other" path takes a 1–120-character free-text label and materializes a deliberately minimal generic Workspace. A muted "blank Workspace" affordance preserves the power-user path. UX component spec authored as `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.4.2 "What Are You Evaluating?" Intake (Phase 14.7) with two screens — Intake Screen and Post-Selection Landing Screen — and acceptance criteria IF-01 through IF-12.

**Scope re-direction (Forward-Reference Numbering Reconciliation).** The Phase 14.2 authoring of Appendix M used "Phase 14.7 Marketplace-as-RFP-Exchange" and "Phase 14.8 per-vertical eval starters" as the prospective phase labels. The Phase 14.7 brief executed in this phase (per `Integration_Prompts.md` Phase 14.7) is **Buyer Maya Onboarding & Per-Vertical Eval Starters**, which corresponds to the original Phase 14.8 scope. Marketplace-as-RFP-Exchange is rescheduled to a later Phase 14.x (number to be assigned). The Appendix M intro paragraph (M.1 opening) and the two forward-reference rows in M.1 are updated in this phase: the row previously labeled "Marketplace-as-RFP-Exchange (Phase 14.7)" is relabeled "Marketplace-as-RFP-Exchange (forthcoming)" with an explanatory note; the row previously labeled "Per-Vertical Eval Starters (Phase 14.8)" is closed and tightened to bind §13.12 / §4.5.9 / Appendix J `EvalVertical`. Historical Appendix M intro reference to Phase 14.7 / Phase 14.8 is updated in place to reflect the new ordering (intro paragraph M.1, line ~45015).

**Conflict surfaced and resolved — §35.1 Step 4 supersedence.** The §35.1 Step 4 (Buyer Onboarding Flow — First Use Case) previously authored the prompt "What are you evaluating?" with three options "Custom SaaS Evaluation / Security-First Evaluation / Compliance Evaluation" routed to the Template Gallery. Phase 14.7 authors §13.12 as the canonical Workspace-creation intake (vertical-driven, EvalStarter-seeded, materializes inline). §35.1 Step 4 is tightened in this same change to a one-line cross-reference at §13.12; the legacy three-option Template-Gallery routing is superseded. Pre-built Template Library entries remain accessible from inside the materialized Workspace per §19. The conflict is between two different framings of the same surface (template-style preset vs. vertical-driven EvalStarter); resolved in favor of the EvalStarter framing because (a) it is platform-scoped Ops-managed content (the per-Org Template Library remains for buyer-authored templates), (b) it composes vertical-specific Use Cases / Requirements / rubric / longlist / deadline in a single bundle, (c) the materialization is one transaction landing the operator on a half-built Workspace ready for editing.

**Resolution.** §13.12 is the canonical intake. §35.1 Step 4 is a thin wrapper. §19 Template Library remains the buyer-authored template surface. Engineering and QA implement against §13.12; any divergence from §13.12 in Step 4 wrapper behavior is a defect against §13.12.

**Conflict surfaced and resolved — Solo monthly/annual price wording.**

The Phase 14.9 prompt cites Solo pricing as "$49/mo (annual: $39/mo) OR $199/eval one-time" (and identical "$199/bid" on the seller side). The v3 Buyer / Seller Pricing Strategy docs (both dated 2026-04-26, the most recent pricing-doc version) cite Solo pricing as "$49/mo annual / $59/mo monthly OR $199/eval-or-bid". These are different by ~20% on the monthly billing path — the prompt asks for $49 monthly with a $39 annual discount; the v3 docs author $49 annual with a $59 monthly premium.

Resolution: per the source-of-truth hierarchy in `CLAUDE.md` §2 — **`Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` and `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md` are authoritative for pricing**. The v3 docs' $49 annual / $59 monthly pricing was authored as the partial Phase 14.9 work (the v3 changeset header explicitly notes "Phase 14.9 — Master Spec scaffolding edit pending") and remains the active pricing decision. The Phase 14.9 prompt's "$49/mo (annual: $39/mo)" wording predates the v3 doc decisions and is treated as a stale instruction. Master Spec §34.2.1 / §34.2.2 are authored with the v3 numbers ($49 annual / $59 monthly / $199 per-eval-or-bid). If the prompt's $49 / $39 / $199 pricing represents a deliberate re-pricing intent (Buyer Maya / Seller Maya more aggressive on-ramp), the user MUST author a Phase 14.9.x re-pricing brief; this Phase 14.9 close honors v3.

**Conflict surfaced and resolved — Master Summary §2.5 cross-side billing pooling.**

The Phase 14.9 prompt's stop condition references potential conflict with "Master Summary §2.5" cross-side billing pooling logic for Solo. The Master Summary is retired (`_versions/Sourcera_Master_Summary_v1.1_retired_2026-04-26.md`, dated 2026-04-26) and was retired explicitly because v7.0.0 absorbed its content into the Master Spec. The active cross-side billing pooling logic lives at Master Spec §34.10.3 (Pooled Budget Across Consoles) and §34.12 (Cross-Side Billing Rules). Phase 14.9 extends §34.10.3 with the Solo-co-resident pool rule (Solo's engine-absorbed envelope is never customer-visible and never pools with the contralateral console's wallet) and §34.12 with §34.12.6 (Solo-Tier Per-Console Subscription Billing, authoritative). No conflict with the retired Master Summary; the existing Free + Free / Free + Paid collapse rules generalize to Solo cleanly because Solo's envelope is engine-side (never visible) and therefore never pools by construction.

**Conflicts resolved.**

1. **V11 §M.4.4.2 predicate set vs P0 #5 recommendation vocabulary.** Pre-remediation §M.4.4.2 (V11) enumerated four predicates (surface-section reachability / plan-gating reachability / public-API reachability / serializer reachability). The P0 #5 recommendation specifies four predicates with different framing (console enum / RBAC reachable / plan-tier reachable / surface-class non-internal). Resolution: rewrite §M.4.4.2 to use the P0 #5 vocabulary verbatim; preserve the V11 predicate coverage by folding each V11 predicate into one of the four P0 predicates as a sub-check. The §M.4.4.2.H V11-to-v7.2.0-REM coverage map confirms strict subsumption (the v7.2.0-REM predicate set absorbs every V11 sub-check). No V11-detected leak class can pass the v7.2.0-REM check; coverage is non-decreasing. Net effect: the rewrite is a refinement, not a reduction.
2. **Spec-side error-code catalog convention (Appendix I HTTP-only vs CI-gate-internal).** Pre-remediation Appendix I had two sub-sections for non-HTTP codes (`Internal Integrity Events`, `Polling Payload Flags`). The new failure-mode codes for the spec-lint CI gate (override-rejection paths) follow the same non-HTTP shape but are conceptually distinct (CI-gate emit-path records, not observability events or polling flags). Resolution: author a NEW sub-section "Spec-Lint CI Gate Internal Failure Modes (Non-HTTP)" with 11 rows, distinct shape (Code | Source gate | Trigger | Resolution path | Authority anchor) versus the existing two non-HTTP sub-sections. CI gate `appendix_i_internal_event_no_http_status` (§M.5) is extended to assert no row in the new sub-section carries an HTTP status column.
3. **AE numbering collision.** The new AE row was initially numbered AE-V72REM-02 in the spec body, but AE-V72REM-02 is already assigned to the D-AK-003 closure (`brand_voice_guide_v1` Glossary entry). Resolution: renumber to AE-V72REM-09 (the next available number after AE-V72REM-08); update the Master Spec body references and append the row to the v7.2.0-REM ledger registry.

**Counterfactual coverage (verification against the §M.4.4 attack surface).** The v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 hardening MUST fail on each of the following adversarial inputs:

1. **Orphan annotation.** A PR with a no-op spec edit (typo fix, comment-only change) carries an override annotation for `customer_visible_field_xyz`. §M.4.4.2.A rejects with `override_target_not_flagged_by_detector` because the detector flagged zero concepts in the diff. (This closes the residual D-11.2-004 attack: V11's predicate-only check could not catch an orphan annotation if the concept name did not match any predicate's spec-section reach.)
2. **Typo'd concept name.** A PR introducing engine concept `solo_envelope_throttle_threshold_value_cents` with an override annotation for `solo_envelope_throttle_threshold` (typo: missing `_value_cents`). §M.4.4.2.A rejects because the annotation's concept_name does not exactly match the detected concept's name. The rejection comment surfaces the near-match suggestion.
3. **Prefix-substring near-match.** A PR introducing engine concept `kb_export_archive_integrity_check_aux` with an override annotation for `kb_export_archive_integrity_check`. The exact ASCII match rule rejects the join (substring matching is not permitted).
4. **Customer-surface field disguised as internal.** A PR introducing an entity field `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode_seller_visible_override` with an override annotation claiming internal-only. §M.4.4.2.B Predicate 1 sub-check 1 fails (the field is named in §22.20 Seller Maya Polish surface section); §M.4.4.2.A passes (the detector did flag the field), but the customer-surface-reachability rejection takes effect with status `override_target_customer_visible`.
5. **Plan-gated field disguised as internal.** A PR introducing a `CapabilityRegistryEntry.surface_throttling_class` value cited in §34.1.3 plan-tier cell with override annotation. §M.4.4.2.D Predicate 3 sub-check 1 fails (the field is in §34.1.3).
6. **RBAC-bound capability disguised as internal.** A PR introducing a `capability_id` cited in §5.11 Feature Access Matrix with override annotation. §M.4.4.2.C Predicate 2 sub-check 1 fails.
7. **Default-deny on missing attestation.** A PR introducing an entity field with override annotation but NO matching internal-only allowlist entry, NO Ops-Console-exclusive surface, NO attestation paragraph, and NO serializer-redaction lock. §M.4.4.2.E Predicate 4 default-deny posture fails (no affirmative internal-only attestation found).
8. **Unknown gate in `@ci-gate-override:`.** A PR carrying `@ci-gate-override: appendix_m_coverage_on_diff_typo — rationale ≥ 60 chars stuff stuff stuff stuff stuff stuff stuff stuff stuff stuff stuff`. §M.4.4.5 ¶2 rejects with `override_unknown_gate`; closest-match suggestion `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` surfaced.
9. **Rationale < 60 chars.** A PR carrying `@ci-gate-override: solo_tier_numeric_single_source — short rationale`. §M.4.4.5 ¶1 rejects with `override_rationale_too_short` (measured 18 chars after prefix-strip).
10. **`coupled_with:` references nonexistent gate.** A PR carrying a §M.5 catalog row whose `override_path` cell declares `coupled_with:s3_replication_policy_nonexistent_sibling`. The `appendix_m5_self_consistency` meta-gate rejects at boot with `override_coupled_gate_unknown`; merge blocked.

All ten adversarial inputs are covered. The v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 hardening closes D-11.2-004's residual attack surface beyond the V11 protection.

**Self-challenge pass (Opus-mandatory).** Hostile staff-engineer review of the authored §M.4.4.2 rewrite:

- **Q: Could a PR get the override accepted by submitting a syntactically valid annotation for a concept that doesn't appear in the diff?** A: No. §M.4.4.2.A detector-flag pre-merge cross-validation rejects with `override_target_not_flagged_by_detector`.
- **Q: Could a PR introduce a customer-visible field with a syntactically valid override and a substring-match concept_name?** A: No. The exact ASCII match rule in §M.4.4.2.A rejects substring matches; even if the concept_name match passes, §M.4.4.2.B–§M.4.4.2.E enforce the customer-surface-reachability invariant.
- **Q: Could a PR weaken the §M.4.4.2.E Predicate 4 default-deny posture by adding an attestation paragraph that doesn't match the regex?** A: No. The regex is anchored on the canonical phrase `**Internal-only construct.** {concept_name} is an internal {kind} that is never serialized to any customer console`; partial-match attestations are rejected.
- **Q: Could a PR exploit the `appendix_m5_self_consistency` meta-gate gap by adding a §M.5 row that points to a coupled gate authored in the SAME PR (so both rows resolve at gate boot)?** A: Yes — but this is by design; the meta-gate runs after the §M.4.2 trigger detector emits the post-edit parse tree, so SAME-PR-authored coupled gates resolve symmetrically. This is the expected behavior.
- **Q: Does the rewrite preserve V11's protection of `Workspace.solo_envelope_throttle_threshold_value_cents` (the D-11.2-004 attack target)?** A: Yes. §M.4.4.2.D Predicate 3 sub-check 5 (any §44 envelope or rate-card cell bound to a plan tier) catches the field; §M.4.4.2.A detector-flag pre-merge cross-validation catches any orphan-annotation variant of the attack; §M.4.4.2.E Predicate 4 default-deny posture catches any attempt to falsely attest internal-only.

QA-acceptance review: every acceptance criterion in §M.4.4.2 is observable (line-counts, regex matches, predicate evaluations), measurable (binary pass/fail per gate; outcome enum per cross-validation result), and scope-bound (per-PR, per-annotation, per-concept tuple).

Junior-engineer buildability review: the §M.4.4.2 rewrite enumerates four predicates with sub-checks in numbered form; each sub-check names the spec sections and the regex / heuristic to apply. The §M.4.4.2.A detector-flag check is a join operation with named matching rules. A junior engineer can wire the detector against `tools/spec-lint/cross_validation.ts` (which carries the canonical TypeScript implementation) without ambiguity.

The `surface_tone_calibration` slot payload is edited at the canonical storage location; this Glossary entry's body is unchanged. Verified: the entry declares the slot key set as stable but the row values as Marketing-owned payload.
3. **Prohibited-term registry expansion.** Legal / Marketing add new prohibited-content classes to §48.4.4 (e.g., "embargoed-jurisdiction references" / "unattested benchmark claims"). The `prohibited_term_registry_ref` slot is a pointer to §48.4.4; expansion propagates via the §48.4.4 registry edit (a separate authoring pass with its own Authoring Convention #3 enum-registration discipline). Verified: the entry declares the slot as a cross-reference, not an inline restatement, and the rewritten body explicitly forbids inline restatement of §48.4.4 content.

A fourth, OUT-OF-SCOPE-for-Counterfactual-#1 amendment class exists: schema- / ownership- / version-axis- / storage- / validator-contract-identity changes (e.g., adding a sixth schema slot; bumping `v1` → `v2`; switching the prohibited-term registry source from §48.4.4 to a new external service). The entry's body explicitly distinguishes the in-scope (no amendment) and out-of-scope (amendment required) classes.

**Conflicts resolved.** Two source-vs-source consistency notes: (1) The pre-rewrite (Phase 2V) entry body stated tonal-axis values + per-surface tone-calibration values inline; the Prompt 2.2 rewrite removes these inline values per Counterfactual #1. **Self-challenge findings.** Re-read the rewritten entry as a hostile staff engineer. Three findings — none blocking the closure:
1. **Storage-location ambiguity (P3 cosmetic, v7.1.x).** The canonical storage location declares both a target entity (`marketing_content_artifact` Ops-Console table) and an interim file (`assets/brandguidelines/brand_voice_guide_v1.json`) with the table marked as "v7.1.x Marketing-Content backlog". Logged for the v7.1.x mechanical-hygiene backlog as a potential `marketing_content_artifact_slug_canonicality` CI gate authoring item.
2. **Schema-version axis future-amendment overhead (P3 cosmetic, v7.1.x).** The body declares `v1` retirement only when no in-flight AC binds to it. A hostile reviewer could argue this is a circular definition (the AC binds the version axis, the version axis governs the AC). Mitigation: the standard Appendix K retirement convention applies (sibling entries permitted, transitional concurrency, deprecation marker). No spec-level action owed.
3. **Editorial-rubric recursion-guard wording (P3 cosmetic, v7.1.x).** The body states payload edits route through the §48.6.2 RUBRIC v1.0 editorial workflow with a "recursive-rubric guard" (a payload edit cannot reduce R6 enforcement strictness without a separate Authored Extension amendment). The recursion-guard is correctly named but the mechanics of "reduce R6 enforcement strictness" are not enumerated. Mitigation: the Authored Extension amendment requirement is the structural enforcement; a future v7.1.x discipline pass MAY enumerate specific strictness-reduction patterns (e.g., loosening a prohibited-content class; widening a tonal-axis tolerance). Logged for the v7.1.x mechanical-hygiene backlog.

All three findings are P3 cosmetic; none touch the Counterfactual #1 invariant or the R6 validator binding contract. The Prompt 2.2 closure is sign-off-ready.

**Conflicts resolved.**

1. **§34.8.5 canonical-form lock note vs §21.4 registry seed.** The pre-Phase-4 lock note referenced `qa_suggestion_buyer` as a runtime-bindable capability "under §17.x Managed Agents" without any §21.4 registry row. Resolved per the source-of-truth hierarchy (Master Spec wins; §17 is Buyer Analytics per the actual §17 heading text, NOT Managed Agents — the canonical-form lock's "§17.x" pointer was stale). The buyer-side Q&A spec home is §18.4 (Agent Q&A Suggestion (Buyer-Side)); the seller-side is §24 (Seller Console Q&A). Both are now bound to first-class §21.4.1.B registry rows.
2. **§4.8.2 AC #1 immutability vs in-place supersession of the v6.0.0 `qa_suggestion` row.** AC #1 reads "`capability_id` MUST be immutable once any AIOperation has referenced it" with no general-purpose exception path. Resolved by the narrowest possible exception interpretation: the storage-layer `id` UUID (the true row-identity carrier under Convex schema) is preserved across supersession; only the human-readable `capability_id` string changes; the legacy string survives as a `CapabilityRegistryEntry.aliases` array element; alias-rewrite at read time per §4.8.1 alias-projection rule ensures historical AIOperation references resolve without migration. The interpretation is registered in AE-V72REM-PH4-01 and requires Pricing Owner + Engineering Lead dual-signoff at v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp.
3. **OutcomeContract FK ownership across the supersession.** The pre-Phase-4 single-row `qa_suggestion` `outcome_contract_id` FK points to the OutcomeContract row that has settled v6.0.0–v7.1.0 seller-side operations. The seller-side sibling preserves this FK in-place (no new OutcomeContract row created on the seller side); the buyer-side sibling is assigned a NEW `outcome_contract_id` FK (new row authored in §34.15.1 against the §21.4.5 buyer-side signal contract). The cross-validator `qa_suggestion_family_outcome_contract_isolation` (§M.5.14) asserts FK independence at deploy time. Resolved without revenue-leakage risk: in-flight v6 OutcomeContract settlement is unaffected by the supersession.
4. **PostHog event-name historical-series continuity.** The pre-Phase-4 PostHog event was `agent.qa_suggestion.invoked` (single event for seller-side operations only). Post-Phase-4, the legacy event name is registered as a deprecated alias of `agent.qa_suggestion_seller.invoked` at PostHog ingestion time; analytics dashboards consuming the legacy event preserve their historical series. The new buyer-side event `agent.qa_suggestion_buyer.invoked` has no v6 history and begins emitting at v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp.

**Conflicts resolved.**

1. **§34.3.4 illustrative rate card vs §4.8.2-default multipliers.** The §34.3.4 published `cost_price` values (e.g., `$0.05` for `requirement_extraction` at cost_base `$0.04` implies `cost_multiplier=1.250`, not the default `1.050`) diverge from the §4.8.2 default multipliers `(value_multiplier=10.000, cost_multiplier=1.050)`. Resolved by per-row `cost_multiplier` overrides on each new §21.4.1.C / §21.4.1.D row, with the override pattern registered in AE-V72REM-PH4.2-01 as the v7.1.0a stamp-minimum-blast-radius option. Alternative options (reconcile §34.3.4 to formula-derived values — lowers customer-facing rate card; or author `default_cost_multiplier_per_model_tier` registry feature — larger scope) are documented in the AE row as rejected at v7.1.0a stamp for narrowness reasons.
2. **D-EM-002 named scope (7 buyer-side capabilities) vs counterfactual-pass discovery (kb_suggestion_seller orphan).** The §34.8.5 line 29817 `kb_suggestion_seller` row is a seller-side matrix row that would remain orphaned if Phase 4.2 only authored the seven buyer-side rows in the named scope. The Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure registered the `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` CI gate that would fail-closed on this orphan at first deploy-validator run. Resolved by expanding scope to author the full `kb_suggestion` family-rooted sibling-split (rollup root + 2 siblings) in §21.4.1.D, with the scope expansion explicitly registered as an Authored-Extension counterfactual-pass finding in AE-V72REM-PH4.2-01.
3. **§34.3.4 single-row `kb_suggestion` (Cross-console) vs §34.8.5 dual-sibling rows.** D-EM-013 P1 documents this rate-card cardinality drift. Resolved at the registry layer in this Phase 4.2 closure (the §21.4.1.D Rows 2 + 3 authoritatively replace the single-row §34.3.4 reference). Superseding 2026-06-23 note: the Phase EM Entitlement Matrix P1 pass closed the remaining §34.3.4 prose-narrative split by publishing `kb_suggestion_buyer` and `kb_suggestion_seller` rows and making legacy `kb_suggestion` alias-only.
4. **`scenario_modeling` is `active_workflow` despite the §34.1.1 "Engine-absorbed envelope" cell narrative.** Per §44.6.3 the Solo-tier engine-absorbed envelope is the **default** Solo treatment for every customer-billed capability; per §44.6.4 the silent-throttling engine evaluates `surface_throttling_class` to determine eligibility — `active_workflow` capabilities are NEVER throttled. The two mechanisms are not in conflict: scenario_modeling on Buyer Solo is paid out of the engine-side margin envelope (per §44.6.3) AND is never silently throttled (because §44.6.4.1 holds `active_workflow` rows immune from throttling regardless of envelope state). The §21.4.1.C Row 6 `scenario_modeling.surface_throttling_class=active_workflow` is correct and the §34.1.1 cell narrative is non-contradictory. Resolved without spec edit beyond §21.4.1.C Row 6 explanatory annotation.
5. **§4.8.2 AC #1 immutability vs new `capability_id` strings that have prior in-flight AIOperation references.** The seven `capability_id` strings have been written to AIOperation rows since v7.0.0 stamp (per the D-EM-002 evidence — `ctx.db.capabilityRegistryEntry(capabilityId)` returns null but the AIOperation `capability_id` field was nonetheless populated). Per §4.8.2 AC #1, `capability_id` MUST be immutable once any AIOperation has referenced it. Resolved: the new `id` UUIDs for the §21.4.1.C / §21.4.1.D rows are NEW; the `capability_id` STRING for each row is preserved from its pre-v7.1.0a usage (no string change); the binding from string → UUID is a forward-binding, not a string mutation; the §4.8.1 alias-projection rule resolves prior-stamp AIOperation rows at read time without a destructive migration. The AC #1 invariant is preserved.

**Conflicts resolved.**

1. **`vendor_page_enrichment_polling` `billing_mode` classification (`customer_billed` vs `sourcera_owned`).** Per D-EM-004 resolution prescription: "decide `billing_mode` per surface (likely `customer_billed` for the suggestion surfaces, `sourcera_owned` for the polling job — Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff per §44.6.4.1)". **Resolution:** `sourcera_owned`. Rationale: the row is a Sourcera-initiated passive enrichment-staleness scan, not a customer-invoked action; saddling the seller with unexpected wallet draws on a Sourcera-initiated polling action is contrary to the §44.6.4 surface contract. Per Source-of-Truth Hierarchy §15 + CLAUDE.md §13 rule 3 (Surface conflicts explicitly), surfaced explicitly here. The §34.8.5 row consequently lands in the Platform-owned block with `enforcement_mode=n/a (sourcera_owned)` rather than `hard` — D-EM-004's "Author three corresponding §34.8.5 matrix rows with `enforcement_mode=hard`" prescription is honored for Rows 1 and 2 only; Row 3 follows the v7.0.0 §34.8.5 Platform-owned-block convention because the customer-facing enforcement contract does not apply to `sourcera_owned` capabilities (which are not customer-invokable).
2. **§21.4.6 vs §21.4.2 vs §21.4.3 landing-site selection.** D-EM-004 prescription enumerated both `§21.4.2 (Extended Capabilities) or a new §21.4.6 sub-section "Solo Throttling Membership"`. **Resolution:** new §21.4.6 sub-section. Rationale documented in §21.4.6 "Authoring intent" paragraph: (a) the three rows share a single binding contract (the closed-set Solo throttling membership mutation-guarded by §44.6.4.1's Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff rule); (b) v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.X precedent registers per-closure-batch sub-sections at full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity; (c) closed-set integrity is a first-class invariant — separating the set into a single named sub-section makes the integrity-asserting deploy-time validator trivially bindable to the §21.4.6 table contents. The companion §21.4.3 entry for `vendor_page_enrichment_polling` is preserved cross-referentially.
3. **`state` promotion `alpha → active` without 30-day-in-beta minimum.** §4.8.2 state-machine standard path requires "30 days in beta minimum" for `beta → active`. **Resolution:** waived under v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp-gate exception per AE-V72REM-PH4.4-01 (mirrors §21.4.1.B / §21.4.1.C / §21.4.1.E precedent). Rationale: the three capabilities have been engine-invokable in production since v7.1.0 stamp; the missing registry rows are the structural defect that prevents the §44.6.4 silent-throttling engine from resolving the capability_ids at the §34.8.2 runtime path, not the capability-lifecycle position. AE-V72REM-PH4.4-01 binds the state-machine exception clause; Engineering Lead + Ops Lead dual-signoff at this ratification covers it.

The check inspects the alias-rewrite resolver's routing table at deploy time, NOT the live PostHog event stream; the routing-table inspection is a Convex-internal query with no PostHog dependency. **Conflicts resolved.**

1. **Two Appendix J enums purporting to register the same `legal_entity` concept (body-side L48027–48036 vs envelope-side L49594–49598).** Per Source-of-Truth Hierarchy §2 + CLAUDE.md §13 rule 3, the post-D-AJ-004 envelope-side `legal_entity_kind` enum (line 49596) carries the canonical 4-value set per the Phase 2V remediation note's explicit retirement of `sourcera_uk_ltd` + addition of `sourcera_custom`. The body-side enum is reconciled to match the envelope-side, NOT the inverse — the Phase 2V remediation note is the authoritative resolution. Both enums now declare the same 4-value membership; CI gate `legal_entity_enum_canonical_consistency` asserts the invariant at deploy time.
2. **§4.8.1 mapping table line 8253 (`uk → sourcera_uk_ltd`) vs Appendix J post-D-AJ-005 `uk` retirement.** Per the Phase 2V D-AJ-005 retirement note's explicit instruction that `uk` is "handled per §4.8.1 Org-side residency configuration", v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 closes the §4.8.1 mapping-table propagation by removing the `uk` row and adding the `custom` row (the canonical post-D-AJ-005 + post-D-RES-004 4-row mapping). UK-resident Orgs route through `sourcera_eu_gmbh` (default) or `sourcera_custom` (UK-sovereign-cloud Enterprise) — both paths documented in §4.8.1 + Glossary + §34.10.5.A.

**Self-Challenge Pass (Opus-mandatory per Convention #15).**

- **Q1: Does the canonical 4-row mapping break any existing AIOperation / AIWallet / MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows in production?** No. The pre-Phase-5 4-row mapping (`us`/`eu`/`apac`/`uk`) is replaced by the post-Phase-5 4-row mapping (`us`/`eu`/`apac`/`custom`); existing rows with `legal_entity ∈ {sourcera_us_llc, sourcera_eu_gmbh, sourcera_apac_pte}` continue to validate against the post-Phase-5 enum; existing rows with `legal_entity = sourcera_uk_ltd` are preserved verbatim under §4.8.1 Settlement Freeze + §40.2 7-year retention (the historical-row migration backstop paragraph documents the preservation rule); new writes against `sourcera_uk_ltd` are rejected at the Convex schema-validation layer. The §M.5.17 sub-assertion (e) explicitly tests the historical-row read-fidelity invariant.
- **Q2: Does the `custom → sourcera_custom` mapping correctly handle multiple `custom`-residency Orgs with different `custom_sovereign_residency_label` values?** Yes. The §34.10.5.A invariant #5 documents the keying: Stripe Customer keyed on `(org_id, sourcera_custom)` with `metadata.custom_sovereign_residency_label = <Organization.custom_sovereign_residency_label>` carrying the Org-specific sub-classification. The `(org_id, legal_entity)` unique index is sufficient because `org_id` is itself unique; multiple `custom`-residency Orgs each receive their own Stripe Customer disambiguated by `org_id`, with the sub-classification carried in metadata.
- **Q3: Does the §34.10.5.A 5-step atomic transaction correctly serialize concurrent residency-change attempts on the same Org?** Yes. The transaction acquires a row-level lock on the Organization row before step (i); a second concurrent residency-change attempt waits for the lock and re-validates eligibility predicates against post-transaction state. The §M.5.17 sub-assertion (b) tests 10 concurrent-attempt scenarios; failure rate must be 0%.
- **Q4: Does the Outcome Resolver legacy-routing rule correctly handle an AIOperation written pre-cutover but settled post-cutover?** Yes. The §34.10.5.A invariant #4 + AC #4 + §M.5.17 sub-assertion (d) document the rule: the AIOperation's `legal_entity` field (snapshot at write time) is the canonical Stripe-Customer-routing key, NOT the Organization's current `legal_entity_active`; the Resolver looks up the matching Stripe Customer via `Organization.stripe_customer_id_historical[]` when settling an AIOperation whose `legal_entity` does not match the current `legal_entity_active`.
- **Q5: Does the §34.10.5.A invariant #6 Ops-Finance correction path correctly handle the v7.1.0a one-time UK-Ltd migration?** Yes. The correction follows the same 5-step transaction as invariant #3 but with `R_old = R_new` (residency unchanged) and `correction_reason = legacy_uk_ltd_to_eu_gmbh`. The correction does NOT close the legacy Customer until the legacy Customer's outstanding invoices reach `paid` or `voided` terminal state — preserving §4.8.1 FX-Locking semantics for in-flight settlements.
- **Q6: Could a junior engineer build against the §34.10.5.A protocol unambiguously?** Yes. The protocol has 8 numbered invariants + 8 acceptance criteria + 7 cross-reference links; each invariant cites Convex / Stripe API mechanics by name; the §M.5.17 gate enumerates 6 sub-assertions with named test paths; the AC #4 integration test is named at the path `tests/integration/legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test.spec.ts`.
- **Q7: Does the closure preserve the §51 envelope-facing analytics dashboard binding?** Yes. The `legal_entity_kind` envelope-side enum (line 49596) was already at the canonical post-D-AJ-004 4-value set per the Phase 2V remediation note; v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 reconciles the body-side to match. Finance reconciliation joins (Stripe invoice → §51 dashboard panel via `legal_entity_kind` → §4.8.1 / §4.8.3 / §4.8.12 `legal_entity`) now resolve cleanly across all four canonical values without alias drift. CI gate `legal_entity_enum_canonical_consistency` asserts the deploy-time invariant.

**Counterfactual Pass (Opus-mandatory per Convention #16).**

- **Failure mode 1 — `custom`-residency Org AC #14 fail-closed (pre-Phase-5 regression).** Pre-Phase-5, the 4-row mapping (`us`/`eu`/`apac`/`uk`) had no `custom` target; an AC #14 deterministic-mapping check on a `custom`-residency Org's AIOperation write would fail with `ai_operation_legal_entity_residency_mismatch` HTTP 422 — effectively blocking the entire `custom`-residency Enterprise / sovereign-cloud cohort from billing. Post-Phase-5, the mapping function is total + surjective; the legitimate `custom` cohort writes succeed under `legal_entity = sourcera_custom`. The §M.5.17 sub-assertion (f) fires 10 synthetic `custom`-residency Org-creation scenarios and asserts all 10 succeed with the correct Stripe Customer metadata.
- **Failure mode 2 — EU→US residency change creating dual active Stripe Customers.** Pre-Phase-5, the §34.10.5 one-liner ("Stripe customer is bound 1:1 to `(org_id, legal_entity)`; an Org changing residency triggers a new Stripe Customer creation") was silent on the atomicity / closure / legacy-invoice-fidelity / Outcome-Resolver-routing rules. A faulty implementation could create the new Customer without closing the legacy one, leaving the Org with two active Customers and two parallel invoice streams. Post-Phase-5, the §34.10.5.A 5-step atomic Convex transaction enforces the closure (step iv updates `stripe_customer_id_active` to the new Customer + appends the legacy Customer to `stripe_customer_id_historical[]`); the `(org_id, legal_entity)` unique index rejects a second active Customer attempt with HTTP 422 `stripe_customer_active_duplicate`. The §M.5.17 sub-assertion (c) tests 10 duplicate-Customer attempts; all 10 must be rejected.
- **Failure mode 3 — Stripe Charge race against residency-lock binding.** Pre-Phase-5, the timing of the residency-change cutover vs. an in-flight AIOperation's settlement was undefined; a Charge could route to the new Customer despite the AIOperation having locked its `legal_entity` and `fx_rate_locked` against the legacy Customer's billing context. Post-Phase-5, the §34.10.5.A invariant #4 documents the rule: the AIOperation's `legal_entity` field is the canonical routing key; the Outcome Resolver consults `stripe_customer_id_historical[]` when settling an AIOperation whose `legal_entity` does not match the current `legal_entity_active`. The §M.5.17 sub-assertion (d) fires 50 synthetic pre-cutover-write / post-cutover-settle AIOperations and asserts correct legacy-Customer routing.
- **Failure mode 4 — Historical `sourcera_uk_ltd` row mutation by post-Phase-5 migration code.** Pre-Phase-5, a naive migration could attempt to mutate the `legal_entity` field on historical `sourcera_uk_ltd` AIOperation rows to align with the post-Phase-5 canonical enum (e.g., rewrite to `sourcera_eu_gmbh`). Post-Phase-5, the §4.8.1 Settlement Freeze + §40.2 7-year retention preservation + §M.5.17 sub-assertion (e) collectively reject such mutations: the Settlement Freeze + `ai_operation_immutable_after_settlement` HTTP 422 fires; the Convex schema validator preserves historical `sourcera_uk_ltd` rows as readable; new writes against the legacy value are rejected. The historical-row migration backstop paragraph in §4.8.1 documents the invariant; the §M.5.17 sub-assertion (e) tests 25 legacy-row mutation attempts (all rejected) + 25 post-Phase-5 writes (all rejected).

**Defect.** D-AE-016 (P2, consistency_drift). **Surfaced:** `_audit/PHASE7_REM_VERIFY.md` Finding F2 (2026-06-13 Phase 7 re-verification). **AE row:** AE-V72REM-PH7R-01 (`_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` v7.2.0-REM registry). **Executed:** 2026-06-13, **before** the canonical Phase 8 cluster ratification pass (all cluster rows verified still `pending`).

**Problem.** The canonical program definition (`_integration/v7.2.0-Remediation_Prompts.md`) defines **one** Phase 7 (Prompts 7.1 / 7.2 / 7.3 = `AE_RATIFICATION_RECOMMENDATIONS.md §2.1 / §2.2 / §2.3`), reserves **Phase 8** for the 1V/2V/3V/3V+/6R/V7/V8.4/V9/10V **cluster ratification** (Prompts 8.1 / 8.2), and **Phase 9** for V11/V12/V13 + AE-14.18.1 unblock. The corpus previously surfaced the *wave-order inversion* (Phase 8.2 block "Conflicts resolved" #4) and the *Phase-9 forward-projection correction* (#3) but not this **prompts-vs-execution phase-number collision**.

**Resolution authority.** (1) CLAUDE.md §2 Source-of-Truth Hierarchy — the canonical program definition (`v7.2.0-Remediation_Prompts.md`) wins; the execution log conforms. **Resolution method — non-destructive crosswalk.** Headers are **NOT renamed.** Dozens of bare-name cross-references cite the closure blocks by their exact "Phase 8 — … Phase 12.x DEF Reconciliation" / "Phase 8.2 — … Phase 14.x Cluster" titles (AE ledger row bodies; Phase 7 Verification block cross-refs at L12137–12139); renaming would strand them — the same hazard CLAUDE.md §16 flags for canonical-file renames ("historical log entries are not retroactively updated"). The collision is resolved by an authoritative crosswalk plus redirect annotations at every collision point.

## v7.2.0-REM Program → Phase 12 — Cross-Phase Programs → enum (PROD-402) — Batch 1 + Course Correction (2026-06-15)

**Context.** "Walk them all" directive: execute all 25 `§3.2` cross-phase programs in dependency order per `_integration/v7.2.0-REM_CrossPhase_Walk_Plan.md`. Program 1 = enum. Pre-edit Master Spec backup at `_versions/Sourcera_Master_Spec.v7.1.0a-pre-v72REM-Phase12-walk-2026-06-15.md` (6,506,716 bytes; md5 `899858e70feff2279a97166e7dee3c08`; 53,669 lines).

**What happened (full transparency).** Batch 1 targeted the additive-registration subset of the `D-AJ-*` cluster (D-AJ-001/-002/-007/-008/-009/-010/-011). The pre-authoring existence check used `^### \`<enum>\`` / `^**\`<enum>\` enum` grep patterns and concluded the seven enums were absent from Appendix J; on that basis a "v7.2.0-REM Phase 12 enum Batch 1" registration block plus four inline-citation rewrites were authored. **Self-challenge verification then caught a duplicate-occurrence signal** (each `D-AJ` id appears at two line-starts in `DEFECT_LEDGER.md`). Reading the second occurrence — the supplementary "Tier 2 — P1 Remediations Landed" table (L868–887) — revealed all seven were already `remediated 2026-05-03` via the **"Phase 2V Audit-Remediation Enum Registrations" section (Master Spec Appendix J, L50627)**, which the grep MISSED because Phase 2V uses `#### \`name\` (… — D-AJ-NNN)` headings, not the `###`/`**` forms searched. The seven enums were therefore already registered; **Batch 1 was a duplicate-registration error, and for `defense_view_lifecycle_state`, `regeneration_reason_code`, `solo_charge_workspace_state`, and `capability_declaration_origin` the Batch-1 values CONFLICTED with the canonical Phase-2V values.**

**Resolution.** (1) Master Spec fully reverted to the pre-edit backup — restored md5 `899858e70feff2279a97166e7dee3c08` (bit-identical; Batch-1 block removed, Phase 2V registrations intact, four inline brace-literals restored). (2) The true condition is a **D-CONS-001 canonical-lag**: the supplementary Tier-2 table correctly carried `remediated 2026-05-03` but the canonical rows (`DEFECT_LEDGER.md` L269–279) still read `open`. Having confirmed closure by reading the Phase-2V spec section, the seven canonical rows were propagated `open → remediated 2026-05-03` with explicit D-CONS-001 provenance and a note that the same-session Batch-1 duplicate was reverted. **Net Master Spec delta this pass: zero. Net ledger delta: 7 canonical-lag propagations (legitimate D-CONS-001 work).**

**New findings surfaced (to be filed as canonical `D-V72REM-PH12-NNN` rows in the next pass).**
- **F-PH12-01 (enum↔state_machine consistency_drift, P2).** Phase-2V `defense_view_lifecycle_state` = {`generated_unopened`, `regenerated_unopened`, `viewed`, `viewed_archived`} but D-AJ-001's source (Appendix L.7 / §13.11.7) quoted {`generated_unopened`, `opened`, `regenerated_unopened`, `archived`}. Value-parity between the Appendix J registration and the Appendix L.7 state machine must be verified — one is stale. (Routes to Program 3 state_machine / Program 25 consistency_drift.)
- **F-PH12-02 (consistency_drift, P2).** Phase-2V `regeneration_reason_code` = {`source_change`, `operator_initiated`, `failure_recovery_retry`, `ops_force_regenerate`}; §13.11 webhook/AC prose and D-AJ-002 referenced a different vocabulary ({`source_record_hash_changed`, `manual_user_request`, …}). Verify the §13.11 body and `defense_view.regenerated` payload cite the registered values.
- **F-PH12-03 (inline-literal residual; documentation_gap, P3).** Phase-2V notes claim "Closes the inline literal at §44.6.5 / §50.4.1 / §27.4 / §34.2.5," but the inline `∈ {…}` restatements remain at Master Spec L4916, L4922, L7701, L34524 (and §34.2.5). The registrations landed; the inline-citation hygiene did not. This is the genuine residual of the D-AJ-007/-009/-010/-011 closures — to be done as the enum-program inline-hygiene micro-batch citing the canonical Phase-2V enums (NOT the Batch-1 values).

**Process correction (binds the rest of the walk).** Walk Plan §3 step 1 is hardened: before authoring ANY registration, grep the spec body for an existing registration in ALL heading formats (`#### \`name\``, `### \`name\``, `**\`name\``, and table-row forms) AND check the `DEFECT_LEDGER.md` supplementary status-transition tables (L639–870, 1745–1804, 2435–2562, 2757–2820, 3094–3135, 3428–3460, 3700–3780, 4826–4990, 5264–5290, 5813–5860) for an existing `→ remediated` transition. The canonical `status=open` cell is NOT sufficient evidence that a defect is truly open — the corpus carries extensive prior V-phase remediation (1V/2V/3V/3V+/V4/V8.x/V12/V13 + Phase 6/10 sweeps) with ≥390 known canonical-lag rows (D-CONS-001).

**Strategic implication (raised to operator).** Because the spec body already contains large V-phase remediation sections and the canonical ledger lags by ≥390 rows, a substantial fraction of the ~762 `§3.2` "open" P1 defects may already be closed in the body. Re-authoring them risks repeating the Batch-1 duplicate error across all 25 programs. **Recommended course correction:** run a **D-CONS-001 reconciliation/triage pass FIRST** (walk each program's canonical `open` set against the spec body + supplementary tables; propagate already-closed rows; isolate the genuinely-missing residual), THEN author only the true residual. See Walk Plan §6 addendum.

**Edit summary.**
- Rewrote Appendix F.1 as the canonical `standard` webhook retry curve: five total delivery attempts, with attempt 1 immediate and retry attempts 2-5 at 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, and 2 hours, for 2h36m cumulative delivery window.
- Preserved Appendix F.2 `financial_impact` as the only elevated webhook curve, with no new customer-visible event classes introduced.
- Removed live webhook references to retired labels including `webhook_standard`, `standard_webhook`, `webhook_critical_business`, `security_critical`, `compliance_critical`, `org_management`, `infra_critical`, and `console_bridge_standard`.
- Rebound live body, Appendix C, and Appendix G webhook rows to Appendix F.1 `standard` or Appendix F.2 `financial_impact`; email-only / in-app / Ops-only rows now explicitly say they have no Appendix F webhook delivery where applicable.
- Recast non-webhook schedules (`bridge_apply_standard`, `transactional_email`, `auto_topup_charge`, `pricing_api_publish`, `retroactive_sweep`, provider reconnect, Stripe charge, DNS / cache fanout) as local operational policies, not `webhook_retry_class` values.
- Added §M.5.26 gate `webhook_inline_retry_curve_lint` and tightened §M.5.18 coverage language around customer webhook endpoints.
- Appended AE-V72REM-WEBHOOK-RETRY-SINGLETON-01 as the pending ratification row.
- Transitioned D-8.2-005, D-8.2-007, and tied P2 D-8.2-035 to `remediated 2026-06-21`.

**Reconciliation choice.** The D-8.2-005 recommendation proposed promoting the historical `1m / 5m / 30m / 2h / 12h` sequence to Appendix F.1. This pass deliberately does not adopt that exact sequence because D-8.2-003 has since made `delivery_attempt` a root-envelope field with a 1-5 attempt domain; treating the initial delivery as attempt 1 means five total deliveries can only include four retry delays. Adding a 12h delay would create six deliveries or force an off-by-one attempt model. The selected F.1 curve keeps the 1-5 envelope invariant and records the 12h form as retired inline drift.

**Defect-id → landing-site map.** D-8.2-005 → Appendix F.1 / F.2, Appendix C, Appendix J `webhook_retry_class`, §M.5.18, §M.5.26 `webhook_inline_retry_curve_lint`. D-8.2-007 → `bid.disqualified` now cites Appendix F.1 `standard`; retired `webhook_critical_business` is rejected by §M.5.26. D-8.2-035 → Appendix F.1 header/table and Appendix J note now agree on the five-total-delivery `standard` curve.

**AE-row → status map.** AE-V72REM-WEBHOOK-RETRY-SINGLETON-01 is pending. Founder sole-signer posture per AE-V72REM-00 holds until named-role hires; Engineering Lead + API/Integrations + Observability counter-signature is required on the named-role-hire trigger.

## v7.2.0-REM Program -> D-DEC-005 Wallet-Pool Additive Decision Closure (2026-06-24)

**Scope.** D-DEC-005, Decisions.md C-1 / C-2, Master Spec §34.10.3 wallet-pool arithmetic, related failure modes / acceptance criteria, AE-V72REM-PHDEC-DECISION-DIVERGENCE-P1-01, and live v7.1.1 count surfaces.

**Adjudication.** D-DEC-005 was a true product/pricing decision blocker, not stale ledger hygiene. This pass adopts the row's recommended option (a): Decisions C-1 / C-2 additive pooling. The prior §34.10.3 $5 Free+Free collapse and paid-side-only Free+Paid behavior is superseded.

| Decision | Resolution |
| :---- | :---- |
| C-1 Free+Free wallet pool | Buyer Free + Seller Free now renders one $10 Org-scoped AIWallet included-budget pool. |
| C-2 Free+Paid wallet pool | Free+customer-visible-paid combinations now add the Free side's $5 contribution to the paid AIWallet pool. Buyer Growth + Seller Free therefore renders $305; Buyer Starter + Seller Free renders $55. |
| Solo exception | Solo remains excluded from customer-visible pooling because Solo's envelope is engine-side and hidden. Solo+Free still renders $0 customer-visible wallet budget; Solo+Paid renders the paid side only. |
| Enterprise + Free | Enterprise committed-spend burn priority remains §34.10.1; the Free contribution appears as $5 included-budget headroom and does not change the committed-spend floor. |

**Backups.** Pre-edit backups were created before this batch for the touched authoritative files: `_versions/Sourcera_Master_Spec_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, `_versions/Decisions_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, `_versions/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, `_versions/DEFECT_LEDGER_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, `_versions/REMEDIATION_BACKLOG_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, `_versions/V711_BACKLOG_INDEX_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, `_versions/RECONCILIATION_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, `_versions/AGENTS_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`, and `_versions/CLAUDE_pre-d-dec-005-wallet-pool-additive-2026-06-24.md`.

**Scope.** Closed D-DEC-006 by adopting Decisions.md C-4 for Ops override guardrails on Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat allocation.

## v7.1.1 Phase 4.6 TCO Acceptance-Criteria P2 Closure (2026-07-09)

## v7.1.1 Marketplace Trust, Disclosure, and Accounting Hygiene Conflict (2026-07-11)

**Conflicts surfaced.** §34.16 omitted its own cross-references for earned Verification badges, Featured-vs-Promoted visual separation, Match Score ranking exclusion, token/a11y disclosure rendering, and the distinct Billing Ledger versus MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord field roles. ## v7.1.1 Phase 4.3 Attachment Security and Attachment-Enum Authority Closure (2026-07-12)

**Conflicts surfaced.** D-4.3-024 correctly identified that Policy Ingestion had no byte-security admission rule: §12 could create a PolicyDocument and job without a clean §4.6.2 Attachment verdict. While binding that rule, current-source inspection found a second live conflict: §4.6.2 named a consumer subset while two different Appendix J `attachment_owner_entity_type_enum` definitions named incompatible value sets. The prior D-AJ-023 closure was therefore not accepted as historical; the current source was reconciled before the PolicyDocument binding was authored.

**Authority selected.** §4.6.2 owns file storage, scan state, quarantine, retention, and firewall behavior. §4.3.34 owns the PolicyDocument source pointer. §12.2.1 owns the Policy-specific admission order and user recovery. §32.10.3.C and Appendix I own transport outcomes. Appendix J owns the one Attachment owner enum. §3.7 and §29 own the generic error and notification treatment. The existing pending `AE-V711-PH12-POLICY-RESILIENCE-SAFETY-01` owns the newly selected clean-scan binding; no second extension or scanner model is created.

**Resolution.** Policy uploads now begin as Buyer-Workspace `presigned_orphan` Attachments. Only a same-Org, same-Workspace, residency-matched Attachment with `scan_status='clean'` may atomically bind as `policy_document` and create the PolicyDocument and PolicyIngestionJob. An infected attachment returns `policy_ingestion_attachment_scan_failed`, follows the existing §4.6.2 quarantine / purge / notification path, and creates no policy, provider, billing, control, webhook, Console Bridge, or telemetry artifact. Nonterminal or unavailable scans return `attachment_scan_pending` and cannot be treated as clean. The §3.7 Failure / Reason / Recovery state is explicit. Appendix I is the error-code authority, so §32.10.3.C now consumes its HTTP 415 unsupported-format and HTTP 422 page-limit values rather than conflicting 422 / 413 values. Appendix J now has one union registry and the conflicting duplicate is retired. The strengthened `policy_ingestion_entity_contract_completeness` static detector verifies the source Attachment field and §12.2 clean-scan tokens.

**Runtime boundary.** This is a source-contract and static-detector closure only. The schema migration, upload resolver, scan worker, clean-verdict enforcement, quarantine notifier, atomic transaction, access controls, client rendering, mobile proof, and security / concurrency / non-leak integration evidence are not present in this workspace. `AE-V711-PH12-POLICY-RESILIENCE-SAFETY-01` remains pending human sign-off. No runtime row is promoted.
